## 1. R3 revision purpose

R2 synchronized the seven upstream authorities to finalized Layer 6 R11. R3 closes the remaining round trip by binding those authority successors back into Layer 6 R12. This document therefore participates in an eight-document closed loop: seven upstream authorities plus the Layer 6 Nuts-and-Bolts successor.

## 2. Closed-loop authority and noninterference lock

1. Superior authority continues to flow from Architecture, Registry, Plan, Protocol, Playbook, accepted Method Selection and completed Layers 1–5 Nuts-and-Bolts into Layer 6.
2. Layer 6 R12 acknowledges the exact successor set and may return only owner-ready realization detail, defect evidence, impact analysis, invalidation roots, consumer requirements and closure tests.
3. No upstream document is amended by Layer 6 itself. Only the lawful owner may accept a versioned change packet and publish a successor.
4. An accepted upstream successor does not mutate existing Layer 6 records in place. It creates an invalidation root, a topological regeneration set, a new semantic configuration identity where applicable, and explicit consumer acknowledgments.
5. A rejected or deferred packet leaves the current contract unchanged and records the remaining gate.
6. Layer 6 R12 preserves R11 byte-for-byte and adds only the synchronization receipt and closed-loop authority binding.

## 3. Protocol-owned R39 update

R39 accepts the implementation-neutral evaluation bindings supplied by Layer 6 R12 without inventing numerical constants or new metrics. It binds dual-clock matching, producer variants, target/model/calibration/policy/configuration identities, denominator conservation, attrition, negative controls, A6/A8/A9/A10/A11 evaluation, conditional A12/A13 participation and no-update legality.

## 4. Forward Protocol contract to Layer 6 R12

Layer 6 must preserve the strict event-time and inclusive availability-time predecessor rule, frozen outer evaluation, grouped/dependence-aware units, actual behavior propensities, support/ESS requirements, estimator sensitivity, route-identification status, trajectory/simulator eligibility and immutable negative results.

## 5. Reverse Layer 6 contract to the Protocol

Layer 6 may submit evidence that an estimand, denominator, matching key, metric reference, sensitivity family or numerical constant is missing or internally inconsistent. It cannot approve the change. Accepted Protocol succession invalidates affected evaluation products and requires rerunning matching, denominators, statistics, cards, manifests and claims.

## 6. Formula and evaluation closure

The synchronized design retains: dual-clock eligibility; nested grouped selection and out-of-fold calibration; typed score/probability/cost/uncertainty/propensity separation; causal or bounded deferral evaluation; IPS/SNIPS/DR/SWITCH-compatible OPE under valid assumptions; pessimistic update gating; and RL necessity/trajectory/simulator gates.

## 7. Remaining Protocol gates

Protocol-v1.0 constants, MetricDictionary approval, clipping/sensitivity values, confirmatory run matrix, multiplicity, confidence levels and promotion thresholds remain owner-frozen rather than invented.


## 8. Final status

`READY-WITH-GATED-ITEMS`. This successor is synchronized with Layer 6 R12 and its sibling authority successors. It authorizes no empirical, deployment, clinical, safety or claim conclusion and does not replace the Implementation Build Book.

## 0. Controlling interpretation

R37 converts the finalized Layer 6 formulas and evaluation contracts into Protocol-owned freeze requirements. It intentionally leaves numerical values unfrozen where no approved project evidence exists.

1. This successor controls only propositions inside this document's established authority domain.
2. The embedded predecessor controls all unaffected content.
3. The Layer 6 R11 design is implementation-neutral technical evidence and cannot silently amend a superior authority.
4. Accepted methods, modules, submodules, phases, gates, ablations and upstream internal algorithms remain unchanged unless explicitly stated in this active addendum.
5. Owner-pending physical schemas, numerical values, runtime evidence and claims remain gated and are not fabricated.

## 1. Protocol update disposition

The global ablation set remains exactly A0-A13. A5 remains immutable and Layer 4-owned; A6, A8, A9, A10 and A11 remain Layer 6-owned; A7 remains separately owned by Layer 5/Layer 4 rerun logic; A12 and A13 remain Layer 8/9-owned with conditional Layer 6 participation through 6.E. No A14 or new headline estimand is created.

## 2. Whole-layer matching key and timing legality

A confirmatory Layer 6 comparison must bind, as applicable: dataset/protocol/split, subject/session/run/trial/window/sequence, source generation, context profile and semantic hash, producer variant, target/model/calibrator/threshold versions, action/legality/budget/fallback/cost/reward/reason profiles, policy/route/support/propensity/trajectory/environment/stress/embodiment identities, seed, phase and ablation.

Decision context obeys the dual-clock rule:

```text
event_time(source) < decision_event_cutoff
availability_time(source) <= decision_availability_cutoff
```

Target, update, evaluation and oracle views are distinct. Same-event post-action outcomes are never decision-time features.

## 3. Denominator ladder

Every result declares and conserves:

1. source-eligible denominator;
2. successfully joined denominator;
3. outcome-observed denominator;
4. common-support/overlap denominator where required;
5. claim-eligible denominator.

Attrition reasons are mutually traceable, negative results are retained, and unsupported cells cannot be silently dropped or merged.

## 4. A6/A9/A8/A10/A11 protocol bindings

| Ablation | Required comparison/evaluation | Mandatory legality and negative closure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A6 | Rule-derived Layer 4 EvidenceQualityRecord/A5-compatible anchor versus learned Layer 6 producer variant; grouped and nested selection; OOF calibration; reliability, selective risk and generalization | Target leakage, split leakage, uncalibrated probability language, unsupported transfer and baseline-sufficient outcomes are explicit. |
| A9 | 6.0 and accepted supervised comparators under matched context/action/cost profiles; per-action criterion cost and action distribution/collapse analysis | Illegal actions are structurally undefined/masked; score/probability/uncertainty/propensity are not conflated. |
| A8 | Direct-versus-defer with route-specific cost, delay, burden, capacity, trust and qualification; paired, propensity-based, local-threshold diagnostic or partial-ID branch | Route existence is not causal qualification; over-deferral, safe hold, unsupported route and baseline-sufficient outcomes remain visible. |
| A10 | Actual logged propensities, support/ESS, IPS/SNIPS/DR/SWITCH or accepted pessimistic estimators, cross-fitting, clipping sensitivity, lower-bound update gate and untouched outer holdout | Invalid propensity, zero support, low ESS, estimator instability or nonpositive pessimistic improvement produces `NO_POLICY_UPDATE`. |
| A11 | Necessity against simpler policies, valid trajectories, inherited legal actions, conservative/constrained offline learning, checkpoint and held-out simulator evaluation | Missing necessity/trajectory/reward/constraint/support/simulator evidence produces `RL_NOT_JUSTIFIED`, `A11_INELIGIBLE` or `SIMULATOR_INVALID`. |

## 5. Numerical freeze ledger

The following remain Protocol v1.0 owner decisions: budget units and limits; VOI admission thresholds; target/cost gaps; model-selection criteria; calibration grid; operating points; support/overlap/ESS minima; propensity validation tolerances; clipping/SWITCH rules; estimator confidence intervals; pessimistic margins; multiplicity; promotion/no-harm margins; RL necessity thresholds; reward/cost/constraint values; episode/terminal/reset semantics; simulator and reward-sensitivity grids; replay tolerances and claim-facing equivalence classes.

No value may be inferred from a paper, default library setting or synthetic fixture.

## 6. MetricDictionary and claim legality

Unregistered measures remain diagnostic. Layer 10 renders only saved validated results and denominators. Layer 0 receives evidence mode, oracle/simulation/diagnostic/no-update/negative-result tags and retains final claim authority.

## Bidirectional synchronization contract

### Authority → Layer 4 `[AUTHORITY_TO_LAYER4]`

Protocol fixes lawful comparisons, metric authority, statistical units, denominator/attrition behavior and final numerical profiles.

Layer 4 must therefore:

1. consume the authority as a fixed constraint within that document's domain;

4. avoid local repair, silent reinterpretation, hidden migration, method reselection or owner substitution;

### Layer 4 → authority `[LAYER4_TO_AUTHORITY]`

Finalized Layer 4 returns available fields, exact semantic identities, estimator/tie candidates, matching feasibility, negative-result states and unresolved numerical interfaces.

The return path is evidence-bearing, not self-authorizing. A Layer 4 return packet must include:

1. the predecessor remains immutable provenance;

3. every dependent Layer 4 record, trace, comparison, manifest and downstream bundle is located through dependency closure;

5. regeneration begins from the earliest changed authoritative input;
6. Layer 10 displays the correction/invalidation state without recomputing primary evidence;
7. Layer 0 receives the strictest resulting limitation and updated claim-evidence pointers.

### Conflict resolution

A conflict is decomposed into propositions and assigned to the lawful authority domain. Higher-ranked authority controls within its domain; finalized Layer 4 supplies realization and evidence but cannot override that owner. A lower-ranked finding may trigger a controlled successor or controlled reopen, never a hidden rewrite.

### Two-way closure criterion

This document and Layer 4 are synchronized only when both directions are satisfied: Layer 4 demonstrably conforms to the authority, and the authority explicitly represents every finalized Layer 4 dependency that belongs in its own domain. Open physical, numerical, implementation, project-instance, consumer or empirical matters remain labeled and fail closed.

### 5. Confirmatory evaluation requirements

1. Operating-point evaluation remains primary and uses approved MetricDictionary identities.
2. Matched comparisons require complete registered keys, common support, explicit branch eligibility, independent-unit definitions, denominator conservation and attrition/missing-cell reporting.
3. AURC/AUGRC are candidate secondary quantities until estimator, tie-plateau, endpoint, denominator and interpretation profiles are approved.
4. Equivalence/no-harm requires a registered estimand, margin, confidence interval and multiplicity rule; nonsignificance is not equivalence.
5. Participant/session dependence is handled by the registered independent-unit and resampling model; row-level pseudo-replication is prohibited.
6. A7 requires event-time and availability-time legality, strict predecessor ordering, compatible sequence/reset generation, no same-event/future information and separate A5/A7 identity.
7. Negative, null, sparse, ineligible and diagnostic-only outcomes remain first-class Protocol results and may not be suppressed.

### 6. Formula and algorithm verification status

The R15 release independently verified 78 governed formula/algorithm/pseudocode surfaces. Bounded tests establish mathematical, compatibility, lifecycle, deterministic-policy and implementation-feasibility evidence only. Final operating points and scientific conclusions require Protocol-controlled empirical execution.

## R30 LAYER 6 POST-SELECTION SYNCHRONIZATION APPLIED — Layer 6 post-selection synchronization addendum

### 1. Synchronization purpose and non-drift contract

This addendum converts the finalized Layer 6 method selections into the exact canonical, evidence, evaluation, and execution obligations owned by this document. It does not repeat the full method rationale; it binds the accepted decision IDs, record/artifact classes, gates, and handoffs needed by subsequent detailed design and official execution.

The following invariants are mandatory:

- No new Layer 6 module, submodule, workstream, official phase, or global ablation is introduced.
- No Layer 1–5 method or Layer 1–3 detailed-design decision is reopened.
- No configuration instance, model file, report, curve, table, card bundle, or convenience alias is silently promoted into a canonical record class.
- No target-, oracle-, evaluation-only, future, or post-action field may enter a decision-time view.
- No action legality, fallback qualification, reward/cost semantics, behavior propensity, update trace, or ownership boundary may be redefined by a downstream consumer.
- Every accepted change is additive, versioned, lineage-preserving, and backward-readable; released predecessor bytes are never repaired in place.

## R29 LAYER 3 FULL BIDIRECTIONAL SYNCHRONIZATION APPLIED - meticulous bidirectional synchronization addendum

### 1. Two-way but authority-asymmetric contract

The contract is deliberately two-way but not authority-symmetric. The authority document sends binding constraints into Layer 3. Layer 3 sends realization evidence, feasibility findings, defects and impact requests back. Only the lawful domain owner can amend the controlling rule. Until accepted, affected Layer 3 products remain blocked, stale, superseded or diagnostic-only.

### 2. Authority -> Layer 3 obligations

| ID | Authority -> Layer 3 obligation | Layer 3 enforcement | Failure/correction rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PROTO-IN-01 | Preserve A0-A13 identities and ownership; introduce no A14. | R18 treats ablation IDs as evaluation metadata, not modules or records. | Any identity/owner change requires Protocol plus architecture/method review. |
| PROTO-IN-02 | Keep A1 raw-versus-calibrated comparisons on lawful identical support. | Calibration selection uses calibration-only data; final-test labels cannot tune choices. | Leakage or support mismatch invalidates confirmatory interpretation. |
| PROTO-IN-03 | Keep A2 a simple frozen registered threshold baseline. | Selection score, operator, target, fit role, applicability, tie policy and version are explicit. | Hidden fusion, dynamic stopping or learned deferral is not A2. |
| PROTO-IN-04 | Keep A3 as separate declared uncertainty/selective-prediction child comparisons. | Mandatory ordinary features and conditional features are separately versioned. | Prerequisite failure makes a child unavailable, not fabricated. |
| PROTO-IN-05 | Require exact matching, eligible-set, denominator and statistical-unit identity. | Matched rows carry dataset, subject/session/window, split, model, budget, source, metric and configuration keys. | Incompatible rows remain unmatched diagnostics. |
| PROTO-IN-06 | Preserve visible positive, negative, equivalent, inconclusive, invalid, harmful and diagnostic-only outcomes. | NegativeResultNote and DiagnosticOnlyFlag are emitted when applicable. | Nonsignificance is never recoded as equivalence or success. |
| PROTO-IN-07 | Reserve final grids, folds, confidence levels, multiplicity, binning, thresholds and support cutoffs to Protocol v1.0. | R18 provides formulas, domains and reserved configuration slots only. | No confirmatory execution before registration and freeze. |

| PROTO-OUT-04 | A reserved numerical choice is infeasible or unstable in pilot execution. | Pilot-only evidence, sensitivity analysis and no-test-leakage proof. | Protocol owner freezes a lawful successor configuration; prior confirmatory identity remains distinct. |

## R28 LAYER 3 NUTS-AND-BOLTS REALIZATION SYNCHRONIZATION APPLIED Layer 3 R16 realization synchronization addendum

### Synchronization principles

1. **Additive synchronization only.** No accepted predecessor content is removed or silently rewritten.
2. **Asymmetric authority.** Layer 3 R16 supplies implementation-feasibility and realization detail; each upstream document changes only within its own authority domain.
3. **No method reselection.** The 25 accepted Layer 3 decisions, ten official module families, A0–A13 identities, three workstreams, fourteen Phase 3 steps and all established layer boundaries remain unchanged.
4. **No silent promotion.** Candidate/supporting objects remain candidate/supporting until a Registry-owner successor explicitly promotes them.
5. **No empirical overclaim.** Design completeness is not live EEG evidence, empirical winner selection, deployed implementation qualification, clinical validation or Layer 0 claim approval.
6. **Immutable history.** Predecessor documents and released evidence remain byte-preserved; accepted corrections create successors, invalidation notices and regenerated evidence rather than in-place repair.

### 1. Ablation identity lock

No new global ablation is introduced. A0 remains the raw/accept-all Layer 2 reference; A1 is calibrated decoder/calibration visibility; A2 is the simple frozen registered confidence-threshold baseline; A3 is score-specific uncertainty and selective prediction; A4 remains ordinary longer-window/multi-window voting/averaging/ensemble controls owned by Layer 2; A5–A13 remain downstream comparisons.

### 2. A1 protocol specialization

A1 compares eligible raw and calibrated probability sources under identical legal evaluation units, class order, split, model/branch, budget, preprocessing, eligible-set and metric identities. Calibration fitting/selection uses calibration-only data. Final-test labels cannot select calibrator family, pooling scope, hyperparameters, bins, report emphasis or fallback. Required outputs include proper-scoring-rule and reliability evidence, argmax-change disclosure where applicable, support/fallback status, group/budget views and failed-attempt/negative-result evidence.

### 3. A2 protocol specialization

A2 is a simple, registered, frozen threshold baseline whose selection score, direction, operator, target, granularity, fit split, applicability keys, tie policy and version are explicit. It is not IHARQ, dynamic stopping, learned deferral or hidden score fusion. Threshold selection and evaluation roles are separated. Every consumable rule must resolve to a `ThresholdRegistryRecord` and exact eligible denominator.

### 4. A3 protocol specialization

A3 consists of separate child comparisons for declared uncertainty scores and selective-prediction rules. Confidence, normalized entropy and top-two margin are mandatory ordinary features where lawful; A4 disagreement, conformal proxies and temporal summaries are conditional and cannot be fabricated when prerequisites fail. Risk–coverage evidence uses the same masks/counts/eligible denominator across views, tie-atomic ordering, explicit zero/full endpoints and visible coverage-collapse/sparse-support failures.

### 5. Matching and estimand contract

Matched claims require compatible dataset, subject/session/window, split, preprocessing, label map, budget, model/branch, probability source, class order, seed/config, metric, eligible-set and operating-target identities. Incompatibility creates unmatched diagnostic rows, not forced comparisons. Independent statistical units, aggregation levels, interval method, multiplicity family, minimum support and exact numerical grids remain Protocol v1.0 declarations.

### 6. Leakage and evaluation-only fields

Correctness, true labels, HCW/wrong-accept flags, future outcomes, oracle reliability and future rewards are evaluation-only. They are excluded from decision-time calibration, uncertainty, threshold and downstream policy projections. Past-only temporal summaries must enforce causal cutoffs and declared reset keys.

### 7. Outcome taxonomy

Positive, negative, equivalent, inconclusive, invalid, unsupported, overconservative and diagnostic-only outcomes remain distinguishable. `NegativeResultNote` and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` are mandatory where their conditions apply. Null or adverse findings cannot be suppressed by threshold/report selection.

### 8. Reserved numerical decisions

R16 provides formulas, domains, invariants and lawful algorithm families but does not freeze final folds, grids, repetitions, confidence levels, multiplicity procedures, binning constants, thresholds, support cutoffs or resource ceilings. Those remain Protocol v1.0 owner decisions and must be registered before confirmatory execution.

**Interpretive correction:** previous `YES/NO` green-light tables conflated *current-stage completeness* with *later-stage execution*. R22 replaces that binary reading with lifecycle-aware states.

### Controlling status vocabulary

```text
GREEN-LIT — CURRENT STAGE COMPLETE
    The document/design deliverable expected at the present lifecycle stage is complete.

GREEN-LIT — HANDOFF READY
    The current stage has produced all inputs required to start the next document or implementation stage.

GREEN-LIT TO BEGIN — FUTURE EXECUTION
    The future execution stage is authorized to begin when its scheduled prerequisites are available.

NOT YET DUE — SUPPORTED BY CURRENT DESIGN
    The later artifact/result has not been produced because its lifecycle stage has not occurred;
    this is not a defect in the current Layer 1 Nuts-and-Bolts specification.

BLOCKED — GENUINE DEFECT
    A required current-stage input, design, authority decision or validation is missing or contradictory.
```

### Correct lifecycle interpretation

The Layer 1 Nuts-and-Bolts deliverable, its upstream synchronization, and its handoff to the Implementation Build Book are green-lit. The current stack also green-lights the *scheduled creation/finalization* of the Implementation Build Book, Experiment Protocol v1.0, Phase 1 implementation package, A0–A13 readiness materialization, and future Paper/Thesis Evidence Map. It does not claim that later empirical runs, concrete frozen record bytes, ablation results, or final thesis claims already exist.

This distinction is required by the established document sequence:

```text
Layer 1 Method Selection Register
→ Layer 1 Nuts-and-Bolts Specification
→ Implementation Build Book
→ Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol v1.0 finalization
→ Phase execution and A0–A13 evidence production
→ Paper/Thesis Evidence Map and final claim review
```

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A0 identity

A0 is the raw decoder evaluation reference. It measures what the declared baseline decoder produces before probability calibration, thresholding, selective prediction, IHARQ evidence verification, RegimeRisk, learned readiness policies, simulation, stress testing, or embodiment mapping are credited.

A0 may be described as an **accept-all raw decoder reference** only in the narrow evaluation sense that every raw decoder output is treated as a decision output without rejection, deferral, evidence request, calibration-based filtering, or readiness control. This does not make A0 a clinical accept decision, safety gate, or deployment controller.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

A0 answers the foundational question:

> Under the declared public-data protocol, fixed splits, preprocessing, label budgets, model-family definitions, seeds, and metric dictionary entries, what is the reproducible baseline behavior of the raw decoder before reliability-control modules are added?

This question is intentionally narrower than IHARQ’s final scientific question. A0 does not ask whether the system is clinically safe, ready for real-time use, or effective for rehabilitation. It establishes the reference against which later reliability, calibration, selective prediction, IHARQ, policy, stress, embodiment, dashboard, and claim-safety evidence must be interpreted.

#### 3.3 A0 contribution to the full protocol

| A0 role | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| Baseline/reference | A0 is the naive raw-decoder reference for A1–A13 comparisons where matched lineage exists. |
| Decoder measurement | A0 measures raw performance, score availability, low-calibration behavior, model-family coverage, failure/skipped-run visibility, and reproducibility. |
| Fairness anchor | A0 carries dataset, split, preprocessing, label-map, budget, seed, model, and metric lineage needed for later matched comparisons. |
| Claim-safety anchor | A0 prevents later sections from claiming improvement without a transparent raw-decoder reference and limitation boundary. |
| Failure signal | Weak A0 results reveal dataset/model/protocol difficulty; strong A0 results still do not prove readiness or safety. |

| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides the source identities and matched-comparison foundation used by A0 | A0 must consume validated `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, optional `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, `Layer1Manifest`, and `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` where available |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Primary source layer for A0 evidence | Produces `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, optional `SubjectProfileRecord`, optional/conditional `FailureCaseIndex`, conditional `LeakageWarningRecord`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, and A0 raw-decoder evidence tables |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Downstream consumer and comparator context for A1–A3 | Must consume A0 records without overwriting raw `PredictionRecord` values; A0 does not require calibration records to exist |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Later comparator/consumer context | A0 provides raw decoder reference evidence; A0 does not produce IHARQ decisions, reason codes, fallback records, unsafe events, or evidence-verification traces |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Later temporal-trust comparator/consumer context | A0 may provide raw prediction lineage for temporal diagnostics only where source-supported; it does not produce regime or trust states |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Later policy comparator/consumer context | A0 outputs may be consumed as split-safe context only if evaluation-only fields are excluded from decision-time features; A0 does not produce policy actions or deferral records |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness | Later simulation consumer context | A0 can serve as an accept-all/raw-decoder baseline in simulation only after Layer 7 creates valid simulation records; A0 itself is not simulation evidence |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Later stress consumer/comparator context | A0 may be stress-tested as a raw decoder under controlled perturbations in A12, but this A0 section does not define stress intensities or stress outcomes |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Later embodiment-proxy consumer context | A0 can be an accept-all action baseline for A13 only when Layer 9 command mapping and embodiment records exist; A0 itself has no embodiment claim |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility | Read-only dashboard/export/reproducibility owner for A0 outputs | May read, validate, summarize, warn, render cards, export, and package A0 records; must not train, tune, recalibrate, repair source records, or create hidden primary evidence |

#### 4.1 Non-forced layer content

| Topic | A0 status | Handling rule |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration method comparison | `downstream_context_only` | Belongs to A1; A0 supplies raw comparator evidence only |
| Threshold selection | `not_applicable_for_A0` | Belongs to A2; A0 must not tune thresholds |
| Selective prediction / risk-coverage | `not_applicable_for_A0` | Belongs to A3; A0 may provide raw score inputs later |
| Longer-window / ensemble controls | `nearby_comparator_only` | Belongs to A4; do not collapse A4 into A0 |
| IHARQ decisions | `not_applicable_for_A0` | Belongs to A5+ |
| Policy updates / deferral | `not_applicable_for_A0` | Belongs to A6–A11 depending branch |
| Stress profiles | `downstream_context_only` | Belongs to A12 |
| Embodiment endpoint or command metrics | `not_applicable_for_A0` | Belongs to A13 |
| Dashboard visuals | `derived_read_only` | Layer 10 may render A0, but visuals are not primary evidence |

### 5. Relationship to Official Phase 0–15 Sequence

A0 is not a phase. It is an evaluation-use metadata identifier whose source evidence is produced primarily in Phase 2 after Phase 0 and Phase 1 foundations exist.

| Official phase | A0 relationship | A0 status |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 — Repository, configuration, and record schema | Prepares schemas, configs, validators, run/hash/seed conventions, metric placeholders, matched-comparison templates, diagnostic-only flags, claim-evidence placeholders, and dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | `required_foundation` |
| Phase 1 — Public data and split protocol | Produces public-data/protocol records, cards, validation reports, manifests, and ablation-readiness artifact required for A0 matched comparison | `required_upstream` |
| Phase 2 — Baseline decoders | Produces the Layer 2 raw-decoder source records and A0 raw-decoder evidence tables | `primary_evidence_phase` |
| Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty | Consumes A0 as comparator for A1–A3; must not overwrite A0 raw prediction values | `downstream_comparator_context` |
| Phase 4 — IHARQ-lite evidence verification | Uses A0 only as upstream baseline context through matched comparison lineage | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust | Uses raw prediction lineage only if valid and split-safe | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Uses raw predictions only through declared split-safe features; evaluation-only fields remain excluded | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | May compare learned deferral to raw/accept-all behavior under matched cost/coverage if later records exist | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | May include accept-all/raw decoder reference in simulation-local comparisons but cannot retroactively redefine A0 | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | May stress raw decoder outputs as part of A12; this A0 section does not finalize stress conditions | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | No direct A0 production; A0 may appear as baseline context in simulation-only branches | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | No direct A0 production; simulation-only comparator context if records are valid | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | No direct A0 production; possible accept-all action comparator in A13 under Layer 9 records | `downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison | No direct A0 production; optional downstream proxy context | `optional_downstream_context_only` |
| Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards | Reads and renders A0 source/evaluation artifacts into traceable dashboard pages, cards, exports, warnings, and reproducibility package | `derived_reporting_phase` |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | Integrates A0 evidence and limitations into final claim-evidence matrix and thesis tables/figures | `final_claim_integration_phase` |

#### 5.1 Phase handoff rule for A0

A0 becomes thesis-usable only when Phase 2 evidence can be linked backward to Phase 0/1 foundations and forward to Phase 14/15 reporting without breaking source identity, metric definition, matched-comparison keys, diagnostic-only visibility, or Layer 0 limitations.

### 6. Relationship to A0–A13 and Nearby Ablations

| Ablation ID | Correct normalized identity | Relationship to A0 |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder / raw decoder reference | Current target. Establishes naive raw-decoder baseline before reliability control. |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder / calibration visibility | Must compare to A0 using identical predictions or matched model family and legal calibration split. |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Must not be confused with A0. A2 applies a registered confidence/threshold rule; A0 accepts raw predictions without rejection or threshold gating. |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Must not be confused with A0. A3 uses uncertainty/selective-prediction/risk-coverage logic; A0 supplies raw score inputs and raw reference metrics only. |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Must not be folded into A0. A4 tests simple aggregation/ordinary controls against A0 and later IHARQ. |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Uses A0 as one baseline reference, but A5 must be compared mainly against A2–A4 under matched coverage/cost/data/split. |
| A6 | IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator where source-supported | Downstream learned evidence-quality branch; A0 is only raw reference evidence. |
| A7 | IHARQ plus RegimeRisk temporal trust where source-supported | Downstream temporal trust branch; A0 may provide raw time-ordered prediction lineage. |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer / deferral comparison where source-supported | Downstream deferral baseline; may compare against raw accept-all behavior under matched cost/coverage. |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ / adaptive readiness policy where source-supported | Downstream supervised policy branch; A0 is not a policy. |
| A10 | Contextual bandit where source-supported and simulation-bounded | Downstream simulation-only adaptation branch; A0 is not an online learning policy. |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy where source-supported and simulation-bounded | Downstream simulation-only RL branch; A0 is not sequential policy evidence. |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests / controlled stress robustness | May include raw decoder under stress as part of A12, but A0 itself is clean raw-decoder reference unless explicitly stress-conditioned in a later A12 section. |
| A13 | Layer 9 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo / simulated embodiment consequence | May include accept-all action comparator only under Layer 9/A13 evidence; A0 alone does not imply embodiment consequence. |

#### 6.1 A0 no-collapse rule

A0 must remain a raw decoder reference. It must not absorb:

- A1 calibration metrics or reliability diagrams as A0 evidence;
- A2 threshold/registered operating-point decisions;
- A3 uncertainty/selective-prediction rejection logic;
- A4 longer-window, voting, averaging, or ordinary ensemble control logic;
- A5+ IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy, stress, or embodiment behavior.

#### 6.2 Relationship to C0–C4 capability tiers

A0 does not by itself establish any Stretch C capability tier. It provides the raw-decoder measurement spine that later capability-tier claims may reference only when the rest of the required evidence chain exists.

| Capability tier | A0 relationship | Claim status | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C0` | A0 can support an initial public-data decoder-baseline evidence path after Phase 0–2 records validate. | `possible_context_only` | Must remain decoder-baseline evidence; no readiness, clinical, or deployment claim. |
| `C1` | A0 may be inherited as the raw baseline for calibration, threshold, selective-prediction, and IHARQ comparisons. | `downstream_context_only` | Requires A1–A5 evidence and matched-comparison reports before any reliability-control contribution claim. |
| `C2` | A0 may be replay/source lineage for temporal trust or policy comparisons. | `downstream_context_only` | Requires downstream RegimeRisk/policy/simulation records; A0 does not create a policy or trust state. |
| `C3` | A0 may be part of a stress-conditioned comparison only under A12. | `future_or_downstream_context_only` | Clean A0 and stressed records must remain distinct; stress robustness is not an A0 claim. |
| `C4` | A0 may provide a raw accept-all/provenance comparator for an embodiment-proxy section only if Layer 9 records exist. | `future_or_downstream_context_only` | Embodiment consequence, command success, endpoint error, and simulator safety remain A13/proxy-only claims. |

**Capability-tier rule:** A0 can help make later tier claims auditable, but A0 alone never upgrades the system beyond a bounded public-data raw-decoder baseline.

### 7. Required Records and Artifacts

This section follows the framework-required record table format more tightly than the initial draft: each record family lists producer layer, producing phase, key fields, validation condition, evaluation use, and missingness consequence. A0 consumes or references these objects for evaluation; A0 itself does not own or produce canonical records.

#### 7.1 Required upstream Layer 1 records for A0 matchability

| Record/artifact | Producer layer | Producer phase | Required fields or key fields for A0 | Validation status required | Consumer/evaluation use | Missingness consequence |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | `dataset_id`, source/version/provenance, license/access status where tracked, inclusion/exclusion status, limitation tags | Validated source record | Dataset identity and public-data claim boundary | A0 cannot make dataset-scoped or public-data baseline claims for affected data |
| `WindowRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | `window_id`, `trial_id` where present, subject/session/run lineage, time/order fields where available, label-budget linkage, artifact context | Validated source record | Unit of raw decoder prediction and matched comparison | Per-window/per-trial A0 comparison becomes diagnostic-only or invalid |
| `SplitRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | `split_id`, `split_role`, train/validation/test/calibration/threshold/adaptation/simulation roles where used, disjointness checks | Validated, leakage-checked | Split legality and leakage control | Affected metrics invalid or blocked until split repair and rerun |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | preprocessing version/hash, fit scope, transform lineage, source-record IDs | Validated, train-fit legality confirmed | Confirms preprocessing comparability and prevents train/test leakage | Affected A0 runs blocked or diagnostic-only |
| `LabelMapRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | normalized/original label mapping, class order compatibility, proxy-intent limitations | Validated | Ensures raw predictions and labels mean the same classes | Metric and score interpretation blocked until repaired |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | artifact/missingness flags, affected windows/channels, limitation tags | Required where available/declared | Data-quality context and warning inheritance | Missing flags weaken affected quality analyses; diagnostic-only where artifact status is claim-relevant |
| `ValidationReport` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | schema, split, metadata, leakage, label, and readiness checks | Passing or explicitly downgraded | A0 source-record readiness gate | Missing report blocks thesis-ready A0 claims |
| `Layer1Manifest` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | source paths, versions, hashes, validation status, config references, limitation tags | Validated handoff manifest | Reproducibility and source-lineage handoff | A0 source lineage incomplete; dashboard/export cannot be claim-ready |
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | A0–A4 matchability fields, missing-key warnings, diagnostic-only flags | Required when available from Phase 1 handoff | A0/A1/A2/A3/A4 comparison-readiness signal | A0–A4 comparisons downgraded until readiness is established |

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

#### 9.1 A0 baseline definition

A0 is itself the baseline/reference point. It does not need a stronger baseline to be meaningful, but it must be internally transparent so later improvements are not measured against an informal or hidden decoder result.

A0 variants may include multiple source-supported model families under the same official A0 identifier, such as sanity baselines, classical CSP/LDA/SVM-style pipelines, Riemannian/tangent-space baselines where compatible, compact neural baselines where feasible, and optional compact SSL/foundation-style adapters where legal and supported. These are **model-family variants inside A0**, not new official top-level ablation IDs.

#### 9.2 A0 internal comparisons

| Internal comparison | Purpose | Required matching |
|---|---|---|
| Sanity baseline versus declared core baseline families | Confirm pipeline and lower-bound behavior | Same dataset/split/window/preprocessing/label-map/budget/seed policy where applicable |
| Classical versus Riemannian/robust classical family | Establish reproducible decoder-family behavior | Same Layer 1 records, label budget, metric dictionary, class order, aggregation level |
| Compact neural family versus classical family where feasible | Test whether a compact neural decoder changes raw baseline behavior | Same split roles, label budget, seed/config policy, score type/class-order validation |
| Low-calibration budget curves across families | Expose label-budget sensitivity | Same budget IDs, split roles, metric definitions, and aggregation units |
| Subject/session aggregation | Expose heterogeneity without diagnosis | Same subject/session identity fields, no physiological diagnosis or patient stratification claim |
| Failed/skipped/unsupported runs | Preserve transparency | Failure status must appear in `ModelRegistryRecord`, logs, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, or negative-result notes |

#### 9.3 Downstream comparators that depend on A0

| Downstream comparator | A0 role | A0 boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A1 calibrated decoder | A0 provides raw prediction and raw metric reference | A0 must not include calibrated probabilities as raw evidence |
| A2 simple registered threshold | A0 provides no-threshold reference | A0 must not tune or apply thresholds |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | A0 provides raw score/reference population | A0 must not reject, defer, or select coverage |
| A4 ordinary controls | A0 provides single/raw decoder reference | A0 must not include multi-window/ensemble aggregation |
| A5+ IHARQ and readiness controls | A0 provides baseline comparator for wrong accepts, cost, burden, or raw accept-all behavior where matched | A0 must not be described as evidence verification or readiness policy |

---

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

#### 10.1 Required key families

Every A0 comparison intended for thesis-ready use must carry a complete matched-comparison envelope. The required keys are grouped below.

| Key family | Required fields or identifiers | A0 use |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset/protocol identity | `dataset_id`, source/version/license/access note where applicable, `protocol_version` | Confirms the public-data source and protocol version |
| Subject/session/run identity | `subject_id`, `session_id` where available, `run_id` where applicable | Supports fair per-subject/session/run aggregation |
| Trial/window identity | `trial_id` where present, `window_id`, `parent_trial_id` where available, overlap group | Prevents pooled-only or mismatched window comparisons |
| Split identity | `split_id`, `split_role`, train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation/simulation roles where used | Prevents leakage and test-set tuning |
| Preprocessing and label identity | `preprocessing_id`, preprocessing version/hash, `label_map_id`, `label_map_version`, normalized/original labels | Ensures decoder outputs mean the same task/class mapping |
| Budget identity | `label_budget_id`, low-calibration/calibration budget definition, budget version | Required for low-calibration and later A1–A4 comparisons |
| Model/decoder identity | `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `model_family`, training status, checkpoint/artifact path, `ModelRegistryRecord` ID | Supports model-family and reproducibility comparisons |
| Score schema identity | `score_type`, `probability_vector` or logits/decision-score fallback, `class_order` | Required for raw metrics and downstream calibration/threshold eligibility |
| Randomness/config identity | `seed`, seed policy, `config_hash`, code version/environment hash | Required for reproducibility and seed summaries |
| Metric identity | `metric_id`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` reference, aggregation unit, directionality, confidence/seed summary status | Required for metric claim readiness |
| Comparison identity | `matched_comparison_key`, source-record IDs, ablation ID `A0`, comparator ablation ID where relevant | Required for fair A0-to-A1/A2/A3/A4/later comparisons |
| Claim/export identity | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` where needed, `NegativeResultNote` ID where applicable, limitation tags, claim-evidence row, dashboard/export IDs | Required for Layer 0 and Layer 10 traceability |

#### 10.2 Matched-comparison pass/fail rule

| Condition | Status |
|---|---|
| All required Layer 1, Layer 2, metric, comparison, and limitation keys are present and validate | `thesis_ready_for_A0_baseline_claim` |
| A0 metrics exist but one or more matched keys are missing | `diagnostic_only` unless the comparison is explicitly descriptive and non-claim-supporting |
| Split leakage, test-tuned preprocessing, or untracked exclusion affects A0 | `invalid_due_to_leakage` for affected claims until repaired and rerun |
| Metric is computed but lacks metric dictionary entry or required fields | `diagnostic_only_metric` |
| Dashboard displays A0 without source-record and metric lineage | `dashboard_output_invalid_for_claim` |
| A0 is compared against A1–A4 using non-identical or unrecorded protocols | `unmatched_comparison_diagnostic_only` |

---

### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

#### 11.1 Source-supported A0 metric families

A0 metrics must be limited to decoder-baseline evidence supported by the source documents. Exact final formulas, final statistical tests, final seed counts, final table numbering, and exact metric dictionary schema remain v1.0/run-matrix details unless the supplied sources already fix them.

| Metric family | A0 use | Required source records | Metric-dictionary status | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accuracy / balanced accuracy where applicable | Basic raw decoder performance | `PredictionRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord` | `MetricDictionaryEntry required; MC-008 unresolved schema/path` | Baseline decoder performance only |
| F1 / AUC where applicable | Class-imbalance or score-sensitive summaries when task-appropriate | `PredictionRecord`, score fields, class order, label map, `BaselineMetricRecord` | `MetricDictionaryEntry required; exact applicability requires confirmation` | Baseline metric only |
| Confusion-matrix lineage | Error structure and class-specific failure visibility | `PredictionRecord`, label map, split role, aggregation key | `MetricDictionaryEntry or table-definition entry required` | Error analysis, not clinical diagnosis |
| Low-calibration / low-label budget curve | Budget sensitivity of raw decoder | `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, budget config, split roles | `MetricDictionaryEntry required for plotted values` | Low-calibration benchmark only |
| Subject/session aggregation and variance/summary | Heterogeneity and reproducibility context | `SubjectProfileRecord` where coverage permits, `BaselineMetricRecord` | `MetricDictionaryEntry or descriptive-stat entry required` | Heterogeneity descriptor, no physiological or patient diagnosis |
| Confidence/score availability summaries | Downstream eligibility for A1–A3 | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, score type, class order | `MetricDictionaryEntry or validation-report entry required` | Score-schema readiness, not reliability proof |
| Failure/skipped/missingness counts | Transparency around unsupported or failed baselines | `ModelRegistryRecord`, failed/skipped logs, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport` | `MetricDictionaryEntry or failure taxonomy entry required for thesis tables` | Failure transparency only |
| Confidence intervals / seed summaries where available | Uncertainty-aware reporting of raw baseline metrics | `BaselineMetricRecord`, seed/config lineage | `requires_confirmation for exact method/statistical test` | Reproducibility summary, not definitive clinical proof |

#### 11.2 Forbidden or non-A0 metrics

| Metric class | A0 handling |
|---|---|
| Calibration metrics such as ECE, Brier, NLL, reliability diagrams | `downstream_context_only` for A1; do not report as A0 improvement evidence |
| Risk-coverage, retained accuracy, rejection rate, selective-prediction curves | `not_applicable_for_A0`; belongs to A3 except raw comparator fields |
| IHARQ accepted accuracy, wrong-accept after evidence verification, evidence-request burden, fallback burden | `not_applicable_for_A0`; belongs to A5+ |
| Policy reward, return, regret, deferral utility, sequential outcome | `not_applicable_for_A0`; simulation/policy branches only |
| Stress robustness drop or stress sensitivity | `downstream_context_only`; belongs to A12 |
| Endpoint error, command success, action safety, assistive-device metrics | `not_applicable_for_A0`; belongs to A13 and must be simulation/proxy-only |
| Clinical BCI-FES validation, patient safety, real rehabilitation efficacy, real-time deployment safety, medical-device readiness | `forbidden_metric_class` |

---

### 12. Split, Leakage, Threshold, Calibration, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint family | A0 requirement |
|---|---|
| Split discipline | A0 must use fixed Phase 1 split roles and must not tune preprocessing, model selection, threshold, or reported metric interpretation on held-out test data. |
| Leakage control | A0 is invalid for thesis claims if split overlap, train/test preprocessing leakage, label-map leakage, untracked exclusions, or test-tuned choices contaminate the result. |
| Calibration separation | A0 must remain raw. Calibration transforms belong to A1 and must be linked as downstream derived records, not overwritten raw predictions. |
| Threshold separation | No threshold-selection or registered rejection rule is allowed inside A0. If confidence thresholding is used, it belongs to A2. |
| Selective-prediction separation | No reject/coverage/risk rule is allowed inside A0. Selective prediction belongs to A3. |
| Model-family selection | Model families and fallback minimums must be declared before interpretation; failed/skipped/unsupported families must remain visible. |
| Score-field legality | Probability vectors, logits, or decision-score fallbacks must declare `score_type` and `class_order`; unsupported score fields restrict downstream A1–A3 eligibility. |
| Evaluation-only fields | `label_true`, `is_correct`, `error_type_raw`, and high-confidence-wrong indicators may be used for scoring or offline audit but must never become decision-time features in downstream policies. |
| Policy/update separation | A0 is frozen/offline baseline evidence. It must not include policy updates, adaptive thresholding, or downstream feedback mutation. |
| Simulation separation | A0 is not a simulated closed-loop record. Accept-all simulation baselines must be defined in later Layer 7/A10/A11 sections if used. |
| Stress separation | A0 clean baseline evidence must remain distinct from stress-conditioned evidence. Stress belongs to A12 unless the later protocol explicitly declares stress-conditioned A0 context. |
| Embodiment separation | A0 must not claim command, endpoint, safety, or assistive-action consequences. Embodiment-proxy evidence belongs to A13. |

---

### 13. Local Sub-Ablation Policy for A0

No new official top-level ablation ID is introduced. A0 variants should be handled through configuration fields rather than new global identifiers.

| Variant type | Protocol handling | ID policy |
|---|---|---|
| Model-family variants | Store as `model_family`, `decoder_id`, `model_id`, training status, config hash, seed | Not new ablation IDs |
| Low-calibration budget variants | Store as `label_budget_id` and budget config/version | Not new ablation IDs |
| Subject/session aggregation | Store as aggregation level in metric dictionary and `BaselineMetricRecord` | Not new ablation IDs |
| Score-type variants | Store as `score_type`, class order, and model registry compatibility | Not new ablation IDs |
| Failed/skipped/unsupported variants | Store in `ModelRegistryRecord`, logs, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, and negative-result notes | Not new ablation IDs |
| Future A0.1/A0.2-style local sub-IDs | Allowed only if a later framework/source explicitly requests them | `inferred_candidate`, `requires_confirmation: true` |

---

### 14. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 may read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, card, export, and package A0 records. It must not train models, tune thresholds, change metrics after results, recalibrate probabilities, repair splits, rewrite source records, hide failed/skipped runs, or produce hidden primary evidence.

#### 14.1 Required Layer 10 outputs for A0

| Layer 10 output family | Required A0 content | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Decoder baseline page | A0 raw-decoder tables, filters by dataset/model/subject/session/split/budget/seed, warning banners | `required` |
| Model-family comparison view | Model registry status, skipped/failed/unsupported notes, score compatibility, class order, model artifacts | `required_where_multiple_families_exist` |
| Low-calibration curve view | Budgeted raw decoder metrics with source `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` links | `required_where_low_calibration_claim_is_made` |
| A0 raw-decoder table export | Metric dictionary IDs, source prediction IDs, matched comparison keys, diagnostic flags, limitation tags | `required_for_thesis_claims` |
| Baseline comparison table | Internal A0 family comparisons and A0-to-A1/A2/A3/A4 linkage where later sections exist | `required_for_comparative_claims` |
| Decoder/model/benchmark card source bundle or rendered card | Summary of source records, metrics, limitations, reproduction command, warnings | `required_for_thesis-facing_reporting_if_cards_used` |
| Warning and diagnostic-only surface | Missing records, split leakage, unmatched keys, metric gaps, failed/skipped runs, score incompatibility | `required` |
| Export manifest | Export hash, source records, metric definitions, run/config/seed, schema versions, generated artifact IDs | `required_for_reproducibility` |
| Figure/table lineage manifest | Source-record IDs, figure/table IDs, metric dictionary entries, warning/limitation tags | `required_for_thesis_figures_tables` |
| Claim-evidence view/export | A0 claim rows, supporting records, metric IDs, matched comparison IDs, limitation tags | `required_for_final_claims; schema/name requires_confirmation` |

#### 14.2 Layer 10 not-applicable outputs for A0

| Output | Status |
|---|---|
| IHARQ flow/reason-code page | `not_applicable_for_A0` |
| RegimeRisk timeline page | `not_applicable_for_A0` |
| Policy rollout/reward/update trace page | `not_applicable_for_A0` |
| StressForge robustness page | `downstream_context_only_for_A12` |
| Layer 9 embodiment page | `not_applicable_for_A0` |

---

### 15. Layer 0 Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

#### 15.1 Allowed A0 claims

A0 may support only bounded claims such as:

| Allowed claim type | Required support |
|---|---|
| The project establishes a reproducible raw decoder baseline under public EEG protocol constraints | Valid Layer 1 records, Layer 2 prediction/model/metric records, metric dictionary linkage, reproducibility manifest |
| Raw decoder performance is measured across declared datasets, subjects/sessions, windows, splits, budgets, seeds, and model families where available | Matched keys, aggregation definition, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, model registry status |
| A0 provides the reference for calibration, threshold, selective-prediction, ordinary-control, IHARQ, policy, stress, and embodiment comparisons | A0 source IDs and matched-comparison keys consumed by later sections |
| A0 reveals decoder difficulty, failure cases, score-field limitations, and baseline sufficiency/insufficiency | Failure logs, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags |
| Strong raw accuracy alone is insufficient to claim readiness | Layer 0 limitation language plus A1–A5+ comparator evidence where generated |

#### 15.2 Forbidden A0 claims

A0 must not claim or imply:

- clinical BCI validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real-time deployment safety;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real assistive-device performance;
- validated therapeutic effectiveness;
- validated physiological fatigue or drift diagnosis;
- that dashboard visuals are independent scientific evidence;
- that raw decoder confidence is calibrated reliability;
- that high raw accuracy proves readiness, safety, or closed-loop control validity.

#### 15.3 Required limitation labels

A0 outputs should carry limitation labels including, where applicable:

`public_eeg_only`, `decoder_baseline_only`, `low_calibration_protocol`, `evaluation_only`, `diagnostic_only`, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, `not_medical_device_readiness`, `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`, `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`, `not_real_deployment_readiness`, `dashboard_derived_only`, `metric_dictionary_required`, and `matched_keys_required`.

---

### 16. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

| A0 result pattern | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| Weak raw decoder performance | Does not invalidate Stretch C. It reveals decoder/protocol difficulty and may motivate calibration, selective prediction, IHARQ, deferral, or robustness controls. Must be visible as a negative/boundary result. |
| Strong raw decoder performance | Does not prove readiness, safety, calibration quality, policy validity, stress robustness, or embodiment consequence. Later reliability-control claims still require matched comparisons and claim boundaries. |
| A0 equals or exceeds later A1–A5 variants under matched conditions | Later improvement claims must be narrowed; the thesis may report that raw decoder or simpler baseline is strong under that protocol. |
| A0 fails for some model families or datasets | Failed/skipped/unsupported runs must remain visible; optional/stretch model coverage may be skipped if honestly documented. |
| A0 metrics are missing metric dictionary definitions | Metric-based claims are diagnostic-only until definitions and fields are registered. |
| A0 matched keys are incomplete | A0 may remain exploratory/descriptive, but A0-to-A1/A2/A3/A4/later comparisons are diagnostic-only or blocked. |
| A0 has leakage or test-tuned choices | Affected claims are invalid until repaired and rerun. |

#### 16.1 Baseline sufficiency rule

A0 is sufficient as a reference only if it includes validated source records, model provenance, raw predictions, metric definitions, split/budget/model/seed lineage, failure visibility, Layer 10 source/export lineage, and Layer 0 limitation tags. A0 is not sufficient merely because a raw accuracy number exists.

---

### 17. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

| Trigger | Downgrade/action |
|---|---|
| Missing or invalid `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, or `LabelMapRecord` | Block affected thesis-ready A0 use or mark diagnostic-only |
| Missing `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` or incomplete matched-key readiness | A0–A4 comparisons diagnostic-only until repaired |
| Split leakage, preprocessing leakage, label-map leakage, test-tuned model/metric selection, or untracked exclusion | `invalid_due_to_leakage` for affected claims |
| Missing `PredictionRecord` for required dataset/model/split/budget | A0 evidence incomplete; affected group blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Orphan prediction file without `ModelRegistryRecord` | Reproducibility failure; affected metric diagnostic-only |
| Missing `score_type`, `class_order`, probability/logit/score fallback declaration | A0 metric may be limited; downstream calibration/threshold/selective use blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Missing `BaselineMetricRecord` or metric dictionary linkage | Metric/table claim diagnostic-only |
| Missing `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` where low-calibration claim is made | Low-calibration claim blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Hidden failed/skipped/unsupported run | Claim invalid until failure is surfaced |
| Missing `Layer2ReadinessReport` | Downstream A1–A13 use of A0 source evidence blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Missing `MatchedComparisonReport` for A0 comparison | Comparison claim diagnostic-only |
| Missing `NegativeResultNote` where baseline underperforms, fails, adds limitation, or is sufficient against later modules | Claim weakened or invalid due to hidden negative result |
| Missing `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` despite known gap | Layer 0 claim-safety violation |
| Dashboard/card/export lacks source-record, metric, config, seed, warning, or claim-evidence lineage | Layer 10 output invalid for thesis evidence |
| A0 wording implies clinical, deployment, patient-safety, real-time, therapeutic, or real muscle stimulation readiness | `invalid_due_to_claim_violation` until rewritten |

### 19. Handoff to Later Protocol Sections

| Later section | A0 handoff obligation |
|---|---|
| A1 — Calibrated decoder | Use A0 `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, raw metrics, and split/budget/model/seed lineage as comparator; do not overwrite raw predictions |
| A2 — Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Compare thresholded outputs against A0 at matched coverage/wrong-accept cost using registered threshold lineage; threshold tuning belongs to A2 |
| A3 — Uncertainty and selective prediction | Use A0 as raw no-rejection reference; compare risk/coverage or uncertainty-aware rejection under matched keys |
| A4 — Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, ordinary ensembles | Use A0 single/raw decoder reference; ordinary aggregation controls remain A4, not A0 |
| A5–A7 — IHARQ / evidence-quality / RegimeRisk | Use A0 as raw baseline context only after matched comparison keys and Layer 2 readiness validate |
| A8–A11 — deferral, supervised policy, bandit, RL | Treat A0 as raw/accept-all comparator only under simulation/policy records and no future-field leakage |
| A12 — StressForge | If raw decoder is stress-tested, mark stress-conditioned evidence under A12 while preserving A0 clean reference lineage |
| A13 — embodiment demo | Use A0 accept-all action only as an A13 comparator with Layer 9 command/embodiment records and simulation-only warning |
| Metric-family section | Finalize A0 metric dictionary entries, aggregation levels, directionality, confidence/seed summary rules, and diagnostic-only metric triggers |
| Matched-comparison rules section | Reuse A0 key envelope and diagnostic-only handling as the baseline discipline for all later comparisons |
| Layer 10 obligations section | Preserve read-only dashboard/export role and source-vs-derived distinction established here |
| Layer 0 claim-safety section | Preserve allowed/forbidden A0 claim classes and limitation labels established here |

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A1 identity

A1 is the calibrated-decoder / calibration-visibility evaluation context. It evaluates whether the raw decoder scores produced under A0 can be transformed into split-safe calibrated probabilities and reliability-visible outputs without claiming that calibration alone makes the system safe, clinically valid, deployment-ready, or action-ready.

A1 is not a new decoder training phase. It is not a thresholding baseline, not selective prediction, not IHARQ, not RegimeRisk, not a learned policy, not stress testing, and not embodiment. It is the calibration slice of Layer 3 / Phase 3 evidence.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

A1 answers the following question:

> Given the same public-data protocol, fixed splits, preprocessing, label maps, model families, seeds, label budgets, prediction records, and metric definitions used by A0, do declared calibration methods make decoder confidence more reliable and more auditable, and where do they fail?

The question is deliberately about reliability visibility and calibration quality, not about real-world safety. A1 may support claims such as “calibration made confidence calibration measurable and revealed high-confidence wrong behavior under public EEG benchmark conditions.” It must not support claims that calibrated outputs are safe decisions, clinical readiness evidence, real patient-safety evidence, or validated assistive-control evidence.

#### 3.3 A1 contribution to the cumulative protocol

| A1 role | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| Calibration comparator | A1 compares calibrated probabilities/confidence against A0 raw probabilities/confidence under matched source lineage. |
| Reliability-visibility layer | A1 makes ECE-style summaries, Brier score, NLL, reliability diagrams, confidence histograms, bin-level behavior, and high-confidence wrong cases visible. |
| Fairness gate for downstream controls | A1 prevents IHARQ, threshold, selective-prediction, and policy branches from being credited before calibrated-confidence evidence and calibration failures are visible. |
| Negative-result source | If calibration fails or does not improve ECE/Brier/NLL, A1 still produces thesis-relevant limitation evidence and negative-result notes. |
| Claim-safety anchor | A1 narrows confidence-related claims to public-data, offline/proxy, diagnostic, calibration-visibility evidence. |

| `MetricDictionaryEntry` | Evaluation framework / producing phase references | Phase 0 template; Phases 2–15 use | Defines A1 metric computations, units, source records, limitations | `required_but_schema_path_unresolved_MC-008` |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Evaluation framework / Phase 15 integration with phase inputs | Phase 0 template; Phase 15 integration | Confirms A0–A1 matched keys and comparison status | `source_supported_evaluation_artifact`; exact schema/path may require confirmation |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Evaluation / Layer 0 governed note | Phase 0 template; Phase 3/15 use | Records calibration failure, no improvement, ineligibility, or weaker-than-A0 results | `source_supported_required_when_applicable` |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Evaluation / Layer 0 governed flag | Phase 0 template; Phases 1–15 use | Marks unmatched, leakage-affected, metric-undefined, or incomplete A1 outputs | `source_supported_required_when_applicable` |
| `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` | Layer 0 / Phase 15 governed, alias unresolved | Phase 15 | Links A1 claims to source records, metrics, limitations, warnings | `requires_confirmation`; alias issue preserved |

### 8. Producer Layer and Producer Phase Summary

| Evidence class | A1 role | Producing layer | Producing phase | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Public-data/protocol source lineage | Required input | Layer 1 | Phase 1 | Immutable source records; A1 cannot mutate them |
| Raw predictions and model lineage | Required input and A0 comparator | Layer 2 | Phase 2 | A1 consumes same prediction/model lineage used by A0 where possible |
| Calibration parameters and calibrated probabilities | Core A1 evidence | Layer 3 | Phase 3 | Must be fitted on legal calibration split, never final test |
| Reliability audit and high-confidence wrong diagnostics | Core A1 evidence | Layer 3 | Phase 3 | Evaluation-only labels allowed for scoring/audit only |
| Dashboard/card/export views | Derived reporting | Layer 10 | Phase 14 | Reads source records and renders views; does not create hidden primary evidence |
| Final claim integration | Claim governance/reporting | Layer 0 / Phase 15 claim integration | Phase 15 | Layer 0 governs claims; Phase 15 integrates; neither produces calibration measurements |

---

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

| Comparator | Required use in A1 | Match requirement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / no-rejection raw reference | Primary comparator for raw-vs-calibrated confidence/probability reliability | Same `PredictionRecord` IDs where possible; otherwise same dataset, subject/session, window/trial, split, model family/model ID, label budget, seed, preprocessing, label map, score type, class order, metric dictionary | A0 accuracy may remain unchanged; A1 tests confidence reliability, not safety |
| No-calibration baseline within the calibrator | Calibration-method anchor where Layer 3 evaluates calibration methods | Same calibration/test split, model, score schema, and metric definitions | This is not a new top-level ablation; it is a local A1 method baseline |
| Temperature scaling / Platt scaling / isotonic / vector scaling / pooled or per-model calibration where feasible | Source-supported local method comparisons | Same calibration data budget and legal selection rules; exact method set requires final run-matrix confirmation | Method comparisons are calibration evidence only; no deployment/safety claim |
| A2 simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Downstream comparator when thresholding calibrated confidence is evaluated | Must use registered threshold, legal selection split, and matched coverage/cost rules under A2 | Not an A1 result unless only referenced as downstream context |
| A3 uncertainty/selective-prediction baseline | Downstream comparator for risk/coverage and uncertainty-aware rejection | Requires A3 records, risk-coverage definitions, and matched operating points | Do not report A3 selective gains as A1 calibration gains |
| A4 ordinary-combination controls | Nearby ordinary-control context | Requires `EnsembleControlRecord` / longer-window or multi-window lineage where applicable | Do not confuse ordinary combination with calibration |
| A5+ IHARQ/readiness branches | Later system comparators | Must include A1 source IDs and matched keys but must satisfy their own section-specific requirements | A1 alone does not prove IHARQ or readiness value |

#### 9.1 Calibration-specific comparison rules

1. A1 should compare raw confidence/probability reliability against calibrated confidence/probability reliability using matched prediction rows.
2. A1 must not claim improved classification performance unless the calibrated decision rule explicitly permits changed top-1 prediction and the source records, metrics, and method configuration support that comparison.
3. Pure probability calibration should primarily be interpreted through ECE-style summaries, Brier score, NLL, reliability diagrams, confidence histograms, calibration-bin statistics, and high-confidence-wrong visibility.
4. If calibration improves one metric but worsens another, the result must be reported as mixed rather than converted into a single unqualified improvement claim.
5. If A0 raw confidence is already strong or calibration is ineffective, the thesis claim must narrow to calibration visibility, negative-result evidence, or baseline sufficiency.

---

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

A1-to-A0 comparisons are thesis-ready only when the following keys are complete or explicitly marked not applicable.

| Key family | Required keys | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset/protocol | `dataset_id`, dataset version/source, task label space, protocol ID/version, public-data limitation tag | Missing or mismatched keys downgrade comparison to diagnostic-only |
| Subject/session/trial/window | `subject_id`, `session_id` where available, `trial_id`, `window_id`, aggregation unit, optional temporal order | Missing row-level lineage blocks row-matched calibration deltas |
| Split and leakage | `split_id`, `split_role`, calibration split ID, test split ID, threshold-validation split where relevant, nested-CV fold IDs where used, leakage-check status | Calibration/test overlap invalidates affected A1 final claims |
| Preprocessing/window/label map | preprocessing ID/version, windowing ID/version, label-map version, class order | Mismatch blocks direct A0–A1 delta claims |
| Model and score schema | `model_id`, decoder ID, model family, checkpoint/registry path, seed, config hash, `score_type`, `class_order`, probability/logit/score availability | Missing score schema blocks calibration-dependent comparisons or marks them diagnostic-only |
| Low-calibration budget | `label_budget_id`, calibration budget, budget config/version, calibration data count, per-class availability | Sparse/missing class budget restricts method eligibility and may force pooled/fallback/diagnostic status |
| Calibration method | calibration method ID, method scope, parameter config, calibration split, fit seed, config hash | Unregistered or test-tuned method is invalid for final claims |
| Metric dictionary | metric IDs for ECE-style, Brier, NLL, reliability-bin summaries, confidence histogram, high-confidence wrong rate, calibration deltas | Undefined metric is diagnostic-only under `MC-008` |
| Evaluation/export lineage | source record IDs, metric computation version, comparison key, dashboard export ID, manifest checksum, limitation tags | Missing Layer 10 lineage blocks thesis-ready export |
| Claim-safety | claim ID, limitation tags, diagnostic-only flag status, negative-result note status, Layer 0 review status | Missing claim boundary blocks final claim use |

#### 10.1 Matchability status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning for A1 |
|---|---|
| `fully_matched` | A1 may support thesis-ready A0–A1 calibration claims if metrics, exports, and claim review are also complete. |
| `partially_matched` | A1 may support narrowed or subgroup-specific claims only for keys that are complete. |
| `unmatched_diagnostic` | A1 can be used for debugging, method exploration, or limitations, but not for final improvement claims. |
| `invalid_until_repaired` | Leakage, hidden test tuning, or missing source lineage requires repair and rerun before use. |
