### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

| Metric family | A1 use | Source records | Metric dictionary status | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ECE-style calibration error | Core calibration-quality metric family | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, bin tables | `MetricDictionaryEntry required`; exact binning and schema require confirmation | Calibration visibility only |
| Brier score | Core probabilistic scoring metric | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport` | `MetricDictionaryEntry required` | Probability quality, not clinical safety |
| Negative log-likelihood / NLL | Core probabilistic scoring metric where probability support exists | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport` | `MetricDictionaryEntry required` | Probability quality; sensitive to score support |
| Reliability diagrams and bin-level summaries | Core visualization/audit family | `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` | Plot/table source must reference metric dictionary and bin config | Derived views must remain traceable |
| Confidence histograms | Calibration and overconfidence visibility | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport` | `MetricDictionaryEntry or report definition required` | Descriptive reliability evidence only |
| High-confidence wrong rate / table | Failure visibility and downstream diagnostic input | `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, source predictions | `MetricDictionaryEntry required` for rate; table is diagnostic/evaluation-only | Not decision-time feature; not safety proof |
| Raw-vs-calibrated deltas | A0–A1 comparison | A0 `BaselineMetricRecord` / `PredictionRecord`, A1 `CalibrationRecord`, matched comparison report | Delta metric entries required | Improvement claim only if fully matched and metric-defined |
| Group-wise calibration summaries | Class, subject, session, model-family, budget diagnostics | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, source records | `MetricDictionaryEntry required` for thesis-facing claims | Subgroup results may be diagnostic if sparse |
| Calibration eligibility / missingness rate | Validity/missingness audit | `CalibrationEligibilityTable`, `SplitIntegrityReport` | Definition required for table/card use | Missingness visible; not performance metric |
| Accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1, AUC | Upstream A0/context metrics only unless calibrated argmax changes are explicitly evaluated | `BaselineMetricRecord`, possibly `CalibrationRecord` if class changes are supported | Existing metric dictionary required | Do not treat unchanged accuracy as calibration improvement |
| Entropy, margin, risk-coverage, retained accuracy, rejection rate | A3/A2 context only unless shown as companion diagnostics | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord` | Belongs primarily to A3/A2 metric sections | Not A1 core improvement evidence |
| Stress drop, endpoint error, reward, safety event, embodiment outcome | Not applicable to A1 | Later records only | Not A1 metrics | Forbidden as A1 evidence |

#### 11.1 Metric interpretation rules

- A1 metric families must be reported with metric-definition IDs, binning/aggregation rules, source records, seeds, config hashes, and limitation tags.
- Calibration improvement is not a single scalar claim unless the protocol later defines a combined ranking rule. In v0.1, ECE-style, Brier, NLL, reliability diagrams, and high-confidence wrong results must remain visible separately.
- If one calibration method improves ECE but worsens NLL or Brier, the output must report a mixed calibration result and avoid ranking language unless a predeclared metric priority exists.
- If a metric definition is missing, the affected metric is diagnostic-only even if the underlying values can be computed.

---

### 12. Split, Leakage, Calibration, Threshold, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint class | A1 rule |
|---|---|
| Split separation | Calibration parameters must be fitted on a legal calibration split, validation fold, or nested-CV calibration partition. Final test labels must not be used to fit, select, or tune calibration. |
| Calibration/test leakage | Any overlap or hidden post-hoc method selection using final test results invalidates the affected final A1 claim and requires `LeakageWarningRecord` plus diagnostic-only/invalid status. |
| Calibration-method selection | Method set and method-selection rule must be declared before final evaluation. Exact final method grid and selection criterion require v1.0 confirmation unless already fixed. |
| Low-calibration budget | A1 must preserve `label_budget_id` and calibration budget; insufficient per-class calibration data must be visible through `CalibrationEligibilityTable`. |
| Score-field legality | A1 requires probability vectors, logits, or declared score conversions with `score_type` and `class_order`. Class-label-only outputs are ineligible or diagnostic-only for calibration metrics requiring probabilities. |
| Evaluation-only labels | Labels and correctness are allowed for fitting calibration on permitted splits and scoring/auditing on evaluation splits; they must never be downstream decision-time features. |
| Raw record immutability | A1 creates derived `CalibrationRecord` outputs and must not overwrite A0 `PredictionRecord` or Layer 2 raw metrics. |
| Threshold separation | A1 may produce calibrated confidence used later by A2/A3, but threshold selection/evaluation is not an A1 result unless clearly marked downstream context. |
| Policy/update separation | A1 is frozen reliability evidence. It does not update policy, reward, transition, bandit, or RL records. |
| Simulation separation | A1 does not produce closed-loop simulation evidence. Later simulation sections may consume A1 source IDs under their own rules. |
| Stress separation | Clean A1 evidence and stress-conditioned A1-derived evidence must be separated; stress robustness belongs to A12. |
| Embodiment separation | A1 does not produce command, endpoint, outcome, or real assistive-control evidence; embodiment-proxy evidence belongs to A13. |
| Dashboard separation | Layer 10 may render and export A1 records but cannot recalibrate, retune, or repair upstream evidence. |

---

### 13. Local Sub-Ablation Policy for A1

A1 may define local children only when they remain inside A1 and do not create new global ablation IDs.

| Local ID | Candidate meaning | Source status | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A1.0` | No-calibration method anchor inside Layer 3 calibration method evaluation | `source_supported_as_method_baseline` | Must not replace A0; used only to isolate calibration-method effects under the same Phase 3 pipeline |
| `A1.1` | Temperature scaling where logits or compatible scores exist | `source_supported` | Exact inclusion and grid require confirmation; ineligible if logits/scores unsupported |
| `A1.2` | Platt scaling / one-vs-rest or binary-compatible calibration | `source_supported` | Must declare class handling and metric definitions |
| `A1.3` | Isotonic calibration where enough legal calibration data exist | `source_supported` | Must monitor overfitting and mark sparse budgets diagnostic-only |
| `A1.4` | Vector scaling or other declared feasible method | `source_supported_as_declared_feasible_method` | Exact method definition requires metric/config confirmation |
| `A1.5` | Pooled/global versus per-model calibration scope | `source_supported` | Must preserve calibration scope, budget, split, and model-family lineage |
| `A1.6` | Subject/session-aware calibration diagnostics | `optional_or_diagnostic_only` | Do not turn into thesis-ready subgroup claim unless sample size, split legality, and metric definitions support it |
| `A1.7` | Calibration-budget sensitivity | `source_supported_context` | Requires `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`/budget lineage and metric dictionary entries |

**Sub-ablation rule:** none of these local IDs may be promoted to `A14` or to a new top-level ablation. If the final run matrix does not include a local A1 child, the section should mark it `not_run`, `optional_only`, or `requires_confirmation` rather than implying completion.

---

### 14. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 may read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, card, export, and package A1 source records. It must not fit calibrators, choose calibration methods, tune thresholds, recompute hidden metrics, repair split leakage, hide negative results, rewrite source records, or create primary empirical evidence.

| Layer 10 output | A1 content | Required source lineage | Missingness handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibration and uncertainty page | A1 reliability diagrams, ECE/Brier/NLL summaries, confidence histograms, high-confidence wrong summaries | `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, source prediction/model/split IDs | Page/card marked diagnostic-only or blocked if source lineage missing |
| Reliability card | Calibration method/scope, split legality, metric summaries, warnings, limitation tags, high-confidence wrong diagnostics | `ReliabilityCard` source bundle, `CalibrationRecord`, `SplitIntegrityReport`, `CalibrationEligibilityTable` | Warning banner and no thesis-ready card if unresolved |
| A0–A1 comparison table | Raw-vs-calibrated deltas and matchability status | A0 source records, A1 records, matched-comparison keys, metric dictionary entries | Comparison downgraded to diagnostic-only when keys incomplete |
| Calibration eligibility view | Sparse budgets, missing classes, fallback methods, invalid runs | `CalibrationEligibilityTable`, split/source lineage | Method-specific claims blocked for ineligible cells |
| Leakage and split-integrity warning panel | Calibration/test overlap, missing split roles, hidden test tuning warnings | `SplitIntegrityReport`, `LeakageWarningRecord` | Final claims invalid or diagnostic-only |
| High-confidence wrong view | Confident wrong prediction examples and grouped counts | `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, source records, limitation tags | Offline diagnostic only; never downstream decision-time feature |
| Export manifest | Reproducibility package linking records, configs, metrics, cards, figures, warnings, limitation tags | Source record IDs, config hashes, seeds, metric dictionary IDs, export checksum | Export not thesis-ready if lineage incomplete |
| Figure/table lineage manifest | Reliability diagram and table provenance | Figure/table source records, metric definitions, binning configs, seeds | Figure/table cannot be final evidence without source manifest |
| Claim-evidence export | A1-supported claim rows and limitations for Phase 15 | `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags | Alias/schema issue preserved; claim blocked if unresolved for final thesis |

### 15. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

#### 15.1 Allowed bounded A1 claim classes

| Allowed claim class | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Calibration metrics were computed for eligible public EEG decoder outputs under declared split constraints | `CalibrationRecord`, `SplitIntegrityReport`, metric dictionary entries, source prediction/model/split lineage |
| Calibrated confidence/probability reliability was compared with raw A0 confidence under matched conditions | A0 and A1 source IDs, matched keys, `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric entries |
| Calibration revealed high-confidence wrong cases or overconfidence pockets that raw accuracy alone could hide | `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, source records, limitation tags |
| Calibration failed, was mixed, or was insufficient under certain datasets/models/budgets | `NegativeResultNote`, metric tables, eligibility/missingness artifacts |
| A1 provides bounded reliability evidence for downstream IHARQ/policy/stress/embodiment contexts | A1 source records plus downstream section-specific records; no stronger claim inside A1 |

#### 15.2 Forbidden or blocked claim classes

A1 must not claim any of the following:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real-time deployment safety;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real-world assistive control validation;
- real physiological stress validation;
- clinical fatigue diagnosis;
- validated therapeutic effectiveness;
- that calibrated confidence guarantees correct decisions;
- that calibration alone proves readiness or action safety;
- that dashboard reliability plots are independent primary evidence;
- that high-confidence-wrong tables can be used as decision-time labels or policy features.

#### 15.3 Required limitation labels

A1 outputs must carry the following limitation labels where applicable:

`public_eeg_only`, `offline_proxy_reliability`, `calibration_visibility_only`, `evaluation_only`, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, `not_medical_device_readiness`, `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`, `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`, `not_real_deployment_readiness`, `metric_dictionary_required`, `matched_keys_required`, `split_safe_calibration_required`, `dashboard_derived_only`, `diagnostic_only_when_unmatched`, and `negative_results_visible`.

---

### 16. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

| Result pattern | Required interpretation | Required artifact/action |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration improves ECE-style summaries but worsens Brier or NLL | Mixed calibration result; no unqualified improvement claim | Report all metrics and create limitation note if used in thesis |
| Calibration improves Brier/NLL but reliability diagram still shows subgroup overconfidence | Improvement is partial; subgroup limitation remains | Group-wise reliability audit and limitation tag |
| Calibration does not improve ECE, Brier, or NLL | Calibration method may not help that dataset/model/split; still valuable as visibility/failure evidence | `NegativeResultNote`; avoid claiming calibration improvement |
| A0 raw confidence is already well calibrated under matched keys | Baseline sufficiency; later improvements must be narrowed | A0–A1 comparison note and bounded claim |
| Calibration fails due to sparse calibration data or missing class coverage | Evidence is limited by calibration eligibility, not proof that calibration is impossible | `CalibrationEligibilityTable`, diagnostic-only flag for affected cells |
| Calibration metrics are unstable across seeds or budgets | Treat as low-calibration fragility; do not hide variance | Seed/budget summaries and limitation note |
| High-confidence wrong cases remain after calibration | Calibration visibility does not eliminate wrong-accept risk; motivates A2/A3/A5+ comparisons | `HighConfidenceWrongTable` and downstream handoff |
| A1 equals or underperforms A0 under all metrics | Improvement claim blocked; report negative result and baseline sufficiency | `NegativeResultNote`, Layer 0 narrowed claim |
| A1 comparison is unmatched or metric-undefined | Diagnostic-only; no thesis-ready comparative claim | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, Layer 10 warning |

### 17. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

| Trigger | Downgrade rule | Required visible record/warning |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, or `LabelMapRecord` | Affected A1 result is blocked or diagnostic-only | Validation report and diagnostic flag |
| Missing `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` or readiness false for A1 context | A1 comparison not thesis-ready | Readiness warning in Layer 10 export |
| Missing `PredictionRecord` or orphan prediction without `ModelRegistryRecord` | Calibration cannot be source-grounded | Diagnostic-only or blocked |
| Missing probability vector/logits/declared score fallback | Calibration metrics requiring probabilities are ineligible | `CalibrationEligibilityTable` and score-schema warning |
| Missing `score_type` or `class_order` | Calibration unreliable/uninterpretable | Diagnostic-only for affected runs |
| Calibration/test split overlap | Final A1 claim invalid until repaired and rerun | `LeakageWarningRecord`, `SplitIntegrityReport` |
| Calibration method selected using final test performance | Invalid for final claim; exploratory only at best | Leakage/method-selection warning |
| Missing `CalibrationEligibilityTable` | Method eligibility cannot be trusted | Diagnostic-only method claims |
| Missing `CalibrationRecord` for eligible predictions | A1 evidence missing | Block or diagnostic-only |
| Missing `ReliabilityAuditReport` for thesis-facing A1 | Reliability visibility incomplete | Dashboard/card warning and no final claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entries for ECE/Brier/NLL/binning/high-confidence wrong | Metric output diagnostic-only | `MC-008` warning and diagnostic flag |
| Missing A0–A1 matched keys | Comparative improvement claim diagnostic-only | `MatchedComparisonReport` / diagnostic status |
| Hidden failed/skipped/unsupported calibration runs | Claim invalid or weakened | Failure/missingness warning |
| High-confidence wrong table uses correctness as downstream feature | Policy/readiness branch invalid; A1 table remains offline diagnostic only | Layer 0 claim-safety warning |
| Layer 10 export lacks source record IDs/config/seed/metric lineage | Dashboard output not thesis-ready | Export manifest warning |
| Layer 0 review or limitation tags absent | Claim cannot be final thesis/paper claim | Claim-safety block |

## A2 — Simple Registered Threshold / Confidence-Threshold Baseline

**Generated target:** `A2`  
**Protocol version:** `v0.1`  
**Generation mode:** append new target section to existing protocol  
**Previous protocol sections provided:** `YES — A0, A1`  
**Previous protocol section preservation:** the supplied A0 and A1 sections remain present above this A2 section and are semantically preserved. In this user-authorized cumulative revision, only framework-grounded structural/handoff repairs are applied where needed; no earlier scientific claim, source record, metric status, open issue, or limitation boundary is broadened.  
**Output behavior applied:** `append_new_section_to_existing_protocol`

**Revision status:** generated and re-audited against the zip-contained prompt, protocol-generation framework, Master Architecture Specification, Canonical Artifact/Record/Interface Registry, Phase 0–15 Execution and Evidence Plan, and the supplied A0/A1 protocol sections. This cumulative professional pass keeps A0/A1/A2 scientifically and semantically aligned while applying only user-authorized structural/handoff corrections where required.

---

### 0. Document Control, Target Resolution, and Continuity Decision

|---|---|
| Protocol document | IHARQ BenchGuard Stretch C — Experiment, Ablation, and Evaluation Protocol |
| Protocol version label resolved for this output | `v0.1` |
| Target selected in prompt | `A2` |
| Official target identity | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline |

| A2 producer status | A2 is **not** a producing layer, implementation phase, module, or schema owner. It is an evaluation-use identifier for registered threshold evidence produced by Layer 3 / Phase 3. |
| Primary producing layer for A2 source evidence | Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction |
| Primary producing implementation phase | Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty |
| Required upstream foundation | Phase 0 repository/config/schema/evaluation-fixture foundation; Phase 1 public-data/split protocol records; Phase 2 baseline prediction/model records; A1 calibration context when calibrated-confidence thresholds are evaluated |

| Nearby but separate ablations | A3 uncertainty and selective prediction; A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls |

| Capability-tier relationship | C0 public-data reliability baseline directly; C1–C4 downstream context only where later sections consume A2 as a comparator under their own evidence rules |
| Claim boundary | Public EEG, offline/proxy threshold-baseline evidence only; registered operating point, not safety threshold; no clinical, deployment, patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation, or real-time control claim |

#### 0.1 Continuity decision

The current zip includes a previously generated cumulative protocol containing A0 and A1. Under the original `OUTPUT_MODE: append_new_section_to_existing_protocol`, those sections were preserved exactly as provided during the original A2 append step. Under the current user-authorized cumulative revision, they remain semantically preserved while framework-grounded Markdown hierarchy, handoff-schema, and stale next-section repairs may be applied and documented.

The A0 section remains the raw decoder reference. The A1 section remains calibration visibility. A2 is appended as the next distinct evaluation context and must not silently repair, rename, or reinterpret A0/A1 records. Any A2 comparison that depends on incomplete A0/A1 lineage is marked diagnostic-only rather than filled with inferred or dashboard-derived values.

#### 0.2 Target resolution note

The prompt’s version field still presents a choice-list placeholder, but the supplied framework is explicitly for `v0.1` and the prompt states that v0.1 is the default unless otherwise specified. This A2 section therefore uses `v0.1`. The selected target is `A2`; no A3–A13 section is generated here except for relationship, comparator, and handoff references required to preserve the complete A0–A13 ladder.

A2 must not collapse into A3 uncertainty/selective prediction, must not absorb A4 ordinary combination controls, and must not treat registered thresholds as safety approvals.

---

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A2 identity

A2 is the **simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline**. It evaluates whether a declared confidence or calibrated-confidence threshold, selected using legal validation or nested-CV rules and recorded in a threshold registry, is sufficient to reduce wrong accepts or improve retained-output behavior before IHARQ, RegimeRisk, learned readiness policies, stress testing, or embodiment-proxy branches are credited with added value.

A2 is intentionally narrow. It is not generic uncertainty modeling, not full selective prediction, not entropy/margin/conformal-set evaluation, not ordinary voting/averaging/longer-window aggregation, not IHARQ evidence verification, and not a clinical safety threshold. It is a registered operating-point comparison for simple threshold rejection.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

A2 answers the following question:

> Given the same public-data protocol, fixed splits, preprocessing, label maps, model families, seeds, label budgets, prediction records, calibration records where applicable, threshold-selection split, threshold registry entry, matched comparison keys, and metric dictionary entries, does simple registered confidence-threshold rejection explain the apparent reliability gain that later IHARQ or adaptive readiness mechanisms might otherwise claim?

The question is deliberately about **baseline sufficiency and comparison fairness**. If a simple registered threshold performs as well as or better than a later mechanism under matched coverage/cost, that result must be preserved as a negative or sufficiency result. If it fails, that failure motivates later A3/A5+ comparisons but does not by itself prove clinical readiness or deployment safety.

#### 3.3 A2 contribution to the cumulative protocol

| A2 role | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| Simple rejection baseline | A2 tests whether top-confidence or calibrated-confidence thresholding is enough under legal threshold selection. |
| Registry discipline test | A2 verifies that every threshold has a `ThresholdRegistryRecord` with selected-on split, selection rule, target constraint, version, allowed consumers, leakage status, and rationale. |
| Matched operating-point anchor | A2 supplies matched coverage/cost rows and threshold lineage needed for A5+ comparisons. |
| Negative-result source | If thresholding is sufficient, later IHARQ/adaptive claims must be narrowed or downgraded rather than hiding the simpler baseline. |
| Claim-safety anchor | A2 prevents threshold baselines from being described as safety thresholds, deployment gates, clinical readiness criteria, or patient-specific decisions. |

---

### 4. Relationship to Official Layers 0–10

| Layer | Relationship to A2 | A2-specific requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Governs A2 claim wording, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, and forbidden threshold-safety language | Every A2 threshold result must be labeled as public-data, offline/proxy, registered-operating-point evidence only |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides source identities, split roles, window/trial lineage, label maps, preprocessing lineage, and ablation-readiness keys | A2 is thesis-ready only when threshold-selection, validation, and evaluation split roles are legal and source lineage is complete |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Provides raw `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, and A0 baseline context; may provide A4 ordinary controls separately | A2 consumes Layer 2 predictions but does not modify raw predictions or reassign A4 ordinary-control artifacts |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Primary source layer for A2 evidence | Produces/strengthens `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, split/leakage reports, and threshold comparison summaries used by A2 |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Downstream comparator/consumer | Must compare IHARQ against A2 where matched threshold baseline evidence exists; must not claim IHARQ superiority while ignoring threshold sufficiency |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Downstream context only | May consume threshold-aware reliability context where legal; must not retune A2 thresholds using temporal outcomes or claim clinical fatigue diagnosis |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Downstream consumer of legal threshold context | May consume threshold IDs and coverage/cost context as features or comparators where protocol permits; must not learn from or overwrite test-derived A2 thresholds |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Simulation-only downstream context | May compare simulated policy behavior against A2 baseline decisions under matched contexts; no real-time deployment claim follows |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite Stress Generator | Downstream stress context only | May evaluate clean-vs-stressed threshold robustness later under A12; A2 clean threshold baseline remains distinct from stress-generation evidence |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Embodiment-proxy downstream context only | May consume A2 decisions only as simulation/proxy inputs where later sections authorize it; no real muscle stimulation or embodied safety claim follows |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Read-only reporting/export consumer | Displays threshold audit panels, retained-coverage/retained-accuracy views, matched operating-point tables, warnings, cards, export manifests, and reproducibility lineage; must not tune thresholds or recompute hidden evidence |

#### 4.1 Non-forced layer content

| Content family | A2 status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Entropy, margin, conformal-set-size, broad uncertainty-feature selection | `downstream_or_nearby_A3_context_only` | These belong to A3 uncertainty/selective prediction unless explicitly reported as non-A2 context. |
| Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, probability averaging, ordinary ensembles | `nearby_A4_context_only` | These belong to A4 ordinary controls, not A2. |
| IHARQ accept/wait/request/combine/fallback/unsafe decision vocabulary | `downstream_context_only` | These belong to A5+ sections; A2 only accepts/rejects thresholded decoder outputs for baseline comparison. |
| Policy updates, bandit/RL rewards, closed-loop transitions | `not_applicable_for_A2` | A2 is not a policy-learning or simulation phase. |
| Stress profiles and embodiment outcome records | `future_work_or_downstream_context_only` | Stress and embodiment evidence are A12/A13 branches, not A2 outputs. |

### 5. Relationship to Official Phase 0–15 Sequence

| Phase | A2 relationship | Required treatment |
|---:|---|---|
| Phase 0 — Repository, configuration, and record schema | Provides schema/config/mock/metric/manifest conventions for threshold records and validation gates | A2 cannot be thesis-ready without schema, metric dictionary, diagnostic-only, negative-result, and manifest conventions |
| Phase 1 — Public data, split protocol, and low-calibration setup | Produces split/window/source protocol records and ablation readiness keys | A2 threshold selection and evaluation require legal, separated split roles and matched source keys |
| Phase 2 — Baseline decoders | Produces `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, A0 source evidence, score schemas, and A4 ordinary controls where compatible | A2 consumes predictions and score fields; no threshold claim is produced in Phase 2 |
| Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty | Produces/strengthens A2 threshold evidence | Primary producing phase for `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, split/leakage reports, and A2 comparison rows |
| Phase 4 — IHARQ evidence verification | Consumes A2 as comparator | A5/IHARQ claims must compare against A2 where matched threshold evidence exists |
| Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust | Downstream context | May consume threshold/context lineage where temporally legal, but cannot retune A2 or redefine threshold sufficiency |
| Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Downstream policy/evidence-quality context | Must preserve A2 threshold registry and no-test-tuning constraints when using threshold features or comparators |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | Downstream deferral context | Uses A2 only as a registered threshold comparator under matched cost/coverage rules |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | Downstream simulation context | A2 records may appear as frozen baseline inputs; simulation outcomes must not retune A2 final thresholds |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | Downstream stress context | A2 clean threshold baseline may be stressed later, but A2 itself does not generate stress schedules |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | Downstream bandit context | A2 is a frozen comparator/input only; it does not emit bandit actions, rewards, or regret |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream RL context | A2 is a frozen comparator/input only; it does not emit RL transitions, rewards, or policy updates |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | Downstream embodiment-proxy context | No A2 result becomes real actuation, endpoint-control, or real muscle stimulation evidence |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison | Optional downstream embodiment/replay context | A2 records remain provenance/comparator inputs only and cannot support real embodied-control claims |
| Phase 14 — Layer 10 dashboard and reproducibility | Renders and exports A2 views/cards/manifests | Dashboard outputs are derived/read-only and must preserve source lineage, warnings, and limitation tags |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | Consumes A2 as claim-bounded evidence | Final A2 claims require metric dictionary entries, matched comparisons, source lineage, Layer 10 export manifests, and Layer 0 review |

#### 5.1 Phase-readiness gates for A2

| Gate | Required pass condition | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 split legality | Calibration/threshold-selection/evaluation roles are separated and recorded | A2 final threshold claim blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Phase 2 score readiness | `PredictionRecord` includes legal score/probability fields, class order, score type, model registry lineage, and source IDs | A2 cannot compute or compare thresholded outputs thesis-readily |
| A1 calibration context, where used | `CalibrationRecord` exists and is split-safe when calibrated-confidence thresholding is evaluated | Calibrated-threshold variant omitted or diagnostic-only; raw-confidence threshold may still be evaluated if supported |
| Phase 3 threshold registry | Every threshold has a valid `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Threshold-based comparisons blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Matched operating-point completeness | `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` or equivalent matched coverage/cost rows link source IDs and metric dictionary entries | Comparative claims against A0/A1/A3/A4/A5+ downgraded |
| Phase 14 export lineage | Dashboard/cards/export manifests point back to source records and threshold registry IDs | Dashboard is useful for review but not thesis-ready evidence |
| Layer 0 review | Limitation tags, forbidden-claim checks, and diagnostic-only flags are present | Final A2 claim blocked |

### 6. Relationship to A0–A13 and Nearby Ablations

| Ablation ID | Official identity | A2 relationship and boundary |
|---:|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder / accept-all raw decoder reference | Primary no-rejection comparator. A2 must show what changes when simple threshold rejection is applied to the same prediction lineage. |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder / calibration visibility | Upstream calibrated-confidence source where A2 evaluates calibrated probability thresholds. A1 does not itself own threshold selection. |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Current target. Registered threshold baseline only; not a producer and not a safety gate. |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Nearby but distinct. A3 may use uncertainty features and broader risk-coverage/selective-prediction behavior; A2 remains simple thresholding. |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Nearby but distinct ordinary-combination controls. A2 must not absorb voting/averaging/ensemble controls. |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Downstream comparator. A5 must prove value beyond A2 when thresholding is a valid matched baseline. |
| A6 | IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator | Downstream comparator/context only; A2 supplies threshold baseline and registry context. |
| A7 | IHARQ plus RegimeRisk temporal trust | Downstream temporal-trust context only; A2 is not a regime-risk or fatigue-diagnosis result. |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Downstream deferral baseline context only; A2 rejection is not the full deferral policy. |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Downstream learned readiness context only; A2 is a non-adaptive threshold baseline. |
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Simulation-bounded downstream context only. |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Simulation-bounded downstream context only. |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests / controlled stress robustness | Downstream stress context only; A2 clean threshold evidence may be reused as baseline if matched clean/stressed lineage exists. |
| A13 | Layer 9 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Downstream embodiment-proxy context only; no A2 result is real-world embodied validation. |

#### 6.1 A2/A3/A4 no-collapse rule

A2 must remain the simple registered threshold baseline. If the evaluated feature is entropy, margin, variation ratio, conformal-set size, learned uncertainty, or a richer risk-coverage/selective-prediction policy, the result belongs to A3 unless the sources explicitly register it as a simple confidence threshold. If the evaluated mechanism is longer-window, multi-window, majority voting, probability averaging, confidence-weighted averaging, model-family aggregation, or ordinary ensemble disagreement, the result belongs to A4.

#### 6.2 Relationship to C0–C4 capability tiers

| Capability tier | A2 relationship | Claim maturity |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Directly supports the public-data reliability baseline by testing simple threshold sufficiency | Can support bounded offline/proxy threshold-baseline claims if split, registry, metric, and matched-key gates pass |
| C1 | Downstream IHARQ/readiness context | A2 alone does not mature C1; it is a comparator for later IHARQ evidence |
| C2 | Downstream adaptive-readiness context | A2 may be a baseline or feature context but does not prove adaptive policy readiness |
| C3 | Downstream simulation/stress context | A2 may be stress-tested later; clean A2 is not stress robustness proof |
| C4 | Downstream embodiment-proxy context | A2 does not validate embodiment, actuation, FES, or real-world control |

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

#### 9.1 A2 baseline definition

An A2 result is valid only when a thresholded accept/reject operating point is selected by a declared rule on a legal selection split and recorded in `ThresholdRegistryRecord`. Thresholded evaluation must then be performed on the declared evaluation/test split without tuning on that split. The threshold may be based on raw decoder confidence or calibrated confidence where source-supported; richer uncertainty features belong to A3 unless explicitly bounded as non-A2 context.

#### 9.2 Comparator matrix

| Comparator | Required comparison | Match requirement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / accept-all reference | A2 thresholded outputs versus A0 no-threshold outputs | Same dataset, split, subject/session, trial/window or aggregation unit, preprocessing, label map, model, seed, score schema, label budget, metric dictionary, and source prediction IDs | Shows value/cost of simple rejection relative to raw accept-all baseline; not a safety proof |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Calibrated-confidence threshold versus calibrated no-threshold reliability context | Same A1 `CalibrationRecord`, calibration split legality, model, budget, score schema, and metric dictionary | Shows whether thresholding calibrated confidence adds useful baseline behavior beyond calibration visibility |
| Internal A2 threshold variants | Raw-confidence threshold versus calibrated-confidence threshold, or matched coverage/cost operating points where source-supported | Same threshold-selection protocol, source records, metric dictionary, and selected-on split logic | Variant comparison only; no new top-level ablation ID unless later confirmed |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | A2 simple confidence threshold versus A3 uncertainty/selective baselines | Matched coverage/cost and source records; A3 must have legal uncertainty/selection features | Keeps simple thresholding separate from richer uncertainty/selective prediction |
| A4 ordinary controls | A2 threshold rejection versus ordinary longer-window, multi-window, voting/averaging, or ensemble controls | Matched source windows/trials, model family, delay/aggregation burden, split, metrics, and source IDs | Ensures simple thresholding is not confused with ordinary aggregation controls |
| A5+ IHARQ/readiness/policy branches | Later mechanisms compared against A2 where applicable | Matched coverage, wrong-accept cost, evidence budget, threshold registry ID, source records, and metric dictionary | Later claims must be downgraded if A2 is sufficient under matched conditions |

#### 9.3 Baseline-sufficiency rule

If A2 achieves the same or better retained-error, high-confidence-wrong, coverage/cost, or declared wrong-accept proxy behavior as a later mechanism under matched conditions, the result must be preserved as threshold sufficiency. Later claims may still discuss traceability, reasoning, fallback behavior, or downstream utility where source-supported, but they must not claim unqualified reliability improvement over A2.

---

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

#### 10.1 Required key families

| Key family | Required A2 keys | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Source identity | `dataset_id`, source dataset/version, `subject_id`, `session_id` where available, `trial_id`, `window_id`, aggregation unit | Prevents comparing different data slices or aggregation levels |
| Split and leakage identity | `split_id`, `split_role`, threshold-selection split ID, calibration split ID where used, evaluation/test split ID, nested-CV fold ID where used, leakage status | Prevents test-tuned thresholds and split leakage |
| Preprocessing and label identity | preprocessing ID/version, windowing ID, label map/version, class order | Prevents incompatible score/label comparisons |
| Model and score identity | `model_id`, `decoder_id`, model family, checkpoint/registry reference, score type, probability/logit availability, seed, config hash | Ensures thresholding uses comparable score distributions |
| Calibration identity | `calibration_id`, calibration method/scope, calibration split ID, calibration budget where calibrated thresholding is used | Separates raw-confidence and calibrated-confidence threshold variants |
| Threshold identity | `threshold_registry_id`, threshold type, feature, selected value/rule, selected-on split, selection rule, target constraint, applicable model IDs, version, allowed consumers, rationale/fairness note | Makes threshold use registered, reproducible, and auditable |
| Comparison identity | source and target ablation IDs, matched comparison key, coverage/cost group, metric dictionary entry ID, source record IDs, diagnostic-only status | Makes comparative A2 claims fair and traceable |
| Claim/export identity | limitation tags, `NegativeResultNote` ID where needed, dashboard export manifest ID, claim-evidence pointer | Connects A2 evidence to Layer 10 exports and Layer 0 claim review |

#### 10.2 Matchability status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning | Allowed claim state |
|---|---|---|
| `fully_matched` | All required source, split, model, calibration/threshold, metric, and limitation keys are present | Thesis-ready bounded A2 comparison may be made after Layer 0 review |
| `partially_matched` | Some keys are missing but comparison remains interpretable as a diagnostic | Diagnostic-only; no unqualified improvement/sufficiency claim |
| `unmatched_diagnostic` | Source or operating-point keys are materially inconsistent | Diagnostic visualization or failure analysis only |
| `invalid` | Threshold selected on test data, leakage detected, metric undefined, or source lineage absent | Blocked; must be repaired and rerun |
| `not_applicable` | Key is genuinely not applicable, with explicit reason | May proceed only if the reason is recorded in the handoff/manifest |

#### 10.3 A2 comparison pass/fail rule

A2-to-A0/A1/A3/A4/A5+ comparisons pass only when threshold registry lineage, split legality, source record lineage, matched coverage/cost keys, and metric dictionary entries are complete. If any required key is missing, the comparison may remain visible in Layer 10 as diagnostic evidence with warnings but must not support thesis-ready claims.

### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

#### 11.1 Source-supported A2 metric families

| Metric family | A2 use | Required source records | Metric dictionary status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coverage | Fraction/scope of outputs retained after thresholding | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, threshold registry ID, source prediction IDs | Required; exact definition/aggregation must be dictionary-confirmed |
| Rejection rate | Fraction/scope of outputs rejected by thresholding | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, threshold registry ID | Required; exact denominator and aggregation unit must be dictionary-confirmed |
| Retained accuracy | Accuracy on retained/accepted outputs | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, evaluation labels protected as evaluation-only | Required; must include coverage context to avoid misleading high accuracy |
| Retained error rate | Error rate on retained/accepted outputs | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, source labels as evaluation-only | Required; directionality and aggregation must be fixed |
| Risk / retained risk | Error/risk behavior under retained coverage | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, metric dictionary entry | Required; exact risk definition requires confirmation |
| High-confidence wrong rate | Wrong predictions above declared confidence threshold or operating point | `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, threshold registry ID | Required for thesis-facing high-confidence-error claims; diagnostic-only if threshold source or correctness handling is incomplete |
| Matched coverage / matched cost | Fair comparison group for A0/A1/A2/A3/A5+ | `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, `MatchedComparisonReport` | Required for comparative claims |
| Wrong-accept proxy cost | Declared proxy cost for accepted wrong outputs where defined | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, metric dictionary, cost/coverage config | Requires confirmation; do not call clinical safety metric |
| Threshold-selection lineage/completeness | Audit status of selected-on split, selection rule, target constraint, version, and leakage status | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `SplitIntegrityReport` | Required as governance metric/status, not a performance metric |
| Diagnostic-only rate / warning count | Completeness and downgrade visibility | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, `LeakageWarningRecord`, export manifest | Required for Layer 10/Layer 0 audit surfaces where implemented |

#### 11.2 Metrics explicitly not A2 metrics

| Metric or metric family | A2 status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration-only ECE/Brier/NLL deltas | `A1_context_only` | A2 may use calibrated confidence but does not own calibration visibility. |
| Entropy/margin/conformal-set-size risk-coverage metrics | `A3_context_only` | These are uncertainty/selective-prediction baselines, not simple confidence-thresholding. |
| Ensemble disagreement, delay burden from voting/averaging, multi-window aggregation metrics | `A4_context_only` | Ordinary combination controls belong to A4. |
| IHARQ action-cost, fallback, unsafe-event, reason-code distribution metrics | `A5_plus_context_only` | A2 has no IHARQ decision vocabulary. |
| Reward, regret, policy-update, episode, transition, closed-loop metrics | `not_applicable_for_A2` | Policy/simulation branches are downstream. |
| Stress robustness drop or embodiment endpoint error | `future_work_or_downstream_context_only` | A12/A13 metrics, not clean A2. |
| Clinical safety, medical-device readiness, rehabilitation efficacy, real patient outcome, real stimulation control metrics | `forbidden` | Outside Stretch C claim boundary. |

#### 11.3 Metric-dictionary rule

No A2 metric is thesis-ready unless the metric dictionary specifies the metric name, definition, directionality, unit/denominator, aggregation unit, required records, split role, matched-comparison requirement, diagnostic-only rule, and claim boundary. If the exact definition is useful but not yet fixed, the metric remains `requires_confirmation: true` and any associated claim is diagnostic-only.

---

### 12. Split, Leakage, Threshold, Calibration, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint family | A2 rule | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Split separation | Thresholds must be selected only on legal validation/selection or nested-CV splits and evaluated on held-out evaluation/test splits | Test-tuned threshold claims are invalid or diagnostic-only |
| Threshold registry | Every threshold used in A2 or downstream comparisons must have a `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Unregistered threshold comparisons are blocked |
| Raw prediction immutability | A2 must not overwrite `PredictionRecord` probabilities, logits, class order, or model registry fields | Source-lineage violation; affected results invalid |
| Calibration boundary | Calibrated-confidence thresholds require valid A1 `CalibrationRecord` lineage; A2 does not produce calibration evidence | Calibrated-threshold variant diagnostic-only or omitted |
| A2/A3 boundary | Entropy, margin, uncertainty-feature selection, and rich risk-coverage policies must be routed to A3 unless explicitly reported as non-A2 context | Identity conflict; comparison downgraded or reclassified |
| A2/A4 boundary | Voting, averaging, longer-window, multi-window, and ordinary ensemble controls must remain A4 | Identity conflict; ordinary-control comparison downgraded or reclassified |
| Evaluation-only labels | True labels and correctness fields may be used for evaluation/threshold selection only where split roles allow; they must not become decision-time features | Leakage or decision-time oracle; claims blocked |
| Policy/simulation boundary | A2 thresholds cannot be retuned by downstream Phase 6 evidence-quality/adaptive-policy, Phase 7 deferral, Phase 8 simulation, Phase 10 bandit, or Phase 11 RL outcomes for final comparisons | Downstream contamination; threshold claim blocked |
| Stress boundary | Clean A2 threshold evidence remains separate from A12 controlled stress robustness | Stress-conditioned claims require later A12 section |
| Embodiment boundary | A2 outputs are not real actuation, stimulation, or endpoint-control evidence | Embodiment or BCI-FES claims forbidden |
| Dashboard boundary | Layer 10 may display and export A2 evidence but must not tune thresholds, alter groups, remove warnings, or create primary evidence | Dashboard result becomes non-thesis-ready |

---

### 13. Local Sub-Ablation Policy for A2

No new top-level ablation ID is introduced. The only official global identifier generated here is `A2`. Local A2 variants may be used only as child labels or table rows if later confirmed by the registry/protocol run matrix. In v0.1, the following are candidate local variants rather than mandatory official sub-ablations:

| Candidate local variant | Status | Requires confirmation? | Allowed use |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `A2.raw_confidence_threshold` | `source_supported_context` | Yes for exact label and run matrix | Threshold raw decoder confidence/top probability using legal threshold registry |
| `A2.calibrated_confidence_threshold` | `source_supported_context` | Yes for exact label and run matrix | Threshold calibrated confidence/probability where A1 `CalibrationRecord` lineage exists |
| `A2.matched_coverage_operating_point` | `source_supported_context` | Yes for exact target constraint | Select registered threshold to match a declared coverage level for fair comparison |
| `A2.matched_cost_operating_point` | `source_supported_context` | Yes for exact cost definition | Select registered threshold to match declared wrong-accept/proxy cost where metric dictionary supports it |
| `A2.threshold_selection_rule_comparison` | `inferred_candidate` | Yes | Compare threshold-selection rules only if source records, selection splits, and metric definitions are complete |

These local labels must not be treated as official A14-style additions. If a later artifact uses numeric labels such as `A2.1` or `A2.2`, the mapping to the candidate local variant, source support, and confirmation status must be recorded in the protocol handoff before thesis use.

---

### 14. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

#### 14.1 Required Layer 10 outputs for A2

| Layer 10 output | Required source lineage | Warning/downgrade behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Threshold audit panel / threshold registry view | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, selected-on split, selection rule, target constraint, leakage status, allowed consumers, version | Show warning if threshold is unregistered, test-selected, incompatible with model, or missing leakage status |
| Retained-coverage / retained-accuracy view | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, threshold registry ID, metric dictionary entry IDs, source prediction/calibration IDs | Mark diagnostic-only if coverage denominator, retained metric, or source lineage is incomplete |
| Matched operating-point table | `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, matched comparison keys, coverage/cost group, source records | Mark unmatched rows and block comparative claims if keys are incomplete |
| A0/A1/A2 comparison table | A0 `PredictionRecord`/`BaselineMetricRecord`, A1 `CalibrationRecord` where applicable, A2 threshold records, metric dictionary | Show no-threshold versus thresholded behavior without hiding coverage loss |
| High-confidence wrong / accepted-wrong warning view | `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, evaluation-only correctness lineage | Warning-only or diagnostic-only; never a decision-time oracle |
| Negative-result and sufficiency note display | `NegativeResultNote`, diagnostic flags, source records | Preserve threshold sufficiency or failure rather than suppressing it |
| Reliability card source bundle | Layer 3 record IDs, threshold IDs, split integrity, warnings, limitations | Rendered card is derived; source records remain primary evidence |
| Export manifest and figure/table lineage manifest | source paths, output paths, hashes, metric IDs, config IDs, run IDs, threshold IDs, limitation tags | Missing manifest downgrades dashboard/table/figure to non-thesis-ready |
| Claim-evidence export | claim IDs, source record IDs, metric IDs, threshold registry IDs, diagnostic-only status, limitation labels | Must expose Layer 0 boundaries and unresolved claim-evidence alias/schema issues |

#### 14.2 Layer 10 prohibitions for A2

Layer 10 must not tune thresholds, choose threshold values, repair split leakage, mutate source records, drop failed threshold variants, hide coverage loss, hide high-confidence wrong cases, recompute hidden metrics from anonymous arrays, convert diagnostic-only rows into thesis-ready claims, or remove Layer 0 limitation warnings.

#### 14.3 Layer 10 not-applicable and downstream-only outputs

| Output family | A2 status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| A3 broad risk-coverage/uncertainty dashboard | `downstream_or_nearby_context_only` | A3 is the evaluation context for uncertainty/selective-prediction feature comparisons. |
| A4 ordinary-control ensemble card | `nearby_context_only` | A4 is the evaluation context for ordinary longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble controls. |
| IHARQ decision-flow card | `downstream_context_only` | Later IHARQ sections evaluate IHARQ decision evidence produced by the relevant layers/phases. |
| Policy-update/reward dashboard | `not_applicable` | A2 has no policy updates or rewards. |
| Stress/embodiment dashboard outputs | `future_work_or_downstream_context_only` | A12/A13 own stress and embodiment evidence. |

---

### 15. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

#### 15.1 Allowed bounded A2 claim classes

A2 may support only bounded claims such as:

- simple registered confidence-threshold baselines were evaluated under declared public EEG splits;
- threshold values/rules were registered with selection split, target constraint, version, leakage status, and allowed consumers;
- thresholding changed retained coverage, rejection rate, retained accuracy/error, risk, or high-confidence-wrong behavior under matched offline/proxy conditions;
- a simple threshold was sufficient, insufficient, unstable, or diagnostic-only under declared matched coverage/cost rules;
- later IHARQ/adaptive mechanisms must be compared against A2 where A2 threshold evidence is valid and matched.

#### 15.2 Forbidden or blocked claim classes

A2 must not claim or imply:

| Forbidden claim | Reason |
|---|---|
| A2 threshold is a clinical safety threshold | Public EEG proxy thresholding is not clinical safety validation |
| A2 proves patient safety or medical-device readiness | The project does not validate a medical device or patient outcome |
| A2 validates real-time deployment safety | Threshold evidence is offline/proxy and split-governed |
| A2 proves rehabilitation efficacy or BCI-FES control success | No real patient rehabilitation or real stimulation control is tested |
| A2 is equivalent to IHARQ evidence verification | A2 is simple thresholding; IHARQ requires later evidence-verification records |
| A2 is equivalent to A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | A3 is the evaluation context for richer uncertainty/selective baselines |
| Dashboard threshold plots are primary evidence | Layer 10 outputs are derived/read-only reporting artifacts |
| High-confidence wrong cases are decision-time features | Correctness labels are evaluation-only and must not leak downstream |

#### 15.3 Required limitation labels

A2 outputs, tables, cards, and final claims must carry relevant labels including:

`public_eeg_only`, `offline_proxy_threshold_baseline`, `registered_operating_point_only`, `not_safety_threshold`, `evaluation_only`, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, `not_medical_device_readiness`, `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`, `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`, `not_real_deployment_readiness`, `threshold_registry_required`, `split_safe_threshold_selection_required`, `matched_keys_required`, `metric_dictionary_required`, `dashboard_derived_only`, `diagnostic_only_when_unmatched`, and `negative_results_visible`.

---

### 16. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

| Result pattern | Required interpretation | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A2 improves retained-error or high-confidence-wrong behavior but sharply reduces coverage | Thresholding may be useful as a baseline but has rejection/coverage burden | Later claims must compare against coverage/cost, not retained accuracy alone |
| A2 performs similarly to or better than A5+ under matched coverage/cost | Simple threshold sufficiency is a valid negative/sufficiency result | Later superiority claims downgraded or narrowed |
| A2 fails to improve retained-error or high-confidence-wrong behavior | Thresholding alone may be insufficient under the declared protocol | Motivates A3/A5+ but does not prove their success |
| A2 results differ by subject/session/model family/budget | Threshold behavior is heterogeneous | Require group-wise limitation or diagnostic-only treatment if subgroup metrics are incomplete |
| Threshold selection is unstable under sparse calibration/selection data | Operating point may be unreliable | Mark limitation; exact stability metrics require dictionary confirmation |
| A2 cannot be evaluated due to missing scores or threshold registry | Absence of evidence is not evidence of threshold failure | A2 claim blocked; downstream claims must state comparator missingness |
| A2 negative result conflicts with later desired narrative | Preserve the negative result | Do not hide, relabel, or omit threshold sufficiency/failure |

---

### 17. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

| Trigger | Affected A2 content | Required downgrade/action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, or `LabelMapRecord` lineage | All A2 threshold comparisons using affected records | Diagnostic-only or invalid; repair source lineage before final claim |
| Missing or invalid `PredictionRecord` score/probability fields, score type, or class order | Threshold computation and comparison | Block thesis-ready A2; record missingness |
| Missing `ModelRegistryRecord` or config/seed lineage | Model-family threshold comparison | Diagnostic-only |
| Threshold selected on final test/evaluation labels | Threshold validity | Invalid; rerun with legal selection split |
| Missing `ThresholdRegistryRecord` for a used threshold | Threshold claim and downstream consumers | Block or diagnostic-only; register threshold before final claim |
| Threshold registry lacks selected-on split, selection rule, target constraint, leakage status, or version | Threshold legality | Diagnostic-only until completed |
| Calibrated-confidence threshold lacks valid A1 `CalibrationRecord` | Calibrated-threshold variant | Omit or diagnostic-only; do not infer calibration lineage |
| A2 rows cannot be separated from A3 uncertainty/selective rows | A2 identity | Reclassify, split records, or downgrade as ambiguous |
| A2 rows are mixed with A4 voting/averaging/ensemble controls | A2/A4 identity | Reclassify or downgrade ordinary-control comparison |
| Missing `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` or matched coverage/cost keys | Comparative claims | Diagnostic-only; no A2 superiority/sufficiency claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Any A2 metric | Diagnostic-only until metric definition confirmed |
| Hidden failed/skipped threshold variants | Baseline sufficiency and negative-result reporting | Invalid or incomplete until failures are visible |
| High-confidence-wrong correctness used as decision-time feature | Leakage/claim safety | Block affected branch; record `LeakageWarningRecord` |
| Layer 10 export lacks source lineage or warning tags | Dashboard/table/figure | Not thesis-ready; regenerate export manifest |
| Layer 0 limitation tags or claim review absent | Final claim | Block final A2 claim |

---

### 19. Handoff to Later Protocol Sections

| Later section | A2 handoff requirement |
|---|---|
| A3 — Uncertainty and selective prediction | Preserve A2 as simple thresholding. A3 must declare which records/rows are uncertainty/selective and must not relabel A2 confidence thresholds as broad uncertainty evidence. |
| A4 — Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Keep ordinary controls separate from A2. Compare delay/aggregation burden and source-window identity explicitly where A4 uses longer windows or ensembles. |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Compare IHARQ evidence verification against A2 registered thresholds under matched coverage/cost and threshold registry lineage. Preserve A2 sufficiency as negative evidence. |
| A6–A9 | Treat A2 as a baseline/comparator or legal threshold context only; do not let learned estimators or policies retune A2 thresholds on final evaluation data. |
| A10–A11 | Use A2 only as simulation-bounded baseline context with frozen threshold registry; no real-world policy or safety claim. |
| A12 | Stress-test threshold evidence only under controlled stress protocol with clean-vs-stressed lineage and stress-only limitations. |
| A13 | Use A2 only as proxy/static-replay comparator where explicitly authorized; no real actuation or FES validation. |
| Metric-family section | Confirm exact A2 metric definitions, denominators, aggregation units, directionality, and diagnostic-only rules. |
| Matched-comparison rules | Add threshold registry ID, selected-on split, target constraint, coverage/cost group, and threshold variant identity as required keys. |
| Diagnostic-only downgrade rules | Include all A2 triggers from Section 17. |
| Layer 10 export/dashboard obligations | Define exact threshold view, retained-coverage table, threshold audit panel, export manifest, and card linkage without making dashboard output primary evidence. |
| Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries | Preserve `registered_operating_point_only` and `not_safety_threshold` limitations in final thesis wording. |

| A2 identity | Fixed as simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | None |
| Required records | Defined with source-supported/candidate statuses preserved | Exact schema paths and storage homes for some artifacts |
| Threshold variants | Candidate local variants listed without promoting new official IDs | Exact local labels, threshold grid/rules, and run matrix |
| Metrics | Metric families and dictionary requirements defined | Exact formulas, denominators, confidence intervals, statistical tests |
| Matched comparisons | Required key families defined | Final comparison IDs, table IDs, and route names |
| Layer 10 outputs | Required output types defined | Exact dashboard routes/card IDs/export filenames |
| Layer 0 boundaries | Allowed/forbidden claim classes defined | Final claim-evidence manifest/matrix schema resolution |
| Experimental execution | Evaluation requirements defined | Exact commands, seeds, run counts, dataset list, and final hyperparameter/threshold grids |

---

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A3 identity

A3 is the **uncertainty and selective-prediction** evaluation context. It evaluates whether uncertainty features and selective-prediction behavior explain or improve reliability-related offline/proxy behavior beyond raw decoder outputs, calibration visibility, and simple registered confidence thresholds.

A3 is source-supported through Layer 3 / Phase 3 outputs such as `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, risk-coverage and accuracy-coverage evidence, uncertainty summaries, and `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`. It may use calibrated probabilities, confidence, entropy, normalized entropy, margin, variation ratio, model disagreement where source-supported, conformal set size if explicitly supported, selective-accept flags, and uncertainty profiles. It must preserve label-free decision-time feature boundaries and keep evaluation-only correctness fields out of decision-time records.

A3 is not A2. A2 is the simple registered confidence-threshold baseline. A3 may include selective-prediction behavior and operating points, but it evaluates richer uncertainty-feature selection and selective-accept/reject behavior under risk-coverage or matched-coverage/cost rules. A3 is not A4: longer windows, multi-window voting, probability averaging, majority voting, and ordinary ensemble controls remain A4 controls even when they produce disagreement features for optional A3 analysis.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

A3 answers the following question:

> Given matched public-data records, fixed splits, preprocessing, label maps, model identities, seeds, label budgets, calibration lineage where applicable, threshold registry lineage where applicable, metric dictionary entries, and source-preserving Layer 3 records, do uncertainty features and selective-prediction baselines provide measurable, split-safe, claim-bounded reliability evidence beyond A0 raw decoder output, A1 calibration visibility, and A2 simple registered confidence-threshold rejection?

The scientific purpose is fairness and sufficiency analysis. A3 must determine whether later IHARQ, deferral, policy-learning, stress, or embodiment-proxy claims truly add value beyond uncertainty-aware rejection and selective prediction. If A3 already explains the benefit of a later mechanism under matched coverage or cost, that negative/sufficiency result must be preserved rather than hidden. If A3 fails, collapses coverage, leaks labels, or is unstable under low-calibration budgets, those failures become evidence for the need for stricter downstream evidence-verification or policy layers, not proof of safety or readiness.

#### 3.3 What A3 may and may not claim

| Claim class | A3 treatment |
|---|---|
| Uncertainty evidence from public EEG predictions can be measured and compared under fixed splits | Allowed when `UncertaintyRecord` lineage, metric definitions, and matched keys are complete |
| Selective prediction changes coverage, risk, retained accuracy/error, rejection burden, high-confidence-wrong behavior, or subject/class/session coverage | Allowed as offline/proxy evaluation when `SelectivePredictionRecord`, split legality, and metric dictionary entries exist |
| A3 is better than A0/A1/A2 under matched coverage or matched cost | Allowed only when all matched keys and metric definitions are complete; otherwise diagnostic-only |
| A3 is sufficient and later IHARQ/policy mechanisms add little under a declared protocol | Allowed as bounded negative/sufficiency interpretation, not as deployment or clinical safety |
| Uncertainty/selective prediction validates safe BCI-FES, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, rehabilitation efficacy, or real-time control | Forbidden |
| High-confidence-wrong or correctness-derived signals can be used as decision-time features | Forbidden unless an explicitly declared oracle/diagnostic analysis is isolated and marked non-final |

---

### 4. Relationship to Official Layers 0–10

| Layer | A3 relationship | A3 boundary |
|---:|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-safety and scope governance | Governs A3 claim boundaries, diagnostic-only downgrades, forbidden claims, and limitation labels | Layer 0 does not produce A3 empirical evidence or tune uncertainty features |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Produces immutable dataset, window, split, preprocessing, label-map, artifact-flag, dataset-card, protocol-card, validation, and manifest lineage required for A3 | A3 may not repair or reinterpret source split roles after the fact |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Produces `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, optional `EnsembleControlRecord`, failure/readiness records, and score fields consumed by Layer 3 | A3 may consume score/probability/logit fields, but it does not train decoders or mutate predictions |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Primary producing layer for A3 source evidence: `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, threshold/selective operating points, reliability audit, split integrity, and dashboard-readable metric sources | Layer 3 does not make final IHARQ actions, policy updates, simulation actions, stress generation, or embodiment claims |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Downstream consumer/comparator context; uses A3 uncertainty and selective baseline evidence to test whether IHARQ adds value beyond selective prediction | A3 is not IHARQ and cannot emit IHARQ decisions or reason-code action traces |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust monitoring | Optional downstream/diagnostic consumer of rolling uncertainty summaries where past-only temporal use is legal | A3 does not produce validated temporal trust or fatigue diagnosis |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive readiness policy layer | Downstream consumer of label-free uncertainty context and registered operating points; later policy comparisons must reference A3 IDs | A3 does not learn readiness policies, update policies, or produce rewards |
| Layer 7 — Simulated closed-loop readiness environment | Downstream simulation context only where later sections use A3 records as inputs | A3 has no episode, transition, reward, or closed-loop safety metric |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite stress generator | Downstream stress context only; A3 records may be replayed under stress later if source IDs and stress schedule IDs exist | A3 does not generate stress profiles or stress robustness claims |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Downstream embodiment-proxy context only; A3 evidence may be preserved as provenance/readiness input | A3 does not validate embodiment safety, endpoint control, real stimulation, or real assistive action |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility layer | Reads, validates, summarizes, warns, visualizes, exports, and packages A3 records and limitation tags | Layer 10 does not recompute hidden A3 evidence, tune thresholds, alter records, or remove warnings |

A3 sits in the Layer 3 trust-conversion layer. It converts prediction/calibration evidence into label-free uncertainty features and selective-prediction evidence that can be fairly compared to A0–A2 and later consumed by A5+ sections. The central layer boundary is that A3 makes uncertainty evidence auditable; it does not convert that evidence into clinical safety, deployment readiness, or real-time control readiness.

Phase 3 may begin serious A3 evidence production only after Phase 2 prediction/model records are sufficient for calibration and uncertainty extraction. Missing score fields, invalid class order, missing split roles, illegal preprocessing fitting, missing source IDs, or incomplete metric dictionary entries downgrade affected A3 comparisons to diagnostic-only or block them from thesis-ready claims.

|---:|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder / accept-all raw reference | Required upstream comparator: A3 must show whether uncertainty/selective prediction improves or changes behavior relative to raw decoder output | A0 remains Layer 2 / Phase 2 raw evidence; A3 must not rewrite raw predictions |

| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Current target section | A3 is evaluation-use metadata, not a producing layer or artifact owner |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Nearby ordinary-control comparator where compatible; ensemble disagreement may be an optional uncertainty feature only if source-supported and labeled | A4 controls remain A4 and must not be renamed A3 |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Downstream comparator/consumer; A5 must prove added value beyond A3 where matched | A3 has no IHARQ actions, reason codes, fallback, combine, unsafe, or request-evidence behavior |
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Downstream consumer/context where uncertainty features may help evidence-quality estimation | A3 does not train or validate evidence-quality estimators |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk temporal trust | Downstream temporal-trust context | A3 does not validate temporal trust or physiological/fatigue states |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Downstream deferral comparator/context | A3 selective prediction may be a baseline, but learned deferral policy evidence is separate |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Downstream supervised adaptive readiness context | A3 does not learn adaptive readiness policies |
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Downstream simulation-bounded policy context | A3 does not emit bandit actions/rewards/regret |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream simulation-bounded policy context | A3 does not emit RL policy/transition/reward evidence |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests | Downstream controlled stress robustness context | A3 does not own stress profiles or stress robustness claims |
| A13 | Layer 9 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Downstream embodiment-proxy context | A3 does not validate embodiment, real stimulation, endpoint control, or patient outcomes |

A3’s most important local relationship is the A1–A3 continuum inside Layer 3. A1 asks whether calibration makes probability reliability visible. A2 asks whether a simple registered confidence threshold is a sufficient baseline. A3 asks whether uncertainty features and selective prediction provide stronger or more interpretable risk/coverage behavior than A0–A2 under matched conditions.
