### 3. Target Purpose and Scientific Question

A5 asks the following thesis-level scientific question:

> Under public-EEG, offline/proxy Stretch C constraints, does transparent rule-based IHARQ evidence verification improve claim-safe readiness evidence over matched raw, calibrated, threshold, uncertainty/selective-prediction, and ordinary aggregation/ensemble baselines, while preserving source lineage, metric definitions, negative results, diagnostic-only downgrades, and non-clinical claim boundaries?

A5 is scientifically meaningful only if it evaluates the full decision behavior, not merely final accuracy. The section must therefore track:

| A5 behavior family | Scientific reason to measure it | Claim-safe interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` | Whether IHARQ-lite accepts current evidence and whether accepted decisions are reliable | Computational accepted-decision evidence only; not real action validation |
| `wait` | Whether the rule engine delays without consuming a new evidence item | Delay/evidence-burden evidence only; not real-time deployment safety |
| `request_evidence` | Whether additional evidence is requested under declared budgets | Proxy evidence-request behavior only; not real acquisition guarantee |
| `combine_evidence` | Whether several allowed evidence items are combined rather than blindly accepted | Rule-based combination evidence only; ordinary A4 aggregation remains a separate comparator |
| `fallback` | Whether conservative fallback route is selected when evidence is weak or unavailable | Proxy/conservative routing evidence only; not real patient safety |
| `uncertain` | Whether evidence is explicitly undecidable | Diagnostic/proxy uncertainty action only; downstream mappings must not overwrite the stored token |
| `unsafe` | Whether an action is blocked under severe computational/proxy conditions | Computational unsafe/proxy warning only; not clinical unsafe-state detection |

A5 cannot be credited for learned evidence-quality estimation, RegimeRisk temporal trust, learning-to-defer, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, contextual bandit, reinforcement learning, StressForge stress robustness, or Layer 9 embodiment effects unless the later source-supported A6–A13 sections add those contexts under matched lineage and explicit limitation tags.

---

### 4. Relationship to Layers 0–10

| Layer | A5 relationship | Required boundary |
|---:|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-safety and scope governance | Reviews A5 limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, forbidden claims, negative-result notes, and claim-evidence entries | Layer 0 does not produce empirical IHARQ evidence |
| Layer 1 — Public-data and protocol anchor | Provides dataset/window/split/label/artifact lineage inherited by A5 through upstream records | Layer 1 clean records must not be overwritten by A5 |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and baseline measurement spine | Provides `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, baseline/control metrics, subject/model identity, failure-case evidence, and A0/A4 comparator context | A5 consumes these records; it does not own decoder evidence |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, uncertainty, and selective prediction | Provides `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, and diagnostic high-confidence-wrong evidence | Decision-time A5 may use only legal label-free evidence; evaluation-only correctness tables cannot tune rules |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Produces the source records used by A5: `IHARQDecisionRecord`, rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, `UnsafeEventRecord`, `IHARQAblationRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, and Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Layer 4 is the producer; A5 is the evaluation-use identifier |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust monitoring | Downstream/optional context; A5 core is regime-unaware unless Phase 5 records exist | No A7/regime-aware claim in A5 core |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive readiness policy layer | Downstream consumer of A5 traces and rule-derived context; may later produce learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants | A5 must preserve rule-derived versus learned variant tags and not claim learned policy behavior |
| Layer 7 — Simulated closed-loop readiness environment | Later simulation consumer of A5 action tokens and records | A5 core is offline/proxy; no simulation-policy or closed-loop claim unless later sections provide records |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite stress generator | Later stress context for A12 | A5 clean records must remain distinct from stress-conditioned copies |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Later embodiment proxy context for A13 | A5 does not validate real embodiment or muscle stimulation |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility layer | Renders A5 source records into dashboard views, reliability cards, warnings, exports, and reproducibility manifests | Layer 10 outputs are derived/read-only and cannot replace source Layer 4 records |

The A5 traceability chain is:

```text
Layer 1/2/3 source evidence
→ Phase 4 / Layer 4 rule-based evidence verification records
→ A5 matched evaluation use
→ metric dictionary + matched comparison + negative-result note + diagnostic-only status
→ Layer 10 card/view/export/reproducibility handoff
→ Layer 0 claim-safety and limitation review
→ bounded thesis claim or diagnostic-only result
```

---

### 5. Relationship to Phase 0–15

| Phase | Relationship to A5 | A5 consequence |
|---:|---|---|
| Phase 0 — Repository, configuration, and record schema | Establishes schemas, configs, validators, metric/claim/dashboard placeholders, action-token fixtures, manifests, and unresolved issue tracking | If inherited schema/config/validator lineage is missing, A5 rows cannot be thesis-ready |
| Phase 1 — Public-data ingestion and source schema | Provides public dataset, window, split, preprocessing, label-map, artifact, and claim-scope lineage | Missing source lineage blocks or downgrades A5 comparisons |
| Phase 2 — Baseline decoders | Produces prediction/model/baseline evidence for A0 and A4-related ordinary controls | A5 cannot compare fairly without matched prediction/model/control lineage |
| Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty | Produces calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, and matched operating-point evidence for A1–A3 and downstream A5 | A5 calibrated/uncertainty/threshold claims are blocked or degraded if Phase 3 records are missing or leaked |
| Phase 4 — IHARQ-lite evidence verification | Produces Layer 4 records, traces, local ablations, evaluation outcomes, matched reports, negative-result notes, and diagnostic-only flags used by A5 | Primary producing phase for A5 evidence |
| Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust | Consumes A5 histories and may later support A7/regime-aware IHARQ comparisons | A5 core remains `regime_aware=false` unless Phase 5 source records are available and matched |
| Phase 6 — Adaptive readiness policy | Consumes A5 contexts and may produce learned quality/policy records | A5 must not claim A6/A9 behavior |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | Later deferral comparison/routing context that may consume A5 traces or compare against A5 under matched cost/coverage rules | A5 does not produce `DeferralRecord` or learning-to-defer evidence |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | Later simulation consumer of A5 action tokens and records under frozen/replay rules | A5 alone is not closed-loop validation and does not produce `TransitionRecord`, reward traces, or simulation claims |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | Later stress-conditioned records and A12 evaluation context | A5 clean evidence must not be overwritten by stress variants and cannot claim stress robustness by itself |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | Later update-enabled policy | A5 produces no bandit updates |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | Later sequential policy learning | A5 produces no RL policy or reward trace |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | Later MyoSuite/static-replay embodiment-proxy context through Layer 9 records | A5 actions may be source context only; no real-control, real muscle-stimulation, or rehabilitation claim |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim/static replay or optional comparison | Later optional OpenSim/replay embodiment-proxy comparison where exported | A5 remains provenance/comparator context only; no real-control or clinical embodiment claim |
| Phase 14 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility | Renders and exports A5 source records and warnings | Dashboard outputs are derived, read-only, and lineage-bound |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | Integrates A5 evidence, negative results, diagnostic-only flags, and claim evidence under Layer 0/Layer 10 boundaries | Final A5 thesis claims require matched records, metric definitions, lineage, and limitations |

### 6. Relationship to A0–A13 and Nearby Ablations

| Ablation ID | Correct identity | A5 relationship |
|---:|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder / accept-all raw decoder reference where source-supported | Primary upstream accept-all/raw comparator |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder / calibration visibility | Comparator and input context when calibrated probabilities are used |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Required simpler threshold comparator; must remain separate from A3 |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Required uncertainty/selective-prediction comparator; must not be collapsed into A2 or A4 |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Required ordinary-control comparator; not IHARQ and not source of IHARQ action tokens |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Current target |
| A6 | IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator where source-supported | Downstream learned-quality extension; A5 supplies rule-derived baseline/context only |
| A7 | IHARQ plus RegimeRisk temporal trust where source-supported | Downstream regime-aware extension; A5 core remains regime-unaware unless Phase 5 records exist |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer / deferral comparison where source-supported | Downstream deferral comparison; A5 fallback/uncertain/request labels may serve as context, not `DeferralRecord` ownership |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ / adaptive readiness policy where source-supported | Downstream learned readiness policy; A5 is deterministic reference policy only |
| A10 | Contextual bandit where source-supported and simulation-bounded | Downstream simulation/update policy; not part of A5 core |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy where source-supported and simulation-bounded | Downstream sequential policy; not part of A5 core |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests / controlled stress robustness | Downstream stress evaluation; A5 clean source records may be replayed but not mutated |
| A13 | Layer 9 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo / simulated embodiment consequence | Downstream embodiment-proxy demo; A5 does not validate real embodiment |

A5 must not introduce `A14` or any other global ablation ID. Local A5 sub-ablation labels may be used only as local protocol labels and must carry source-supported or `inferred_candidate` status rather than being promoted into the global A0–A13 namespace.

#### 6.1 Relationship to C0–C4 capability tiers

C0–C4 are capability-tier and claim-maturity concepts, not implementation phases, layers, ablation IDs, record owners, or metric families. A5 is most directly tied to the C1 IHARQ reliability-control path, but A5 alone does not mature the full C1 tier because C1 also includes RegimeRisk temporal trust, fallback/unsafe governance, and reliability-card integration that depend on Phase 5 and later dashboard/final-integration evidence.

| Capability tier | A5 relationship | Claim-safety boundary |
|---|---|---|
| C0 — Public-data reliability spine | Required foundation through Phase 1–3 source, prediction, calibration, uncertainty, threshold, and matched-comparison records | A5 cannot compensate for missing C0 source/split/model lineage; incomplete C0 lineage downgrades A5 to diagnostic-only |
| C1 — IHARQ and RegimeRisk reliability control | A5 supports the IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence-verification portion of C1 | A5 does not by itself prove the RegimeRisk half of C1, real safety, real deployment, or clinical readiness |
| C2 — Adaptive policy layer | Downstream context only for A6/A8/A9 learning and deferral sections | A5 must not claim learned evidence-quality estimation, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, or learning-to-defer behavior |
| C3 — Bandit/RL simulation layer | Downstream simulation/update context only for A10/A11 | A5 produces no bandit/RL update trace, reward trace, or closed-loop policy-learning evidence |
| C4 — Embodiment and dashboard layer | Later dashboard/export/embodiment reporting may display or consume A5 records | Dashboard and embodiment outputs remain derived/proxy; A5 does not validate MyoSuite/OpenSim embodiment or real muscle stimulation |

### 8. Producer-Consumer Discipline

A5 may say that a record is **used by**, **evaluated in**, **compared under**, **dashboarded from**, or **summarized for** A5. It must not say that A5 itself produces canonical records. Correct producer statements are:

| Correct statement | Incorrect statement to avoid |
|---|---|
| Phase 4 / Layer 4 produces `IHARQDecisionRecord` outputs used by A5. | A5 produces `IHARQDecisionRecord`. |
| Phase 4 / Layer 4 exports `IHARQAblationRecord` and Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` rows for A5 evaluation. | The A5 identifier is treated as the owner of the ablation record schema. |
| Layer 10 renders A5 dashboard/card/export views from source records. | A5 dashboard metrics are primary evidence. |
| Layer 0 reviews A5 claim boundaries and downgrades. | Layer 0 produces A5 empirical results. |
| A5 compares against A4 ordinary controls under matched keys. | A4 ensemble voting is IHARQ or an A5 action. |

This discipline prevents three common errors: treating ablations as producers, treating dashboard outputs as evidence sources, and treating claim-governance artifacts as empirical results.

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

| Comparator | Required source support | Matched-comparison requirement | A5 interpretation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / accept-all reference | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, source split/window IDs, baseline metrics | Same dataset, subject/session where available, split, preprocessing, label map, model family/seed where applicable, trial/window identity where applicable | A5 value over raw acceptance is meaningful only if source records and keys match |
| A1 calibrated decoder | `CalibrationRecord`, calibrated probabilities, calibration IDs, calibration/test separation | Same calibrated output lineage and split/legal-use status | If calibrated decoder is sufficient, A5 must record that negative/baseline-sufficiency result |
| A2 simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord` or threshold rows, coverage/cost context | Same threshold registry, selected-on split, operating-point context, coverage and action/evidence cost keys | A5 must not claim improvement over thresholding unless threshold comparison is matched and leakage-safe |
| A3 uncertainty and selective prediction | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, threshold lineage | Same uncertainty features, selective operating point, split, coverage, cost, and source record keys | A5 cannot conflate uncertainty/selective prediction with simple thresholding or A4 ordinary controls |
| A4 longer-window / multi-window voting / averaging / ordinary ensemble controls | `EnsembleControlRecord` or ordinary-control summaries, aggregation rule, source window universe, delay/evidence cost, class-order mapping | Same source window universe, aggregation rule, delay/evidence accounting, score type, class order, and model-family compatibility | If ordinary controls match or beat A5, that is a valid negative result, not a failure to hide |
| Fallback-only baseline | Fallback route/config/source decision records where available | Same eligible decision cases and action/fallback cost accounting | Useful to test whether A5 only behaves like conservative fallback; source-supported or diagnostic-only |
| Local Layer 4 submodule ablations | `IHARQAblationRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, local configuration, matched source IDs | Same source records, fixed split, same thresholds and budgets unless the local ablation declares otherwise | Used only as local A5 children, not new global ablation IDs |
| Oracle/headroom diagnostic | Evaluation labels or future outcomes partitioned as evaluation-only | Must be clearly separate from decision-time features | Diagnostic/headroom only; cannot support deployable or clinical claims |

---

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

A5 comparison rows must carry a `matched_comparison_key` or equivalent key envelope sufficient to reproduce the comparison. At minimum, the A5 key family must include the following where available and applicable:

| Key family | Required fields or checks | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Public-data identity | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, source-record IDs, declared missingness for unavailable public metadata | Missing source identity or undeclared public-data missingness |
| Split and budget legality | `split_id`, `split_role`, `label_budget_id`, calibration/threshold/test separation, leakage warnings | Split leakage, threshold/calibration tuned on final test labels, or hidden future evidence |
| Preprocessing and labels | preprocessing ID/hash, label-map version, class order, artifact flags where available | Class-order mismatch, label-map mismatch, hidden preprocessing change |
| Model/decoder identity | `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `model_family`, `seed`, model config hash, score type | Missing model lineage, incompatible score type, hidden failed/skipped run |
| Calibration/threshold lineage | `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, selected-on split, allowed consumer, operating point | Missing/invalid threshold registry or calibration leakage |
| Uncertainty/selective lineage | `uncertainty_id`, selective prediction ID, coverage, rejection/cost denominator | Missing A3/A2 lineage for claimed comparison |
| Ordinary-control/A4 lineage | aggregation rule, aggregation unit, number of windows/members, voting/averaging/probability-average rule, delay/evidence burden note | Missing source window universe, hidden delay, or ordinary control not compatible with A5 cases |
| A5 decision lineage | `iharq_decision_id`, `iharq_trace_id`, canonical action token, reason code, rule path, config hash, action budget | Missing reason code, invalid token, missing trace, hidden rule/order change |
| Metric and claim lineage | `metric_dictionary_id`, `negative_result_note_id` where applicable, `diagnostic_only_flag`, claim-boundary tags, dashboard/export ID where rendered | Missing metric definition, hidden negative result, or unsupported claim tag |

If a key is missing because the public dataset does not provide the underlying identifier, the row must carry declared missingness. Undeclared missingness is not allowed to become a silent match.

---

### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

A5 metrics are v0.1 protocol requirements, not final v1.0 formulas. Every thesis-facing metric must have a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or be marked diagnostic-only / requires-confirmation. Exact denominators, aggregation modes, statistical tests, and table/figure numbering remain deferred unless a supplied source fixes them.

| Metric family | Example A5 use | Source support status | Metric dictionary requirement | Claim-safety limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accepted-decision accuracy / reliability where applicable | Reliability of decisions with `accept` action | Source-supported as evaluation metric family | Required for exact denominator and aggregation mode | Evaluation-only; not real action correctness |
| Wrong-accept rate / unsafe-accept proxy | Rate of accepted decisions later found wrong in evaluation partition | Source-supported | Required, including denominator and match keys | Proxy wrong-accept only; not clinical unsafe event |
| Coverage / accepted fraction | How often A5 accepts versus abstains, waits, requests, falls back, uncertain, or unsafe | Source-supported | Required | Coverage collapse must be reported as negative/diagnostic evidence |
| Request rate / evidence-request burden | Frequency and cost of `request_evidence` | Source-supported | Required | Proxy evidence burden; not real acquisition latency |
| Combine rate and combine success/failure | Whether `combine_evidence` helps beyond ordinary A4 aggregation | Source-supported when combination active | Required | Must not hide contradictory windows or rebrand A4 aggregation |
| Fallback rate / fallback burden | Conservative fallback frequency, cost, and evaluation result | Source-supported when fallback active | Required | Proxy fallback only; not real patient-safety fallback |
| Unsafe / blocked-action proxy rate | Frequency of `unsafe` token and associated warning fields | Source-supported when unsafe behavior active | Required | Computational/proxy warning only; not clinical safety detection |
| Uncertain rate | Frequency of explicit undecidable evidence | Source-supported | Required | Must not be mapped to executable command without declared downstream adapter |
| Action cost / delay / evidence cost | Cost of waiting, requesting, combining, fallback, or unsafe blocking | Source-supported at family level; exact cost model requires confirmation | Required, with exact units/denominators deferred | No real-time deployment claim |
| Reason-code distribution | Which rule paths and reasons drive decisions | Source-supported | Required for dashboard/thesis summaries | Explanation trace only; not causal clinical explanation |
| Trace completeness / source-lineage completeness | Whether every A5 row has source IDs, rule path, metrics, negative notes, and limitations | Source-supported | Required | Missing trace downgrades thesis readiness |
| Matched delta against A0–A4 | Improvement, degradation, or equivalence under matched keys | Source-supported at protocol level | Required for exact delta formula/statistical test | Negative/null deltas must remain visible |
| High-confidence-wrong diagnostic relation | Post-decision relation to high-confidence wrong cases | Diagnostic-only source-supported from Phase 3 | Required if reported | Evaluation-only; forbidden as decision-time tuning input |
| Feature-completeness / degraded-evidence frequency | Missing or degraded calibration, uncertainty, window, channel, or agreement helper evidence | Source-supported | Required if reported | Missing helper evidence narrows claims |

Forbidden metric classes remain blocked: no clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle-stimulation control, real-time deployment safety, clinical fatigue diagnosis, real physiological stress validation, real patient outcome improvement, or validated therapeutic effectiveness metric may be introduced.

---

### 12. Split, Leakage, Threshold, and Decision-Time Constraints

A5 decision-time logic may use only legal evidence available at the decision point:

```text
saved prediction outputs
→ calibrated probabilities where legal
→ label-free uncertainty features
→ threshold registry entries selected on legal splits
→ source/window metadata
→ past or otherwise permitted nearby-window history
→ artifact/channel flags where available
→ model-family agreement features where available
→ explicitly available RegimeRisk context only in later regime-aware contexts
```

A5 must not use:

```text
true labels as decision-time features
future correctness
future rewards
future simulation outcomes
future windows not permitted by replay configuration
final test-tuned thresholds
hidden dashboard-derived metrics
post-hoc high-confidence-wrong labels for ordinary decisions
```

| Constraint | A5 requirement | Failure response |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration separation | Calibration records must identify legal calibration split and method; test labels cannot tune calibration | Block calibrated claim or diagnostic-only |
| Threshold legality | Threshold registry must identify feature, selected value/rule, selected-on split, applicable consumers, and leakage status | Block threshold-dependent A5 rule/comparison if invalid |
| Evaluation-only partition | True labels and outcome correctness are used only after decision logging | Reject run or mark oracle/headroom diagnostic only |
| Future-window control | Request/combine/stability logic must not silently use windows unavailable at the decision point | Diagnostic-only or block combine/stability claims |
| Action-token integrity | Stored action must be one of canonical Layer 4 tokens | Invalid record; no silent rewrite |
| `combine` alias handling | Stored action is `combine_evidence`; `combine` may appear only as mapped display/adapter alias if supported | Alias violation; repair by versioned rerun or mark invalid/diagnostic |
| Rule tuning | Rule thresholds and budgets must be declared before final evaluation | Hidden test tuning blocks thesis-ready claim |
| Failed/skipped runs | Failures, unsupported models, and skipped outputs must be visible | Hidden failures block claim integration |

---

### 13. A5 Decision Vocabulary, Reason Codes, and Degraded Modes

The canonical Layer 4 stored action tokens required for A5 are:

```text
accept
wait
request_evidence
combine_evidence
fallback
uncertain
unsafe
```

Human-readable dashboard labels may display the actions in natural language, but stored records must preserve the canonical token. Downstream policy/simulation labels such as `no_action` or `defer` are not Layer 4 stored tokens and must not be inserted into `IHARQDecisionRecord.action`.

Every A5 decision row requires:

| Required field family | Minimum A5 expectation |
|---|---|
| Decision identity | `iharq_decision_id`, `run_id`, `phase_id=Phase 4`, `global_ablation_id=A5`, optional local sub-ablation ID |
| Source lineage | Source record IDs for prediction, calibration where used, uncertainty where used, threshold registry where used, window/source records, and helper views where used |
| Action and reason | Canonical action token, reason code, reason text or mapped label, rule path, action cost |
| Evidence features | Confidence, entropy, margin, calibrated probability where used, stability/agreement/channel/signal-quality features where available |
| Degraded mode | Missing-calibration, missing-window-history, missing-channel, missing-model-agreement, missing-artifact-flag, missing-RegimeRisk, invalid-vector, or ID-mismatch status where applicable |
| Evaluation linkage | matched comparison key, metric dictionary ID, diagnostic-only flag, negative-result note ID where applicable |
| Claim/export linkage | claim-boundary tags, dashboard/export ID where rendered, validation status, config hash, seed, schema version |

A5 must use explicit degraded modes rather than silent assumptions:

| Missing/degraded input | Required A5 behavior |
|---|---|
| Missing calibrated probabilities | Use declared uncalibrated fallback only if configured; otherwise block calibrated A5 claims |
| Missing window history | Disable stability/combine logic and record degraded-evidence reason code |
| Missing channel-subset output | Disable channel-subset checks and block strong spatial-robustness claims |
| Missing model-family alternatives | Run single-model IHARQ if configured and mark agreement unavailable |
| Missing artifact flags | Treat signal quality as unknown rather than clean |
| Missing RegimeRisk | Set `regime_aware=false`; no A7/regime-aware A5 claim |
| Invalid probability vector or mismatched IDs | Block acceptance and record validation error |
| Missing fallback/unsafe logs for active behavior | Block fallback/unsafe-specific claims |

---

### 14. Local Sub-Ablation Policy for A5

A5 may include local sub-ablations only to test source-supported Layer 4 components. These labels are local children of A5 and do not create new global ablation IDs.

| Local label candidate | Variant meaning | Source support | Required status handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A5.local.confidence_only` | Confidence-only IHARQ-like rule path | Source-supported comparator family | Local label exact naming requires confirmation if numeric A5.x labels are later used |
| `A5.local.entropy_only` | Entropy-only rejection / rule path | Source-supported comparator family | Metric dictionary and matched keys required |
| `A5.local.margin_only` | Margin-only rule path | Source-supported comparator family | Metric dictionary and matched keys required |
| `A5.local.no_stability` | Removes window-stability checker | Source-supported where stability helper exists | Diagnostic-only if `WindowHistoryRecord` unavailable |
| `A5.local.no_combination` | Disables `combine_evidence` behavior | Source-supported where combination active | No combine claim if combination record missing |
| `A5.local.no_fallback` | Removes fallback router | Source-supported where fallback behavior active | Must not imply real safety fallback |
| `A5.local.no_unsafe` | Removes unsafe-state monitor | Source-supported where unsafe monitor active | Proxy unsafe only; not clinical safety |
| `A5.local.fallback_only` | Tests conservative fallback-only logic | Source-supported as baseline family | Must report coverage/cost collapse if present |
| `A5.local.no_channel_subset` | Disables channel-subset checker | Inferred candidate from Layer 4 module structure | Requires confirmation of exact helper-view schema |
| `A5.local.no_model_agreement` | Disables model-family agreement checker | Inferred candidate from Layer 4 module structure | Requires confirmation where model-family alternatives exist |
| `A5.local.regime_unaware` | Marks core A5 without Phase 5 temporal trust | Source-supported as baseline/context for later A7 | A7 comparison deferred until Phase 5 records exist |

The protocol may later convert these local labels into numeric `A5.1`, `A5.2`, etc. only if a supplied source or user instruction fixes the exact local numbering. Until then, exact local numbering is `requires_confirmation: true`.

---

### 15. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 must be able to read and render A5 source records without recomputing or repairing them. A5 source packages should therefore provide:

| Layer 10 output/input family | A5 source requirement | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| IHARQ timeline view | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, source IDs, action tokens, reason codes, decision time index | Derived view only; not primary evidence |
| Reason-code distribution view | reason-code taxonomy/config, decision rows, validation status | Displays explanation distribution; not clinical explanation |
| Evidence-flow / request-combine view | `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, request/combine logs, evidence cost, source windows | Requires combine/request activity; otherwise not applicable |
| Fallback view | `FallbackDecisionRecord`, fallback route/reason/target/cost, source decision IDs | Proxy fallback only |
| Unsafe-event view | `UnsafeEventRecord`, unsafe trigger/reason, blocked action, severity/warning text | Computational/proxy unsafe warning only |
| Baseline comparison view | `MatchedComparisonReport`, A0–A4 comparator rows, metric dictionary IDs | Diagnostic-only warnings for unmatched rows |
| A5 ablation view | `IHARQAblationRecord`, local sub-ablation rows, config hashes | Local A5 labels only; no new global ablation IDs |
| Trace-completeness view | source lineage, rule path, metric dictionary, diagnostic flag, negative-result note, export IDs | Missing trace blocks thesis-ready export |
| IHARQ reliability card source bundle | bounded A5 summaries, limitations, warning banners, negative results | Rendered card is Layer 10 derived output |
| Claim-evidence coverage view | claim IDs where available, limitation tags, diagnostic-only status, Layer 0 review status | Claim evidence remains governed by Layer 0/Phase 15 |
| Reproducibility manifest | source paths/hashes where available, run IDs, seeds, config hashes, schema versions, metric dictionary, matched keys | Exact storage paths remain `MC-009` confirmable |

Layer 10 must surface warnings for missing source lineage, invalid action tokens, `combine`/`combine_evidence` alias mismatch, missing reason code, missing metric dictionary entry, missing matched key, diagnostic-only comparison, missing negative-result note, missing behavior-specific logs, source-vs-dashboard metric ambiguity, and forbidden clinical/deployment/safety claim attempts.

Layer 10 must not silently repair action tokens, threshold choices, reason codes, evidence-combination eligibility, fallback decisions, unsafe triggers, metric definitions, diagnostic-only downgrades, source records, or alias conflicts.

---

### 16. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

| Claim class | A5 status | Required wording boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Rule-based evidence verification | Allowed when source records, matched comparisons, metrics, traces, and limitation tags are complete | “A5 evaluates rule-based IHARQ-lite evidence verification under public EEG proxy/offline conditions.” |
| Proxy readiness-control behavior | Allowed where action tokens, reason codes, and costs are complete | “computational/proxy readiness-control evidence,” not real readiness or safety |
| Accepted-decision reliability / wrong-accept reduction | Allowed only under matched keys and metric dictionary support | “reduced wrong accepted decisions in this public-data proxy evaluation,” not clinical safety |
| Request/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe behavior | Allowed as traceable computational behavior | “reason-coded proxy behavior,” not real action, treatment, or safety validation |
| Negative/null result | Required when A0–A4 or local baselines are sufficient | “baseline sufficiency under matched conditions,” not failed experiment to hide |
| Clinical BCI-FES validation | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Real patient safety | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Medical-device readiness | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Real rehabilitation efficacy | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Real muscle stimulation control | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Real-time deployment safety | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Clinical fatigue/neurological-state diagnosis | Forbidden | Must be blocked |
| Real-world closed-loop reliability | Forbidden | Must be blocked |

Required limitation labels include:

```text
public_eeg_only
proxy_readiness
computational_evidence_verification
evaluation_only
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where matching/lineage/metric completeness fails
simulation_only where later Layer 7 records are used
stress_conditioned where later Layer 8 stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where later Layer 9 records are used
```

Layer 0 must later review A5 claim-evidence entries, limitation tags, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, dashboard/card captions, and forbidden-claim wording. Layer 0 must not be cited as producing the A5 performance evidence.

---

### 17. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

A5 must preserve negative and null results as evidence. A negative result is required when:

| Negative-result condition | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| A2 confidence-threshold baseline matches A5 at matched coverage/cost | A5 is threshold-equivalent under the tested condition; record `NegativeResultNote`; do not claim IHARQ necessity |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction is sufficient | Selective prediction may be the simpler adequate method under the tested operating point |
| A4 longer-window, voting, averaging, or ordinary ensembles match or beat A5 | Ordinary control sufficiency must be reported; IHARQ novelty is narrowed |
| A5 over-requests evidence or adds unacceptable delay/cost | Report action-cost burden; no low-latency/readiness claim |
| A5 over-fallbacks or becomes too conservative | Report fallback-burden and coverage collapse; no safety-improvement overclaim |
| `unsafe` blocking reduces wrong accepts only by collapsing coverage | Report coverage collapse as limitation, not safety success |
| `combine_evidence` adds no value over A4 ordinary aggregation | Report no additional combine value and preserve A4 sufficiency |
| Missing helper views prevent stability/agreement claims | Mark stability/agreement conclusions diagnostic-only |
| RegimeRisk records are unavailable | A7/regime-aware claims are deferred; core A5 remains regime-unaware |

Baseline sufficiency is thesis-useful because it identifies when a simpler, cheaper, more transparent baseline is enough. The final thesis may report that finding only with matched keys, metric dictionary support, limitation tags, and clear diagnostic/negative-result language.

---

### 18. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

| Trigger | Required downgrade or block | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Missing or invalid `PredictionRecord` | Block affected A5 decision | No A5 row for affected case |
| Missing `ModelRegistryRecord` or class-order/score-type mismatch | Block or diagnostic-only | No fair comparison claim |
| Missing `CalibrationRecord` in calibrated mode | Declared uncalibrated/degraded mode or block | Calibrated A5 claim blocked |
| Missing `UncertaintyRecord` where uncertainty rules are claimed | Block/degrade uncertainty rule | No uncertainty-based A5 claim |
| Missing/invalid `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Block threshold-dependent rule/comparison | No threshold-comparison claim |
| Split leakage or test-tuned thresholds | Reject run or diagnostic-only | No thesis-ready claim |
| True label/future outcome used decision-time | Reject ordinary run | Oracle/headroom diagnostic only if separated |
| Invalid action token | Reject record | No valid A5 decision |
| `combine` stored instead of `combine_evidence` | Alias violation; repair by rerun or mark invalid | No silent normalization |
| Missing reason code or rule path | Incomplete/diagnostic-only or block | No interpretable IHARQ claim |
| Missing `IHARQTraceRecord` | Diagnostic-only or block | No traceable thesis-ready row |
| Missing matched comparison key | Diagnostic-only | No comparative improvement claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Diagnostic-only | No metric-based claim |
| Missing negative-result note where applicable | Block claim integration | Cherry-picking risk |
| Missing source/export lineage for Layer 10 | Dashboard warning and diagnostic-only | No thesis-ready export |
| Missing fallback/combine/unsafe logs when behavior active | Block behavior-specific claim | No fallback/combine/unsafe claim |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants not separated | Diagnostic-only for A5/A6 learned-quality comparisons | No learned-quality claim |
| RegimeRisk absent but regime-aware claim attempted | Block/defer A7 claim | Core A5 remains regime-unaware |
| Stress/simulation/embodiment tags missing for later contexts | Diagnostic-only or block downstream context | No A12/A13 claim |
| Forbidden clinical/deployment/safety wording appears | Layer 0 block | No public claim until corrected |

### 19. Open Issues and Requires-Confirmation Items

| Issue | Type | A5 handling |
|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` `TrialRecord` / trial-level representation | schema/naming conflict | Require `trial_id` / `window_id` keys where needed; preserve declared missingness; do not invent standalone official record if unresolved |
| `MC-002` `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared-producer nuance | producer/ownership conflict | Require producer module, phase ID, branch/variant tag, and source IDs to distinguish Layer 4 rule-derived from Layer 6 learned variants |
| `MC-003` `combine` vs `combine_evidence` | action-token alias conflict | Preserve `combine_evidence` as canonical stored Layer 4 token; `combine` display/adapter alias only if mapped |
| `MC-007` `DashboardMetricRecord` boundary | dashboard ownership conflict | Separate source/evaluation metrics from Layer 10 generated dashboard metric/view records |
| `MC-008` `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path | metric-definition schema gap | Mark final schema/path and exact metric formulas as requires-confirmation; missing metric entry downgrades claim |
| `MC-009` repository paths and storage homes | storage path gap | Use conceptual homes and manifest mappings; exact storage paths remain confirmation-dependent |
| `MC-010` lifecycle/status vocabulary | status preservation issue | Preserve candidate, inferred, normalized, requires-confirmation, diagnostic-only, and blocked statuses |
| `MC-011` Layer 10 evidence boundary | dashboard/claim boundary risk | Dashboard outputs remain derived/read-only; source records remain primary evidence |
| `MC-012` Layer 0 evidence boundary | claim-safety boundary risk | Layer 0 audits claims; does not produce empirical evidence |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` vs `ClaimEvidenceManifest` | alias/schema ambiguity | Preserve ambiguity until resolved; do not silently treat them as identical or separate final artifacts |
| Exact local A5.x numbering | local sub-ablation naming gap | Use descriptive local labels for v0.1; exact numeric labels require confirmation |
| Exact final dataset list, seeds, run counts, statistical test, metric formulas, table/figure numbers, dashboard routes, command lines | v1.0 run-matrix gap | Defer as `requires_confirmation: true` |

| A10/A11 — Bandit/RL | Provide frozen A5 action traces/context only; no policy updates, rewards, or RL claims in A5 |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Provide clean A5 source records for controlled stress replay; stress-conditioned copies must preserve clean/stress separation |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Provide proxy readiness/action context through later layers; no real embodiment validation |
| Metric-family section | Carry A5 metric dictionary requirements, exact formula gaps, and forbidden metric classes |

| Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries | Carry allowed/forbidden A5 claims, limitation tags, diagnostic-only conditions, and negative-result language |

### 21. v0.1 Versus v1.0 Boundary and A5 Self-Audit Summary

This A5 section defines the protocol-level scientific comparison requirements for IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification in `v0.1`. It does not finalize the complete `v1.0` run matrix unless the supplied documents already fix the choice.

| Boundary item | v0.1 treatment in this section | v1.0 / confirmation status |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset list | Requires public-data source lineage, split IDs, and declared missingness | Exact dataset list remains `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Model and run matrix | Requires model/decoder identity, class order, seeds where available, and matched baseline/control lineage | Exact model-family run list, final seeds, and number of runs remain `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Rule configuration | Requires declared action tokens, reason codes, rule path, thresholds, budgets, and config hash | Exact A5 rule grid, request budget, and local numeric A5.x labels remain `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Metrics | Requires metric-family definitions, metric dictionary linkage, matched keys, and negative-result visibility | Exact metric formulas, denominators, aggregation, statistical tests, and table/figure numbering remain `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Dashboard/export | Requires source lineage, warning surfaces, export IDs where rendered, and Layer 10 read-only behavior | Exact dashboard routes, card IDs, export paths, and manifest schema remain `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Claim integration | Requires Layer 0 limitation tags, diagnostic-only triggers, and forbidden-claim blocking | Exact final claim-evidence matrix/manifest schema remains unresolved and `requires_confirmation: true` |

A final self-audit of this A5 append gives the following result:

| Audit item | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt target honored | `pass` | Target is A5 and output mode is append to preserved A0–A4 protocol |
| Previous A0–A4 preservation | `pass` | Prior protocol body remains intact in the full Markdown file |
| Official A5 identity | `pass` | A5 is IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification, not a phase, layer, producer, dashboard, or learned policy |
| Corrected A2/A3/A4 identities | `pass` | A2 threshold, A3 uncertainty/selective prediction, and A4 ordinary longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble controls are not collapsed |
| C0–C4 relationship | `pass` | Added explicit capability-tier boundary and C1 partial-maturity note |
| Required records and artifacts | `pass_with_open_issues` | Added Phase 2 baseline metric/readiness/card context and preserved helper-view, metric-dictionary, dashboard, and claim-evidence unresolved statuses |
| Matched comparison discipline | `pass` | A5 versus A0–A4 requires matched source, split, model, threshold, uncertainty, ordinary-control, cost, metric, and claim keys |
| Metric governance | `pass_with_v1_0_deferred_items` | Metric families are defined; exact denominators/formulas/statistical tests remain confirmation-dependent |
| Layer 10 boundary | `pass` | Layer 10 reads, validates, renders, warns, exports, and packages; it does not repair or create hidden primary evidence |
| Layer 0 boundary | `pass` | Layer 0 audits/downgrades claims and blocks forbidden wording; it does not create empirical A5 results |
| Diagnostic-only and negative-result governance | `pass` | Missing lineage, leakage, alias violations, missing metrics, and negative/null outcomes are explicitly handled |
| No unsupported top-level ablation IDs | `pass` | No A14 or new global ID introduced; local A5 labels remain local/candidate where appropriate |

### 3. Target Purpose and Scientific Question

A6 asks the following thesis-level scientific question:

> Under public-EEG, offline/proxy Stretch C constraints, does adding a split-safe evidence-quality estimator to IHARQ-style evidence verification improve reliability, high-confidence-wrong detection, accepted-decision quality, and matched coverage/cost behavior beyond calibrated confidence, simple registered thresholds, uncertainty/selective prediction, ordinary aggregation/ensemble controls, and rule-based IHARQ-lite, without target leakage or claim overreach?

A6 is scientifically meaningful only if the evidence-quality score is evaluated as a constrained reliability estimator, not as an all-purpose adaptive controller. The A6 evaluation must therefore track:

| A6 behavior family | Scientific reason to measure it | Claim-safe interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Learned or estimated evidence-quality score | Tests whether current evidence reliability can be predicted from legal calibration, uncertainty, stability, agreement, signal-quality, IHARQ, and optional RegimeRisk features | Computational/proxy evidence-reliability score only; not a clinical safety score |
| Predicted failure probability | Tests whether failure risk is captured beyond confidence/entropy/margin | Offline reliability-estimation evidence only; denominator and target definition require metric-dictionary entries |
| Quality-score calibration | Tests whether quality scores are themselves reliable probabilities or scores | Calibration/audit claim only; not proof of readiness or deployment safety |
| Reliability-vs-coverage curve | Tests whether thresholding the quality score preserves better accepted-decision reliability at matched coverage/cost | Matched proxy evaluation only; not real action validation |
| High-confidence-wrong detection | Tests whether the estimator detects failures that confidence alone misses | Public-data failure-detection evidence only; not patient-risk prediction |
| Feature/context ablations | Tests whether quality estimation depends on calibration, uncertainty, stability, agreement, signal quality, IHARQ reason codes, or optional RegimeRisk context | Contribution analysis only; no physiology or clinical-state claim |
| Evidence-quality-enhanced IHARQ action analysis | Tests whether A5 decisions improve when quality scores are used in a declared, leakage-safe variant | Local A6 comparison only; it must not become A9 supervised policy or A7 RegimeRisk claim |
| Negative-result preservation | Tests whether simple baselines are sufficient or the estimator is unreliable | Valid thesis evidence when documented with limitations and diagnostic flags |

A6 must be evaluated even if the result is negative. A weak quality estimator, a poorly calibrated score, or a result where A2/A3/A5 is sufficient is not a failed document outcome. It is a required source-grounded negative or baseline-sufficiency result.

| `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, evidence-quality card, card/export/reproducibility artifacts | Layer 10 / Phase 14 | Derived display, warning, export, card, and reproducibility packaging from source records | Derived/read-only; not primary evidence |

If a source-supported local diagnostic variant emits a policy-like artifact, it must be marked as downstream/contextual, separated from the core learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` claim, and prevented from implying A8/A9/A10/A11/A12/A13 completion. |

---

### 6. Producer-Consumer Discipline

A6 may say that a record is **used by**, **evaluated in**, **compared under**, **dashboarded from**, or **summarized for** the A6 evaluation context. It must not say that A6 itself owns or produces canonical records.

| Correct statement | Incorrect statement |
|---|---|
| Layer 6 / Phase 6 produces learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants used by A6. | A6 produces `EvidenceQualityRecord`. |
| Layer 4 / Phase 4 produces `IHARQDecisionRecord` rows used as A5 baseline/context for A6. | A6 rewrites IHARQ decisions. |
| Layer 3 produces calibration, uncertainty, threshold, and selective-prediction records used as features/comparators. | The A6 identifier is treated as the source of calibration or threshold selection. |
| Layer 5 supplies optional temporal-trust context where records are available and decision-time legal. | A6 proves RegimeRisk or real fatigue-state detection. |
| Layer 10 renders A6 dashboard/card/export views from source records. | A6 dashboard cards are primary empirical evidence. |
| Layer 0 reviews A6 claims and downgrades invalid ones. | Layer 0 produces A6 quality scores or metrics. |

A6 must preserve the distinction between:

1. **Rule-derived evidence-quality fields** produced by Layer 4/Phase 4 where present;
2. **Learned evidence-quality estimator outputs** produced by Layer 6/Phase 6;
3. **Supervised readiness-policy actions** produced by Phase 6 for A9, not by core A6;
4. **Action-token alias mapping** inherited from Layer 4, especially the `combine` versus canonical `combine_evidence` issue;
5. **Deferral, simulation, stress, and embodiment outputs** produced later and not required for core A6.

---

### 7. Target Construction, Feature Legality, and Leakage Controls

#### 7.1 A6 target-construction rule

A6 may train or evaluate evidence-quality scores only from explicitly declared proxy targets. The primary source-supported target is a reliability proxy such as:

```text
reliable = 1 if the decoder prediction equals the true task label
reliable = 0 otherwise
```

This correctness-derived reliability target is permitted only as a training/evaluation target under split-safe target-construction rules. It must never appear as an observable decision-time feature, controller input, dashboard-side repair signal, or claim that real clinical readiness was observed.

Allowed optional target families, where source-supported and explicitly documented, include:

| Target family | Status | Required caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Decoder-correctness reliability | `core_supported_proxy_target` | Measures decoder correctness under public EEG labels, not real readiness or patient safety |
| High-confidence wrong status | `supported_evaluation_target_where_high_confidence_wrong_audit_exists` | Must be partitioned correctly; cannot be a decision-time feature |
| Stable-correct vs stable-wrong category | `conditional_target` | Requires source-supported stability definitions and matched windows |
| Wrong-accept risk under declared IHARQ variant | `conditional_target` | Requires IHARQ action records, metric dictionary entries, and no use of held-out labels at decision time |
| Failure probability under declared stress | `future_or_downstream_conditional` | Belongs to A12/stress-conditioned contexts unless stress records exist and are explicitly tagged |
| Real patient readiness, clinical safety, rehabilitation success, real muscle activation | `forbidden_target_for_A6` | Must not be used or claimed from public EEG evidence |

Every target-construction route must have a target-construction card/source bundle stating source labels, permitted partitions, forbidden fields, transformation logic, split role, validation result, limitation tags, and exact target version/hash. If this card/source bundle is missing, A6 learned-quality claims become diagnostic-only.

#### 7.2 Decision-time feature legality

| Feature group | A6 use status | Leakage rule |
|---|---|---|
| Decoder output, score, class-order, model ID | `allowed_if_source_prediction_record_valid` | Must come from the current prediction row and matched model lineage |
| Calibrated confidence, calibration-bin membership, Brier/NLL-derived training summaries where legal | `allowed_if_calibration_record_valid` | Calibration parameters must be learned on allowed splits; held-out/test labels cannot tune them |
| Entropy, margin, probability gap, variation ratio | `allowed_if_computed_from_decision_time_scores` | Must not use correctness labels as features |
| Selective-prediction flags and threshold IDs | `allowed_if_threshold_registry_valid` | Thresholds must be registered and selected on permitted splits |
| Model-family agreement, ensemble disagreement, channel-subset agreement | `allowed_if_A4_or_source_feature_lineage_valid` | Must preserve aggregation/ensemble config and row matching; future windows are forbidden unless declared for target construction only |
| Time-window stability and previous-window agreement | `allowed_if_causal_window_history_valid` | Only current/past windows visible at the decision time may be used as features |
| Artifact flags, channel masks, dropout indicators, signal-quality fields | `allowed_if_source_artifact_flag_or_signal_quality_lineage_valid` | Must not infer clinical state; missing or post hoc flags must be marked |
| IHARQ action token, reason code, fallback/unsafe status, trace IDs | `allowed_if_IHARQ_record_precedes_A6_score_for_that_variant` | Must preserve source action token and avoid circular use where quality score caused the action being used as a feature |
| RegimeRisk label, trust score, risk trend, stop-loss warning | `optional_if_Phase5_records_available_and_causal` | Future regime labels or post-outcome fields are forbidden; A7 claim boundary must be preserved |
| Ground-truth label, decoder correctness, future windows, future rewards, oracle costs | `target_or_evaluation_partition_only` | Forbidden as decision-time features; use in features is leakage |
| Stress profile, embodiment outcome, transition reward | `downstream_context_only_for_A6` | Not core A6 unless later-phase records exist and are explicitly tagged; cannot support core A6 claim alone |

#### 7.3 Leakage blockers

A6 must be blocked, or marked diagnostic-only for affected rows, when any of the following occurs:

- target labels, decoder correctness, future windows, future rewards, or oracle costs appear as decision-time features;
- calibration or thresholds are selected on held-out/test outcomes;
- evidence-quality thresholds are selected on final test outcomes;
- subject/session leakage contaminates train/validation/test partitions;
- target-construction and evaluation partitions are not separated;
- a quality score is evaluated on the same rows used for model selection without proper validation separation;
- RegimeRisk fields use future temporal information;
- A6 comparisons use different row populations without a diagnostic label;
- metric dictionary entries or denominator definitions are missing;
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` producer/variant tags are absent;
- negative results or baseline sufficiency findings are hidden.

---

### 8. Required A6 Evaluation Design

#### 8.1 Minimum viable A6 evaluation

A minimum viable A6 section requires:

1. validated upstream Phase 1–5 source lineage where used;
2. a split-safe `ReadinessContextRecord` or equivalent context assembly record with feature legality status;
3. a learned or estimated `EvidenceQualityRecord` variant tagged with producer layer, phase, branch, variant, source IDs, split, seed, config hash, target-construction ID, and claim tags;
4. a target-construction card/source bundle documenting reliability/failure target logic;
5. reliability-vs-coverage and high-confidence-wrong evaluation where source metrics exist;
6. comparison against confidence/uncertainty/simple threshold baselines where matched rows exist;
7. comparison against rule-only IHARQ-lite A5 where IHARQ records exist;
8. Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` rows with metric dictionary references;
9. A6 `MatchedComparisonReport` with matched keys and diagnostic-only flags;
10. `NegativeResultNote` entries when the estimator is weak, poorly calibrated, or baseline-equivalent;
11. Layer 10 warning/export source fields;
12. Layer 0 claim-safety tags and limitation language.

#### 8.2 Strong / thesis-ready A6 evaluation

A strong A6 additionally includes:

- subject-wise, session-wise, dataset-wise, model-family-wise, and seed-level stability analysis;
- quality-score calibration analysis, not only ranking metrics;
- context ablations separating confidence-only, uncertainty-only, calibration+uncertainty, stability/agreement, signal-quality, IHARQ-reason-code, and optional RegimeRisk feature groups;
- high-confidence wrong detection tables with matched A1/A2/A3 baselines;
- comparison against A4 ordinary longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble controls where source rows exist;
- A6-vs-A5 analysis showing whether quality scoring improves rule-only IHARQ accepted-decision reliability, wrong-accept behavior, coverage, or evidence burden;
- generalization and overfitting diagnostics for subject/session/dataset splits;
- sensitivity to target definitions and quality-threshold choices;
- complete evidence-quality card and source bundle for Layer 10;
- explicit handling of baseline sufficiency and negative results;
- claim-evidence entries for Phase 15 with limitations and diagnostic-only status.

#### 8.3 Required baselines and comparators

| Comparator | Required source support | A6 comparison question | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw / accept-all | `PredictionRecord`, model/split/source IDs, baseline metric rows | Does quality scoring improve over forced prediction? | Missing source IDs, unmatched rows, no metric dictionary |
| A1 calibrated decoder | `CalibrationRecord`, calibration eligibility, score lineage | Does the quality estimator add value beyond calibrated probability visibility? | Calibration leakage, ineligible calibration, missing calibration ID |
| A2 simple registered threshold | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, matched operating point, coverage/cost rows | Is a learned quality threshold better than a simple confidence threshold? | Test-tuned threshold, unmatched coverage/cost, missing registry |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, risk-coverage rows | Does quality estimation add value beyond entropy/margin/selective prediction? | Unmatched risk-coverage, illegal threshold selection |
| A4 ordinary aggregation/ensemble controls | `EnsembleControlRecord`, aggregation/ensemble config, row lineage | Is the estimator more than ordinary voting, averaging, longer-window smoothing, or model agreement? | Different window populations, missing delay/evidence-cost accounting |
| A5 IHARQ-lite | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, A5 matched reports | Does quality scoring improve rule-only IHARQ evidence verification? | Missing source action token, missing trace, circular feature/action use |
| A7 RegimeRisk context | `RegimeStateRecord` / `TrustStateRecord` where available | Does temporal-trust context improve evidence-quality estimation or explain degradation? | Future regime fields, untagged regime-aware feature group, A7 claim overreach |
| Evidence-quality threshold baseline | learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, threshold selection record, validation split | Does score thresholding produce reliable accepted sets? | Threshold selected on test, missing threshold lineage, no validation separation |
| Oracle or label-aware upper bound | Explicit diagnostic-only configuration | What is theoretical headroom? | Any use as deployable or thesis-superiority evidence is invalid |

---

### 9. Local A6 Sub-Ablation Policy

Local sub-ablations are allowed only as children of A6 and only for explaining the evidence-quality estimator’s contribution. They do not become new global A-IDs.

| Local sub-ablation ID | Parent global ID | Variant definition | Required config difference | Required records | Metric purpose | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A6.1` | A6 | Confidence-only evidence-quality estimator or threshold-style quality score | Uses only calibrated/top-class confidence where legal | `CalibrationRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, learned or baseline quality record, matched report | Tests whether A6 collapses to A2/A1 | `inferred_candidate`; exact label requires v1.0 confirmation |
| `A6.2` | A6 | Uncertainty-only estimator | Uses entropy/margin/probability-gap features without IHARQ/stability/regime fields | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, quality outputs | Tests whether A6 collapses to A3 | `inferred_candidate`; exact label requires v1.0 confirmation |
| `A6.3` | A6 | Calibration + uncertainty + stability/agreement estimator | Adds window stability, model agreement, channel-subset or signal-quality features where source-supported | Feature-provenance bundle, `EvidenceQualityRecord`, matched report | Tests nontrivial evidence-quality gain beyond A1–A3 | `inferred_candidate`; exact feature set requires confirmation |
| `A6.4` | A6 | IHARQ-context quality estimator | Adds source IHARQ action/reason/trace features without circularity | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` | Tests quality scoring as an addition to A5 | `inferred_candidate`; circularity checks required |
| `A6.5` | A6 | Regime-aware quality-feature variant | Adds causal Phase 5 regime/trust features | `RegimeStateRecord`, optional `TrustStateRecord`, temporal cutoff evidence | Tests optional temporal-trust contribution without claiming A7 completion | `conditional`; must be cross-tagged with A7 context |
| `A6.6` | A6 | Quality-score calibration variant | Calibrates the evidence-quality score on a permitted calibration/validation partition | score calibration record/plot, metric dictionary, split lineage | Tests whether quality score is probabilistically meaningful | `conditional`; not a clinical reliability guarantee |
| `A6.oracle_diagnostic` | A6 | Label/future-aware upper-bound or headroom diagnostic | Uses forbidden deployable information only in isolated diagnostic upper-bound mode | diagnostic-only flag, target-construction card, leakage note | Estimates headroom only | `diagnostic_only`; cannot support final superiority claims |

Local sub-ablation labels in this table are v0.1 protocol labels, not final repository run IDs. Exact local numbering, config names, feature-set manifests, and storage paths require v1.0 confirmation.

---

### 10. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Requirements

A6 metric rows must be exported only with metric dictionary IDs or explicit diagnostic-only status. The following families are allowed as v0.1 requirements; exact formulas, denominators, confidence intervals, and statistical tests remain v1.0 confirmation items unless already fixed by source artifacts.

| Metric family | Example metric intent | Required source records | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reliability-estimation discrimination | AUROC/AUPRC or equivalent for reliable/unreliable or failure target | learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, target-construction card, split IDs, metric dictionary | `allowed_with_metric_dictionary`; exact metric set requires confirmation |
| Quality-score calibration | ECE/Brier/NLL or calibration-curve style evaluation for quality score where probabilistic | score outputs, calibration/evaluation split, metric dictionary | `allowed_with_metric_dictionary`; must not imply clinical safety |
| Reliability-vs-coverage | accepted reliability as quality threshold varies | score outputs, threshold-selection record, matched rows, metric dictionary | `core_A6_metric_family`; denominators require confirmation |
| High-confidence wrong detection | detection or reduction of high-confidence wrong cases | high-confidence-wrong audit, predictions, quality score, metric dictionary | `core_A6_metric_family_where_source_audit_exists` |
| Accepted-decision reliability | accuracy/reliability of accepted decisions under quality-enhanced IHARQ variant | IHARQ source records, learned quality outputs, matched report | `allowed`; must be matched against A5/A2/A3 |
| Wrong-accept behavior | wrong accepted decisions under matched coverage/cost | IHARQ/quality decisions, labels in evaluation partition, metric dictionary | `allowed`; denominator must be defined |
| Coverage / rejection / gating burden | retained coverage, rejected/flagged quality rows, evidence burden | quality thresholds, IHARQ action records, matched keys | `allowed`; must compare fairly to A2/A3/A5 |
| Feature/context contribution | delta from adding feature groups | context-ablation table, same rows/splits/seeds | `allowed`; negative results required |
| Generalization stability | subject/session/dataset/model/seed generalization | split records, group IDs, metric rows | `allowed`; exact aggregation policy requires confirmation |
| Delay/request/fallback/unsafe burden | only if quality score changes IHARQ action behavior | IHARQ decisions, fallback/unsafe records, quality-enhanced variant config | `conditional`; not required for pure score evaluation |
| Reward, regret, transition outcomes, embodiment endpoint errors | simulation/stress/embodiment metrics | Layer 7/8/9 records | `not_core_A6`; downstream A10–A13 only unless explicitly tagged diagnostic context |

Forbidden metric treatment:

- Do not report medical safety, patient readiness, rehabilitation efficacy, real-time BCI-FES success, real muscle activation, or deployment safety as A6 metrics.
- Do not report dashboard-rendered values as primary metrics unless their source `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` and metric dictionary entry exist.
- Do not treat a quality score threshold tuned on test data as a valid A6 operating point.
- Do not hide that simple A2/A3/A5 baselines may be sufficient.

A6 comparisons are thesis-ready only when the matched comparison report preserves all applicable keys.


| Comparison | Required matched keys | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A6 learned quality vs A2 simple threshold | same rows/splits/model/calibration/threshold lineage, coverage/cost operating point, metric dictionary | missing threshold registry, test-tuned threshold, unmatched coverage/cost |
| A6 learned quality vs A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | same rows/splits/model/calibration/uncertainty/selective lineage, risk-coverage rows | different row populations, missing risk-coverage source, metric gap |
| A6 learned quality vs A4 ordinary controls | same model/window/session universe, aggregation/ensemble config, delay/evidence-cost visibility | different window history, missing delay burden, no ensemble provenance |
| A6 learned quality vs A5 IHARQ-lite | source `IHARQDecisionRecord`, action token, reason code, trace ID, same prediction/calibration rows | missing IHARQ trace, action-token rewrite, circular quality-feature use |
| A6 feature ablations | same train/validation/test split, target construction, model family, seed/config except declared feature set | hidden feature changes, target leakage, nonidentical row set without flag |
| A6 regime-aware vs regime-unaware quality | same rows and causal temporal cutoff; Phase 5 records tagged | future regime fields, missing temporal cutoff, overclaiming A7 |
| A6 quality-threshold operating points | validation-selected threshold, held-out evaluation, metric dictionary | threshold selected on held-out/test outcomes, missing quality threshold ID |

If matched keys are incomplete, the row may remain dashboard-visible with warnings but must be marked diagnostic-only and must not support thesis-ready comparative claims.

### 12. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 must be able to read and display A6 evidence without becoming the source of that evidence.

| Layer 10 output / obligation | A6 requirement | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence-quality card | Summarize estimator family, feature groups, target construction, split/seed/config, metric dictionary, limitations, negative results, and diagnostic flags | Derived card only; source records remain Layer 6/evaluation artifacts |
| Reliability-vs-coverage panel | Render source curves/tables and matched comparator rows | Must cite source `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` / matched report lineage |
| High-confidence-wrong panel | Render source high-confidence wrong detection table and examples where allowed | Must preserve public-data/proxy limitation and not present patient-risk claims |
| Feature/context-ablation panel | Show contribution of feature groups and baseline sufficiency | Must not hide negative or null contributions |
| Matched-comparison table | Expose A6 vs A2/A3/A4/A5 and optional A7-context comparisons | Must show missing-key and diagnostic-only status |
| Warning engine | Surface leakage, producer-variant ambiguity, metric dictionary gap, missing target card, missing feature legality, unmatched row populations, negative-result hiding, and forbidden claim wording | Warning visibility is required; warnings cannot silently repair evidence |
| Reproducibility export | Package source IDs, configs, feature-set IDs, target-construction ID, quality-estimator config, seeds, hashes, metric dictionary IDs, and validation results | Export is read-only and lineage-bound |
| Dashboard filtering | Allow global/local ablation IDs, split, dataset, subject/session, model family, feature set, target construction, producer layer/phase, diagnostic status, and claim tags | Filters must not alter source evidence |

Layer 10 may produce `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, cards, figures, and export manifests only as derived reporting artifacts. Missing or ambiguous source records must produce warnings or diagnostic-only status, not dashboard-side repair.

---

### 13. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Rules for A6

#### 13.1 Allowed claim forms

A6 may support only bounded claims such as:

- “A split-safe evidence-quality estimator improved proxy evidence-reliability ranking under the declared public-EEG protocol.”
- “The learned quality score improved reliability-vs-coverage compared with matched confidence/uncertainty/IHARQ-lite baselines for the evaluated rows.”
- “The estimator detected some high-confidence wrong cases that simple confidence or entropy baselines missed, under the declared target-construction and metric definitions.”
- “The evidence-quality estimator was not consistently better than simpler baselines; this limits the adaptive-policy claim and supports a baseline-sufficiency interpretation.”

#### 13.2 Required limitation language

Every A6 thesis-facing summary must state that:

- targets are proxy/computational, usually based on public EEG decoder correctness or declared failure proxies;
- labels are not clinical readiness labels;
- evidence-quality scores are not patient-safety scores;
- public EEG motor-imagery/task labels do not validate real assistive control;
- accepted-decision reliability is an offline/proxy metric;
- any RegimeRisk context is temporal-trust/proxy context and not clinical fatigue diagnosis;
- dashboard outputs are derived views from source records;
- exact metric definitions and run-matrix choices require final metric dictionary and v1.0 confirmation where not yet fixed.

#### 13.3 Forbidden A6 claims

A6 must not claim:

- clinical safety or medical-device readiness;
- validated patient readiness;
- real BCI-FES deployment readiness;
- real muscle stimulation or real embodiment control;
- rehabilitation efficacy;
- real fatigue, neurological decline, or patient-risk detection;
- online adaptation or deployment learning;
- reinforcement-learning or contextual-bandit improvement;
- StressForge robustness or embodiment success unless later A12/A13 evidence is separately produced and tagged.

Any draft claim that violates these rules must be blocked or rewritten by Layer 0 and marked as unsupported.

---

### 14. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

A6 must preserve negative and baseline-sufficiency outcomes. The following results are valid and must not be hidden:

| Result | Correct interpretation | Required artifact |
|---|---|---|
| A2 simple threshold matches or beats A6 under matched coverage/cost | Simple confidence threshold may be sufficient for that tested condition | `NegativeResultNote`, matched report, limitation |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction matches or beats A6 | Learned quality may not add value beyond uncertainty/selective baselines | `NegativeResultNote`, risk-coverage comparison |
| A4 ordinary aggregation/ensemble matches or beats A6 | Evidence quality may be replicating ordinary agreement/smoothing | `NegativeResultNote`, delay/evidence-cost accounting |
| A5 IHARQ-lite matches or beats A6 | Rule-only IHARQ may be sufficient; quality estimator is not justified as improvement | `NegativeResultNote`, A5/A6 matched report |
| Quality score has poor calibration | It may rank some cases but cannot be treated as calibrated reliability probability | score calibration report, diagnostic or narrowed claim |
| High-confidence wrong detection is weak | A6 cannot claim robust failure detection | high-confidence-wrong table and limitation |
| Feature ablation shows RegimeRisk or IHARQ features add no value | Context contribution is not supported in that protocol slice | context-ablation table and limitation |
| Subject/session/dataset generalization is unstable | Learned quality may overfit public-data artifacts | group generalization report and diagnostic flag |
| Target construction is leaky or ambiguous | A6 learned-quality claims are invalid or diagnostic-only | leakage warning, diagnostic flag, target-card repair request |
| Metric dictionary entries are missing | Metric-bearing claims cannot be thesis-ready | diagnostic-only flag and open issue |

Negative results should be visible in Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A6 `MatchedComparisonReport`, evidence-quality card source bundle, Layer 10 warning inputs, claim-evidence rows, and the final handoff manifest.

---

### 15. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Rules

A6 evidence must be downgraded to diagnostic-only when:

1. source rows cannot be matched to A0–A5 comparators;
2. producer layer/phase/variant tags for `EvidenceQualityRecord` are missing;
3. target-construction card/source bundle is missing or ambiguous;
4. decision-time feature legality is not validated;
5. held-out labels, future evidence, or oracle fields leak into features;
6. calibration, threshold, or quality-threshold selection uses final test outcomes;
7. inherited IHARQ action-token aliases are unresolved, especially stored `combine` rows that should be canonical `combine_evidence` without a versioned alias map;
8. subject/session/dataset split leakage is detected;
9. metric dictionary entries are missing;
10. quality-score calibration is claimed without score-calibration evidence;
11. RegimeRisk features lack temporal cutoff or future-information checks;
12. A6 is used to claim A9 supervised policy, A10/A11 simulation learning, A12 stress robustness, or A13 embodiment success without separate source evidence;
13. negative results are omitted from cards, exports, or claim-evidence rows;
14. Layer 10 dashboard outputs are treated as primary source evidence;
15. Layer 0 forbidden clinical/deployment/real-control wording appears.


Diagnostic-only rows may be used for debugging, dashboard warnings, and future repair planning. They must not support final thesis-ready improvement claims.

A7 is a scientific evaluation-use identifier. It is not Layer 5, not Phase 5, not a module, not a record owner, not a dashboard page, not a clinical fatigue detector, not a patient-safety controller, and not a real-time medical deployment claim. The records used by A7 are produced by official layers and phases, especially Layer 5 / Phase 5 for RegimeRisk temporal-trust evidence, Layer 4 / Phase 4 for IHARQ-lite regime-unaware decisions, Layers 1–3 / Phases 1–3 for public-data, decoder, calibration, uncertainty, threshold, and matched-comparison lineage, and Layer 10 / Phase 14 for read-only dashboard/export rendering.

A7 evaluates whether legally observable temporal-trust context from RegimeRisk changes, improves, explains, or safely downgrades IHARQ-family evidence verification under matched temporal sequences.
