### 3. A7 Purpose and Scientific Question

A7 asks whether adding RegimeRisk temporal-trust context to IHARQ-family evidence verification provides source-supported value beyond matched regime-unaware IHARQ-lite and upstream static or ordinary baselines.

The primary scientific question is:

> Under identical public-data source lineage, ordered window sequences, split/legal-feature constraints, decoder/calibration/threshold/IHARQ configuration, and metric-dictionary lineage, does RegimeRisk temporal-trust context improve or explain reliability behavior compared with regime-unaware IHARQ and upstream baselines, without using future information or making clinical/deployment claims?

A7 may support the following bounded evaluation questions when source records exist:

| Question | A7 treatment | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Does temporal trust identify unstable periods? | Compare causal `RegimeStateRecord` risk/regime/trust fields against legally available error bursts, uncertainty spikes, fallback clusters, stop-loss events, stress profiles, or simulated unsafe proxy events | Temporal-trust proxy; not clinical fatigue or patient-state diagnosis |
| Does RegimeRisk improve IHARQ decisions? | Compare regime-aware IHARQ variants against matched `regime_aware=false` A5 IHARQ-lite baselines | Matched A7 comparison only; diagnostic-only if keys or controls are missing |
| Does RegimeRisk reduce wrong accepts or unsafe proxy events? | Report wrong-accept, high-risk accepted-error, fallback/no-action/unsafe recommendation, and simulation-only unsafe-proxy metrics where supported | Public-data/proxy/simulation-only; no real patient safety claim |
| Does stop-loss behavior add value? | Compare with/without stop-loss under identical temporal features and decision budget | Conservative evaluation; over-abstention must be visible as a possible negative result |
| Does trust allocation add value? | Compare full RegimeRisk against trust-allocator-disabled or compact-trust variants where records exist | Trust allocation is a proxy reliability feature, not a clinical trust or safety guarantee |
| Does RegimeRisk merely behave like random or shuffled risk? | Mandatory negative-control comparisons where an A7 improvement or temporal-signal claim is made | If random/shuffled controls are competitive, A7 claim is downgraded |

### 4. Relationship to Official Layers 0–10

A7 must preserve the architecture-layer roles below.

| Layer | Relationship to A7 | Required boundary |
|---:|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-safety and scope governance | Reviews A7 claims, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, negative-result visibility, and forbidden wording | Layer 0 governs claims; it does not produce empirical RegimeRisk evidence |
| Layer 1 — Public-data and protocol anchor | Supplies dataset, window, split, preprocessing, label-map, artifact, subject/session/run, and temporal-order lineage | A7 cannot bypass split, window, public-data, or proxy limitations |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and baseline measurement spine | Supplies `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, subject profiles, raw decoder history, and ordinary-control lineage | A7 cannot retrain or repair decoder records and cannot treat raw accuracy as temporal trust |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, uncertainty, and selective prediction | Supplies calibrated probabilities, uncertainty features, threshold registry, selective-prediction records, split-integrity reports, reliability audits, and matched operating points | No test-tuned thresholds, future correctness, or post-hoc calibration repair may enter decision-time RegimeRisk features |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ evidence verification | Supplies regime-unaware IHARQ decisions/traces, evidence-quality fields where available, fallback/unsafe histories, and A5 baseline context | A7 evaluates regime-aware variants against Layer 4 outputs; A7 does not overwrite canonical IHARQ tokens |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Produces RegimeRisk temporal-trust records, risk trends, trust summaries, trusted sets, stop-loss warnings, and Layer 5 evaluation artifacts used by A7 | Layer 5 is the producer; A7 is the evaluation-use context |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive readiness policy layer | May later consume RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss fields in `ReadinessContextRecord` and policy evaluations | A7 does not validate supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, bandit, or RL policies |
| Layer 7 — Simulated closed-loop readiness environment | May consume A7/Layer 5 regime state as simulation context where official simulation records exist | Simulation-only; no real-time deployment safety claim |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite stress generator | May provide stress-conditioned context for RegimeRisk analysis in later A12 sections | Stress-conditioned only; no physiological stress validation claim |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | May consume regime risk for simulated/proxy embodiment gating context | Embodiment-proxy only; no real muscle stimulation or rehabilitation claim |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility | Reads saved records, validates lineage, renders temporal trust panels/cards, warnings, exports, and reproducibility manifests | Derived/read-only reporting; no hidden retuning, source mutation, or primary-evidence creation |

### 5. Relationship to Official Phase 0–15 Sequence

A7 uses records generated across the official phase sequence. The ablation ID must not be described as a phase, and phases must not be compressed into unofficial macro-phases.

| Phase | A7 relationship | A7 claim condition |
|---:|---|---|
| Phase 0 | Prepares schemas, configs, validators, record lineage, metric/claim/dashboard fixtures, and global run/seed/hash conventions | If schema/path/metric fixtures remain unresolved, affected A7 outputs are open or diagnostic-only |
| Phase 1 | Produces public-data lineage, windows, splits, preprocessing, label maps, artifacts, and temporal order | Missing or ambiguous sequence identity can block or downgrade A7 |
| Phase 2 | Produces predictions, model registry, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, and ordinary controls | A7 comparisons must use matched decoder/model/seed/source lineage |
| Phase 3 | Produces calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, reliability, split-integrity, and matched-operating-point artifacts | A7 may consume only legal current/past features; future correctness remains evaluation-only |
| Phase 4 | Produces IHARQ-lite decisions/traces/fallback/unsafe histories and A5 comparison artifacts | Primary A7 regime-unaware baseline; unresolved action-token or reason-code gaps downgrade affected rows |
| Phase 5 | Produces RegimeRisk temporal-trust records and evaluation artifacts | Primary Phase 5 evidence used for A7; must pass causal, split, matched-key, negative-control, and metric-dictionary gates |
| Phase 6 | Produces learned evidence-quality / readiness-context artifacts where implemented | Optional A6 comparator/context only; A7 must not claim learned policy or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ maturity |
| Phase 7 | Learning-to-defer / deferral comparison | Downstream context only; A7 does not produce `DeferralRecord` |
| Phase 8 | Simulated closed-loop readiness | Downstream simulation context only; simulation claims remain bounded |
| Phase 9 | StressForge-Lite stress evidence | Context for stress-conditioned temporal-trust analysis; Layer 8 / Phase 9 produce stress evidence used by A12 |
| Phase 10 | Contextual bandit | Downstream simulation-bounded policy context only |
| Phase 11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream simulation-bounded policy context only |
| Phase 12 | MyoSuite embodiment demo | Optional proxy embodiment context only; Layer 9 produces embodiment evidence used by A13 |
| Phase 13 | OpenSim/static replay or optional comparison | Optional proxy embodiment/replay context only |
| Phase 14 | Dashboard/cards/reproducibility closure | Renders/export A7 artifacts from saved records; cannot create primary evidence |
| Phase 15 | Final thesis integration | Uses claim-evidence entries, negative results, and limitation tags to decide thesis-safe A7 wording |

### 7. C0–C4 Capability-Tier Relationship

C0–C4 are claim-maturity concepts, not phases, layers, records, modules, or ablation IDs. A7 contributes most directly to C1 only when Phase 5 outputs are validated and matched.

| Capability tier | A7 relationship | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| C0 — Public-data reliability spine | A7 consumes C0 source lineage from Phases 1–3 | A7 cannot rescue weak C0 split/window/decoder/calibration foundations |
| C1 — IHARQ and RegimeRisk reliability control | A7 is central to the RegimeRisk half of C1, paired with A5 IHARQ-lite | C1 remains proxy reliability control, not real patient safety or clinical validation |
| C2 — Adaptive policy layer | A7 prepares temporal-trust fields for later policy contexts | No supervised policy or deferral maturity claim from A7 alone |
| C3 — Bandit/RL simulation layer | A7 context may later influence simulation-bounded bandit/RL policies | No bandit/RL improvement claim in A7 |
| C4 — Embodiment/demo/dashboard layer | A7 feeds dashboard/cards and optional simulated embodiment gating context | Dashboard and embodiment remain derived/proxy evidence |

A7 may evaluate only source-supported records and artifacts. Missing or unresolved items must be exposed, not silently invented.

| `ModelRegistryRecord` | Layer 2 / Phase 2 | Decoder/model-family identity | Required for matched decoder comparability |
| `BaselineMetricRecord` | Layer 2 / Phase 2 | Baseline performance context | Comparator lineage; metric dictionary required for thesis claims |

| `UncertaintyRecord` | Layer 3 / Phase 3 | Entropy, margin, disagreement, conformal set, variation-ratio or other legal uncertainty features | Required for uncertainty-aware RegimeRisk; future correctness forbidden |

A7 must not introduce unregistered canonical records. Candidate or local artifacts may be referenced only as `inferred_candidate` / `requires_confirmation: true` and cannot become official merely because they are useful.

### 9. A7 Evaluation Design

#### 9.1 Minimum viable A7 evaluation

A minimum viable A7 evaluation requires all of the following:

1. A validated, causal `RegimeStateRecord` sequence linked to required Phase 1–4 source records.
2. A matched regime-unaware A5 IHARQ-lite baseline using the same ordered window sequence and compatible source lineage.
3. A declared RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ variant or comparison context that uses only current/past legally visible fields.
4. A `MatchedComparisonReport` or equivalent evaluation artifact for IHARQ-only versus IHARQ + RegimeRisk.
5. Metric dictionary references, or diagnostic-only marking if metric dictionary entries are incomplete.
6. Layer 0 limitation tags and diagnostic-only flags on incomplete, unmatched, or unsupported rows.
7. Layer 10-readable source IDs and export lineage, without treating dashboard views as primary evidence.

If the minimum comparison is unmatched, temporally illegal, missing source IDs, or missing required metric dictionary references, A7 may still exist as a diagnostic temporal-trust audit, but it may not support a thesis-facing improvement claim.

#### 9.2 Strong / thesis-ready A7 evaluation

A strong A7 evaluation additionally includes:

| Strong requirement | Purpose | Downgrade if missing |
|---|---|---|
| Conditional `TrustStateRecord` where independent trust timelines are consumed | Makes per-target trust allocation and trusted-set evolution traceable | Trust timeline claims become incomplete or diagnostic-only |
| `trust_scores.csv` and `stop_loss_warnings.csv` where trust/stop-loss claims are made | Enables trust/stop-loss burden, compliance, and reason-code analysis | Trust/stop-loss analysis cannot be thesis-ready |
| Shuffled-RegimeRisk negative control | Tests whether temporal alignment matters | A7 temporal-signal claim weakened |
| Random-risk negative control | Tests whether arbitrary risk labels perform similarly | A7 temporal-signal claim weakened or blocked |
| With/without trust allocator comparison | Tests trust allocator contribution | Trust allocation contribution remains unproven |
| With/without stop-loss comparison | Tests stop-loss contribution and burden | Stop-loss claims remain diagnostic |
| Over-abstention / fallback burden analysis | Prevents hiding conservative failures | Improvement claim weakened if cost is excessive |
| Risk-error alignment and failure-explanation tables | Supports interpretability claims | Interpretability claim downgraded |
| Negative-result notes for non-improvement, random-control parity, over-conservative behavior, or stress-only benefit | Prevents result cherry-picking | Claim-evidence matrix must mark weakened claim |
| Layer 10 RegimeRisk dashboard/card/export lineage | Ensures dashboard traceability | Reporting/export claim incomplete |
| Layer 0 claim-evidence entry | Ensures claim-safe thesis wording | Thesis wording blocked or diagnostic-only |

### 10. Baselines and Comparators

A7 must compare against a sufficient baseline ladder, or explicitly record missing baseline coverage.

| Comparator | Required matching | A7 use | Missingness handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw / accept-all decoder | Same dataset, split, model, window sequence, seed/config where applicable | Lowest raw reference; shows static decoder behavior | If absent, A7 cannot situate against raw baseline |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Same decoder outputs and split-safe calibration | Probability-reliability context | If absent, calibration-dependent RegimeRisk features are invalid or diagnostic |
| A2 simple registered threshold | Same threshold registry and matched operating point | Static confidence-threshold comparator | If absent, static-threshold limitation claim weakened |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | Same uncertainty/selective records and operating point | Uncertainty/reject baseline and feature context | If absent, A7 cannot claim superiority over selective prediction |
| A4 longer-window / voting / averaging / ordinary ensemble controls | Same source sequence and ordinary-control configuration except ablated control | Ordinary temporal/ensemble comparator | If absent, ordinary temporal-control comparison weakened |
| A5 IHARQ-lite | Same ordered windows, IHARQ config, action-cost/request budget, threshold registry, and metric dictionary | Direct regime-unaware baseline | Required for core A7 improvement claim |
| A6 evidence-quality estimator | Same source records and legal quality features where implemented | Optional quality-aware comparator/context | Not required for core A7; cannot replace A5 baseline |
| Confidence-only risk proxy | Same sequence and decision budget | Tests whether RegimeRisk adds beyond confidence trend | Diagnostic-only if not matched |
| Entropy-only / margin-only / disagreement-only risk proxy | Same uncertainty records and budget | Tests whether full RegimeRisk beats simple uncertainty proxies | Diagnostic-only if not matched |
| No-regime policy/context | Same context excluding regime/risk fields | Separates regime contribution in downstream contexts | Downstream only; policy phases must validate |
| Shuffled-RegimeRisk | Same records, shuffled temporal risk/regime assignment under declared procedure | Negative control for temporal alignment | Improvement claim weakened if missing; downgraded if competitive |
| Random-risk score | Same records and decision budget, random risk under declared seed/config | Negative control for arbitrary risk labels | Improvement claim weakened if missing; downgraded if competitive |
| RegimeRisk without trust allocator | Same temporal features, trust disabled | Local contribution of trust allocation | Requires confirmation of local sub-ablation label |
| RegimeRisk without stop-loss | Same temporal features, stop-loss disabled | Local contribution and burden of stop-loss | Requires confirmation of local sub-ablation label |

### 11. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

A7 comparisons must use a strict matched-comparison envelope. Any key that is not applicable must be explicitly marked `not_applicable`; any missing required key downgrades the affected row.

```text

selective_prediction_record_id where applicable
iharq_config_id
iharq_decision_record_id / iharq_trace_record_id where applicable
evidence_quality_record_id where applicable
rolling_window_config_id
regime_config_id
risk_threshold_config_id
trust_allocator_config_id
stop_loss_config_id

```

| Comparison | Required matched condition | Claim status if unmatched |
|---|---|---|
| IHARQ-only A5 vs IHARQ + RegimeRisk A7 | Same ordered sequence, split, decoder, calibration, threshold registry, IHARQ config, request/evidence/action-cost budget, and metric dictionary | Diagnostic-only; no A7 improvement claim |
| Full RegimeRisk vs shuffled RegimeRisk | Same records/sequence except declared shuffle assignment; seed/config logged | If shuffled is competitive, temporal-trust signal claim downgraded |
| Full RegimeRisk vs random risk score | Same records and budget except random-risk generation; seed/config logged | If random is competitive, RegimeRisk-specific claim downgraded |
| With vs without trust allocator | Same temporal features, risk thresholds, and stop-loss config except trust allocation disabled | Diagnostic-only if other configs differ |
| With vs without stop-loss | Same temporal features and trust allocation except stop-loss disabled | Diagnostic-only if stop-loss cost/budget differs without disclosure |
| Clean vs stress-conditioned context | Same source IDs and declared stress profile/schedule | Stress-only/proxy-only; no real fatigue or safety claim |
| Simulation/embodiment-context variants | Same source sequence, simulator/replay configuration, and embodiment mode where applicable | Simulation-only/proxy-only; diagnostic-only if mapping incomplete |

### 12. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

A7 metric families are allowed only with metric dictionary linkage or diagnostic-only marking. Exact metric definitions, denominators, aggregation rules, confidence intervals, and statistical tests remain `requires_confirmation: true` unless finalized by the supplied sources or a later v1.0 run-matrix document.

| Metric family | Purpose | Required boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal risk trend summaries | Summarize regime risk, volatility-like trend, drawdown-like trend, drift-risk, fatigue-like-risk, dropout-risk, and failure-risk behavior | Operational/proxy temporal trust only |
| Risk-error alignment | Tests whether high-risk periods align with error bursts, wrong accepts, fallback clusters, high-confidence wrong cases, or simulated unsafe proxies where legally evaluated | Correctness/outcomes are evaluation-only unless legally past |
| High-risk precision / recall | Measures whether flagged high-risk states correspond to later/evaluation-only failures where labels are available | Not clinical diagnosis |
| Risk calibration / risk-coverage curves | Tests calibration of risk score and risk/coverage tradeoff | Metric dictionary and denominator required |
| Wrong-accept reduction | Tests whether A7 reduces accepted incorrect outputs compared with A5/A2/A3/A4 baselines | Matched coverage/cost required; no real safety claim |
| High-risk accepted-error rate | Measures accepted error behavior inside high-risk bands | Proxy decoder/evaluation metric only |
| Fallback, no-action, unsafe recommendation rate | Tracks conservative action burden | Over-abstention must be negative-result visible |
| Request-evidence burden / evidence cost | Tracks added evidence requests or delays | Must not hide delay/cost of regime-aware behavior |
| Stop-loss activation and compliance | Tests stop-loss trigger burden, reason-code lineage, and whether recommendations are followed in declared comparisons | Proxy stop-loss warning; not medical safety stop-loss |
| False stop-loss / over-abstention burden | Detects valid-action blocking or excessive conservative behavior | Must be reported as negative result where harmful |
| Recovery latency | Measures how quickly risk state or stop-loss status recovers after instability/stress where valid | Stress/simulation tags required when applicable |
| Trust allocation stability | Measures trusted-set membership, trust-score trend, and trust-band changes | Requires `TrustStateRecord` or `trust_scores.csv` lineage if independently claimed |
| Regime transition frequency / consistency | Describes regime label transitions and stability | No true physiological regime claim unless source-supported and claim-safe |
| Early-warning lead time | Measures lead time before failure/stress/proxy unsafe event where causal evaluation is valid | Must prove no future leakage; otherwise diagnostic-only |
| Shuffled/random negative-control performance | Tests whether temporal-trust structure adds signal beyond arbitrary risk | Required for strong A7 improvement claim |
| Card/export trace-completeness | Measures Layer 10 traceability from cards/figures/tables back to source records | Dashboard-derived, not primary evidence |

Forbidden metric classes include clinical fatigue diagnosis accuracy, real patient-safety rate, medical-device readiness score, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle-stimulation control quality, real deployment readiness, or any metric name that implies validated physiological or therapeutic effect.

### 13. Split, Leakage, Temporal, Policy, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint family | A7 requirement | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal cutoff | RegimeRisk decision-time features may use only current and past values under a declared temporal cutoff | Future-leakage rows blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Split legality | Rolling histories must not cross forbidden train/validation/test or subject/session split boundaries | Block thesis-facing use; mark leakage warning |
| Correctness/outcome separation | Labels, correctness, rewards, stress outcomes, and embodiment outcomes are evaluation-only unless legally known in the past under a declared protocol | Decision-time leakage blocks A7 claim support |
| Calibration/threshold legality | Calibration methods and thresholds must not be retuned on test outcomes for RegimeRisk | Diagnostic-only or invalid comparison |
| IHARQ token integrity | Stored Layer 4 tokens must remain canonical: `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, `unsafe` | Alias gaps or missing reason codes downgrade affected histories |
| Evidence-quality variant tags | Rule-derived and learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants must be distinguishable | Missing producer tag downgrades A7 feature-context rows |
| Regime-aware rerun | If Layer 5 changes Layer 4 behavior, original and adjusted decisions, regime state ID, trigger, threshold/rule change, reason code, and outcome if available must be logged | Unlogged rerun cannot support A7 comparison |
| Trust allocation | Independent trust timelines require `TrustStateRecord`; compact trust summaries may remain inside `RegimeStateRecord` if no independent timeline is claimed | Missing `TrustStateRecord` downgrades trust timeline claims |
| Stop-loss logic | Stop-loss trigger, severity, affected IDs, recommendation, cooldown/recovery, reason codes, and source evidence must be saved | Stop-loss claim diagnostic-only if unlogged |
| Stress context | Stress profiles/schedules can be used only where official stress artifacts exist and are tagged | Stress-conditioned proxy-only; Layer 8 / Phase 9 produce stress evidence used by A12 |
| Simulation context | Transition/reward/policy/closed-loop records are downstream-only unless official phases produced them | Simulation-only; no deployment claim |
| Embodiment context | Embodiment state/outcome records are optional downstream proxy context | Embodiment-proxy only; Layer 9 produces embodiment evidence used by A13 |
| Dashboard boundary | Layer 10 views/cards/exports cannot feed back as RegimeRisk features | Dashboard-derived source use invalidates comparison |

The global top-level ID remains A7. Local sub-ablation labels below are `inferred_candidate` labels for v0.1 planning only and require final confirmation before becoming a fixed v1.0 run matrix.

| Local candidate label | Purpose | Status |

| `A7.1_regime_label_only` | Test regime label contribution without full risk/trust/stop-loss bundle | `inferred_candidate`; `requires_confirmation: true` |

| `A7.3_full_RegimeStateRecord` | Test full causal RegimeStateRecord context | `inferred_candidate`; `requires_confirmation: true` |
| `A7.4_trust_allocator_disabled` | Test contribution of trust allocator/trusted-set membership | `inferred_candidate`; requires matching |
| `A7.5_stop_loss_disabled` | Test stop-loss contribution and burden | `inferred_candidate`; requires matching |
| `A7.6_shuffled_RegimeRisk_negative_control` | Test whether temporal alignment matters | Strongly recommended negative control; exact procedure requires confirmation |
| `A7.7_random_risk_negative_control` | Test whether arbitrary risk performs similarly | Strongly recommended negative control; exact seed/procedure requires confirmation |
| `A7.8_stress_conditioned_context` | Stratify RegimeRisk under stress profiles where official stress records exist | `downstream_context_only` for A7; A12 claim context requires Layer 8 / Phase 9 stress evidence |

No local label may be used to create A14 or a new global ablation. Local labels must inherit A7 source lineage, matched keys, metric dictionary references, and Layer 0 claim-safety tags.

### 15. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 may read and render A7 source records after validation. It must not mutate upstream records, recompute hidden alternative metrics without lineage, tune RegimeRisk thresholds, repair split leakage, or convert dashboard views into primary evidence.

| Layer 10 output/view | Required A7 source lineage | Required warning behavior |
|---|---|---|
| RegimeRisk timeline view | `RegimeStateRecord`, `regime_timelines.csv`, source window IDs, config hash, temporal cutoff | Warn on missing causal cutoff, split leakage, missing source IDs, or diagnostic-only status |
| Trust-score / trust-state view | `TrustStateRecord` and/or `trust_scores.csv`, trust allocator config, source RegimeState IDs | Warn if independent trust timeline is claimed but `TrustStateRecord` is absent |
| Stop-loss warning panel | `stop_loss_warnings.csv`, trigger/reason/source IDs, severity, recommendation, cooldown/recovery fields | Warn on unlogged trigger, missing reason codes, or over-abstention burden |
| Regime-aware vs regime-unaware comparison table | `MatchedComparisonReport`, Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A5 baseline source IDs | Warn when matched keys differ or metric dictionary ID is missing |
| Negative-control panel | Shuffled/random-risk control records, seeds/configs, source IDs | Warn if negative controls are missing or perform similarly to full RegimeRisk |
| Risk-error alignment figure | `RegimeStateRecord`, evaluation-only labels/outcomes, metric dictionary IDs | Warn that correctness/outcome fields are evaluation-only and not decision-time features |
| Over-abstention/fallback burden panel | IHARQ decision/fallback/stop-loss records and cost/request metrics | Warn if wrong-accept reduction is achieved only through excessive no-action/fallback burden |
| Stress-regime context panel | `StressProfileRecord` / schedule plus RegimeRisk records where available | Must show stress-conditioned/proxy-only tags; A12 ownership preserved |
| Embodiment-risk context panel | Layer 9 embodiment records plus RegimeRisk source IDs where available | Must show embodiment-proxy/simulation-only tags; A13 ownership preserved |
| `RegimeCard` | Source record IDs, metrics, matched reports, negative results, limitations, claim tags, export manifest pointer | Card cannot strengthen claims beyond source evidence |
| Reproducibility manifest | Source files, output files, schema versions, hashes, configs, seeds, metric dictionary IDs, limitation tags, dashboard/card IDs | Must preserve unresolved issue IDs and diagnostic-only flags |

Layer 10 outputs required for A7 are read-only derived reporting artifacts. The dashboard may surface missingness, warnings, traceability, and limitation labels, but it cannot be the producer of RegimeRisk evidence.

### 16. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

#### 16.1 Allowed bounded A7 claims

A7 may support claim-safe wording such as:

| Allowed claim family | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| RegimeRisk temporal trust monitoring was evaluated on public EEG proxy sequences | Valid causal `RegimeStateRecord` lineage and public-data limitation tags |
| Regime-aware IHARQ changed reliability behavior compared with matched regime-unaware IHARQ | Matched A5 vs A7 comparison and metric dictionary lineage |
| A7 improved wrong-accept behavior under matched cost/coverage | Matched metrics, negative controls, and over-abstention reporting |
| A7 provided interpretable temporal failure timelines | Regime timelines, risk-error alignment, source IDs, and RegimeCard/dashboard lineage |
| Stop-loss warnings exposed conservative fallback/no-action behavior | `stop_loss_warnings.csv`, reason codes, source IDs, and burden metrics |
| Trust allocation summarized changing evidence-source/model reliability | `TrustStateRecord` or `trust_scores.csv` lineage where independently claimed |
| A7 was diagnostic-only or not beneficial under tested conditions | Negative-result notes and limitation tags |
| Stress-conditioned or simulation-only RegimeRisk behavior was observed | Official stress/simulation records and explicit stress/simulation tags |

#### 16.2 Forbidden A7 claims

A7 must not claim or imply:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle-stimulation control;
- real-time deployment readiness or real assistive-control safety;
- diagnosis of clinical fatigue, neurological state, or patient state;
- validated physiological stress detection;
- guaranteed harm prevention;
- RegimeRisk as a medical or clinical risk controller;
- dashboard-rendered cards as primary empirical evidence;
- stress or embodiment proxy outputs as real physiological outcomes.

#### 16.3 Required limitation labels

A7 records, evaluation artifacts, dashboard views, cards, exports, and claim-evidence entries should carry relevant tags such as:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_proxy
temporal_trust_proxy
regime_label_computational
```

### 17. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

A7 must preserve negative results rather than hiding or over-interpreting them.

| Negative or weak result | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| A7 does not improve over A5 IHARQ-lite | Record as negative or baseline-sufficient result; A7 may still be useful for interpretability if timelines are traceable |
| A2/A3/A4 already match or outperform A7 | Treat upstream baseline as sufficient under tested conditions; do not claim RegimeRisk benefit |
| Shuffled/random risk performs similarly to full RegimeRisk | Downgrade temporal-signal and RegimeRisk-specific claims; revise or mark diagnostic-only |
| Wrong accepts decrease only through excessive fallback/no-action/stop-loss | Report over-abstention and cost burden; do not present as unqualified improvement |
| Trust allocator is unstable or uninterpretable | Downgrade trust allocation claims; preserve as failure/diagnostic note |
| Stop-loss blocks many valid actions | Preserve conservative-failure or over-abstention negative-result note |
| Regime labels do not align with error bursts or failure clusters | Interpret as diagnostic-only temporal labeling failure or non-informative signal |
| A7 helps only under synthetic stress | Mark stress-conditioned/proxy-only; no clean-public-data or real physiological claim |
| `TrustStateRecord`, metric dictionary, or matched keys are missing | Block thesis-ready trust/improvement claims and mark diagnostic-only |
| Phase 5 records are valid but dashboard/card lineage incomplete | A7 may be empirical but not dashboard/reproducibility complete |

Baseline sufficiency rule: if Phase 4 IHARQ-lite, Phase 3 selective prediction, or Phase 2/4 ordinary controls already provide sufficient reliability behavior under matched comparisons, the thesis may report that RegimeRisk was evaluated and found unnecessary, too costly, or diagnostic-only under tested conditions. That is a valid scientific outcome when negative-result notes and claim downgrades are explicit.

### 18. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers and Open Issues

#### 18.1 Diagnostic-only downgrade triggers

A7 rows, comparisons, figures, cards, or claims must be downgraded to diagnostic-only when any of the following apply:

| Trigger | A7 consequence |
|---|---|
| Ordered windows differ between variants | No A7 improvement claim |
| Temporal cutoff differs without declared reason | Diagnostic-only or invalid comparison |
| Split roles, label budgets, preprocessing, label maps, decoder/model family, calibration, threshold, or IHARQ configs differ outside the ablated factor | Diagnostic-only |
| Future labels, correctness, reward, stress outcome, embodiment outcome, or dashboard-derived metrics enter decision-time features | Block thesis-facing use |
| `RegimeStateRecord` lacks source IDs, causal cutoff, risk config, or validation status | A7 core invalid or diagnostic-only |
| `TrustStateRecord` is missing for independently consumed trust timelines | Trust timeline claims incomplete/diagnostic |
| Stop-loss trigger/recommendation/reason-code/source IDs are missing | Stop-loss claim diagnostic-only |
| Shuffled/random negative controls are missing where an A7 temporal-signal or improvement claim is made | Claim weakened; strong A7 claim blocked |
| Shuffled/random controls perform similarly to full RegimeRisk | RegimeRisk-specific signal claim downgraded |
| Metric dictionary ID is missing | Metric/table/claim diagnostic-only |
| `MC-003` action-token alias or reason-code issue affects IHARQ histories | Affected A7 comparison diagnostic-only |
| `MC-001` trial identity ambiguity prevents ordered-sequence matching | Affected rows diagnostic-only |
| `MC-002` EvidenceQualityRecord producer variant is unclear | Feature-context rows diagnostic-only |
| Dashboard view/card is used as upstream evidence | Invalid source use; claim blocked |
| Stress/embodiment context is mixed with clean evidence without tags | Diagnostic-only; claim-safety warning |
| Forbidden clinical, medical, real-safety, deployment, or rehabilitation wording is attempted | Layer 0 blocks or rewrites claim |

#### 18.2 Open issues and requires-confirmation items

| Issue | Type | A7 handling |
|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` TrialRecord / trial identity ambiguity | schema / matched-comparison gap | Use validated `WindowRecord` and existing trial/window fields; unmatched sequences diagnostic-only |
| `MC-002` EvidenceQualityRecord variant ownership | producer-consumer ambiguity | Require producer-variant tags for rule-derived vs learned evidence-quality fields |
| `MC-003` `combine` versus `combine_evidence` action-token alias conflict | alias conflict | Preserve canonical Layer 4 token; do not rewrite silently; affected histories diagnostic-only if unresolved |
| `MC-004` ReadinessContextRecord ownership boundary | producer-consumer ambiguity | A7 may prepare RegimeRisk context; Layer 6 owns readiness context except run-specific candidates |
| `MC-007` DashboardMetricRecord mapping | dashboard boundary risk | Layer 10 dashboard metrics remain derived/read-only and cannot be primary evidence |
| `MC-008` MetricDictionaryEntry schema/path gap | metric-definition gap | Every metric requires dictionary reference; exact definitions remain confirmation items |
| `MC-009` Repository path / storage-home resolution | repository/path gap | Use source-supported canonical homes as candidates; exact final paths deferred |
| `MC-010` Lifecycle/schema maturity | schema maturity gap | Preserve planned/draft_schema until validators and final manifests promote rows |
| `MC-011` Layer 10 evidence boundary | claim-safety / dashboard boundary | Dashboard cannot mutate or create primary evidence |
| `MC-012` Layer 0 evidence boundary | claim-safety boundary | Layer 0 governs claims/limitations; does not produce empirical evidence |
| Conditional `TrustStateRecord` requirement | schema/conditional artifact gap | Required only when independent trust timelines or per-target trust views are claimed |
| Exact local A7 sub-ablation numbering | v0.1/v1.0 boundary | Candidate labels only; final numbering requires confirmation |
| Exact negative-control procedure | v0.1/v1.0 boundary | Shuffled/random controls required conceptually; exact seeds/procedure deferred |
| Exact metric denominators and statistical tests | metric-definition gap | `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Exact dashboard routes, card IDs, and export filenames | dashboard/path gap | `requires_confirmation: true` |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` vs `ClaimEvidenceManifest` naming | alias/schema ambiguity | Preserve both names until final source resolves |

### 19. Handoff to Later Protocol Sections

A7 prepares temporal-trust context for later sections but must not silently claim their results.

| Later section | A7 handoff | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A8 — Learning-to-defer | Supplies RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss context that a later deferral comparison may consume | A7 does not validate deferral or produce `DeferralRecord` |
| A9 — Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Supplies temporal context for learned readiness-policy evaluation | A7 does not validate supervised policy or pseudo-label policy maturity |
| A10/A11 — Bandit/RL | Supplies simulation-compatible risk/trust context where official simulation records exist | A7 does not validate bandit/RL policy improvement |
| A12 — StressForge | Supplies regime/timeline context to stratify stress-conditioned robustness | Stress evidence belongs to A12 and remains synthetic/proxy |
| A13 — Embodiment demo | Supplies optional temporal risk context for simulated/proxy embodiment gating | Embodiment evidence belongs to A13 and remains simulation/proxy-only |
| Metric-family section | Needs exact A7 metric dictionary entries, denominators, directions, and aggregation rules | v1.0/final-run confirmation required |
| Matched-comparison rules | Should incorporate A7 temporal sequence, regime config, trust allocator, stop-loss, and negative-control keys | Missing keys diagnostic-only |
| Diagnostic-only downgrade rules | Should include A7 temporal leakage, negative-control, trust-state, stop-loss, dashboard-boundary, and clinical-claim triggers | Layer 0 governance required |
| Layer 10 export/dashboard obligations | Should define final RegimeRisk pages/cards/export manifests | Dashboard is derived/read-only |
| Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries | Should finalize A7 allowed/forbidden wording and limitation inheritance | Strictest source limitation controls thesis wording |

A8 is a scientific evaluation-use identifier. It is not Phase 7, not Layer 6, not a module, not a record owner, not a dashboard page, not a clinical triage system, not an expert-handoff validation, not a real patient-safety controller, and not a deployment-readiness claim. ### 3. Target Purpose and Scientific Question

A8 asks whether learning to defer is a strong enough routing baseline to explain the observed benefit of more complex readiness-policy components. It is a criticism-defense section: if a simpler deferral router can match supervised Adaptive-IHARQ under the same cost, coverage, fallback, split, and source-record constraints, the protocol must say so instead of hiding the simpler-baseline sufficiency result.

The primary A8 scientific question is:

> Under matched public-data source lineage, split/legal-feature constraints, readiness context, cost model, fallback-source availability, action-space legality, and metric dictionary entries, does a learning-to-defer policy improve the direct-versus-defer trade-off beyond raw, calibrated, threshold, uncertainty/selective, ordinary aggregation, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality, and temporal-trust baselines — or is deferral merely an adequate simpler alternative to supervised Adaptive-IHARQ?

A8 may support the following bounded evaluation questions when source records exist:

| Question | A8 treatment | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Can deferral reduce wrong accepted predictions at acceptable coverage or cost? | Compare direct prediction, threshold/selective baselines, IHARQ-lite, A6/A7 contexts where valid, and A8 under matched cost/coverage | Proxy readiness only; no real safety claim |
| Is a learned deferral router better than a simple confidence or uncertainty rejector? | Compare A8 against A2 and A3 at matched coverage and/or matched expected cost | Deferral/routing baseline; not clinical triage |
| Is deferral different from waiting or longer-window aggregation? | Compare A8 against A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls where available | Ordinary controls remain controls, not policy deferral unless `DeferralRecord` exists |
| Does deferral explain most of supervised Adaptive-IHARQ's benefit? | Compare A8 against A9 under matched context, cost, legal actions, and held-out evaluation | Baseline-sufficiency result must be stated honestly |
| Does deferral become excessive or useless? | Report over-deferral, no-action/safe-hold burden, fallback burden, missed-opportunity cost, and coverage collapse | Negative result or weakened claim, not hidden failure |
| Does temporal trust improve deferral? | Compare regime-aware and regime-unaware deferral variants only when Phase 5 records are legal and matched | Temporal-trust proxy; no clinical fatigue or patient-state diagnosis |
| Does a supervisor-proxy route help? | Use only explicitly labeled simulation/proxy/oracle fallback routes and never treat them as real expert handoff | Simulation/proxy-only, requires clear limitation tags |

#### 6.1 C0–C4 capability-tier relationship

| C3 — Bandit/RL simulation layer | A8 can be a fixed non-bandit baseline for A10/A11 | Simulation-only downstream context; not core A8 unless explicitly scoped |
| C4 — Stress/embodiment/dashboard final demonstration | A8 deferral traces may be consumed by stress/embodiment/dashboard demos | C4 does not convert A8 into real-world embodied safety evidence |

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

A8 must be compared against simpler baselines and nearby policy variants with matched source records. A deferral result is not thesis-ready if it is compared only against a weak or unmatched baseline.

| Comparator | Required status for A8 | Matching requirement | Interpretation if A8 wins | Interpretation if comparator matches or wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 direct prediction / accept-all | Required | Same dataset, subject/session, trial/window, split, model, seed, config, label map | Deferral may reduce wrong accepts or cost relative to direct prediction | Direct prediction sufficient; deferral burden may be unjustified |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Required where calibrated records exist | Same prediction source and calibration split lineage | Deferral adds routing value beyond calibrated scores | Calibration alone may be sufficient at the chosen operating point |
| A2 simple registered threshold | Required | Same threshold-selection split, coverage/cost target, threshold registry ID | Learning-to-defer adds value beyond simple confidence rejection | Simple threshold is sufficient; A8 claim weakened |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | Required where uncertainty/selective records exist | Same uncertainty feature set, selection split, coverage/cost target | Deferral adds target-aware routing beyond rejection | Uncertainty/selective prediction is a sufficient baseline |
| A4 longer-window / multi-window / voting / averaging / ordinary ensemble controls | Required where available | Same trial/window identity, delay burden, aggregation config, model family, seed | Deferral adds value beyond ordinary evidence accumulation | Ordinary controls are sufficient; A8 complexity weakened |
| A5 IHARQ-lite | Required | Same IHARQ config, threshold references, reason-code/action-token map, source IDs | Deferral improves or complements rule evidence verification | IHARQ-lite sufficient; A8 may be optional |
| A6 evidence-quality estimator | Optional but important where available | Same evidence-quality feature legality, target construction, split, cost config | Deferral uses or improves learned quality signal | Evidence-quality alone may be enough; A8 target route not justified |
| A7 RegimeRisk temporal trust | Optional where valid | Same temporal cutoff, regime/trust context, source windows, cost config | Regime-aware deferral may add value under unstable regimes | RegimeRisk context not needed for deferral; A7/A8 interaction weakened |
| A9 supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Required where A9 exists; otherwise future handoff | Same readiness context, cost model, action-space version, legality masks, policy-training/evaluation split, seed | A8 is a strong simpler competitor; if it also beats A9, A9 claims must be narrowed | A9 adds value beyond deferral; A8 remains a necessary baseline |
| A10/A11 bandit/RL policies | Downstream_context_only | Simulation-only matched environment/reward/update controls | A8 can serve as fixed non-adaptive baseline | Not a core A8 claim; belongs to A10/A11 |

#### 9.1 Baseline-sufficiency rule

If A8 matches A9 or higher-complexity policies under matched cost, coverage, wrong-accept, and burden metrics, the protocol must state that learning-to-defer is a strong sufficient baseline for the tested setting. This is not a failure of the protocol. It is a thesis-relevant negative or simplifying result.

#### 9.2 Forbidden or misleading comparisons

A8 must not be declared superior when:

- comparator records are unmatched or missing;
- fallback/source availability differs across variants;
- A8 has access to target labels, future correctness, future reward, future windows, oracle costs, or dashboard-derived inspection notes at decision time;
- cost weights are selected after seeing held-out test outcomes;
- supervisor-proxy or oracle fallback is treated as real expert triage;
- training/adaptation curves are compared against frozen baselines;
- dashboard-filtered subsets hide high-burden or high-error deferral cases.

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

A8 comparisons are thesis-ready only when the required key envelope is present or an explicitly justified key is marked `not_applicable`.

| Key family | Required A8 fields | Status if missing |
|---|---|---|
| Source identity | dataset ID, subject ID, session ID, trial ID, window ID, parent trial/window where applicable | Missing source identity makes comparison invalid or diagnostic-only |
| Split and leakage identity | split ID, train/validation/test role, calibration split ID, threshold-selection split ID, policy-training split ID, target-construction split ID | Missing split identity blocks thesis-ready A8 |
| Model and decoder identity | model ID, model family, prediction record IDs, preprocessing ID, label-map ID | Missing model identity weakens or invalidates baseline matching |
| Calibration/uncertainty/threshold identity | calibration ID, uncertainty feature set ID, threshold registry ID, selective-prediction config ID | Missing fields downgrade A1–A3/A8 comparisons |
| IHARQ/evidence identity | IHARQ config ID, reason-code version, action-token map, evidence-quality variant ID, fallback/unsafe source IDs | Missing fields downgrade A5/A6/A8 comparisons |
| Temporal/regime identity | causal cutoff, sequence/window-history ID, regime state ID, trust state IDs, stop-loss status | Required only for regime-aware A8; otherwise `not_applicable` |
| A8 policy identity | learning-to-defer policy ID, deferral config ID, deferral target manifest ID, deferral reason vocabulary ID, context hash, config hash | Missing A8 identity blocks A8 evidence |
| Fallback/cost identity | fallback source ID, fallback availability, fallback cost config ID, cost model version, direct-versus-defer cost table ID | Missing cost/fallback identity makes deferral claims diagnostic-only |
| Action legality identity | action-space version, legality-mask ID, request budget ID, wait/replay availability ID, no-action/safe-hold rule ID | Missing legality identity weakens or invalidates policy comparisons |
| Randomization/run identity | seed, run ID, config hash, policy artifact hash, evaluation report ID | Missing run identity blocks reproducibility claims |
| Downstream-only identity | stress profile/schedule ID, simulation environment ID, reward config ID, embodiment mode ID | Required only when stress/simulation/embodiment claims are made |
| Reporting identity | metric dictionary ID, matched-comparison report ID, dashboard export ID, negative-result note ID, claim-evidence ID | Missing reporting identity downgrades Layer 10/Layer 0 use |

#### 10.1 Matchability status vocabulary

| Status | A8 meaning |
|---|---|
| `fully_matched` | Required keys are present; comparison may support thesis-ready bounded claims if metric and claim gates also pass |
| `partially_matched` | Some non-critical keys are missing or justified; claim must be weakened |
| `unmatched_diagnostic` | Comparison is useful for debugging but cannot support A8 superiority/sufficiency claims |
| `invalid` | Leakage, source mutation, target/fallback/cost ambiguity, or illegal feature use invalidates the comparison |
| `not_applicable` | A key belongs to downstream simulation/stress/embodiment context not claimed by core A8 |

### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

A8 metrics must be presented by family, denominator, interpretation, and limitation. Exact final metric dictionary entries remain required for thesis-ready reporting.

| Metric family | Metrics | Required records | Direction / interpretation | Primary or secondary | Metric dictionary status | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deferral quality and burden | deferral rate, non-deferral/direct rate, deferral target distribution, deferral reason distribution, over-deferral rate, no-action/safe-hold rate, request/wait rate | `DeferralRecord`, target manifest, reason vocabulary, action-space/legality files | Lower burden is not always better; interpret jointly with wrong-accept, coverage, and cost | Primary | Source-supported family; exact denominators require metric dictionary confirmation | Proxy routing only; no real triage |
| Fallback/request burden | fallback rate, fallback-source usage, request-more-evidence burden, fallback unavailable rate, missed fallback cases | `DeferralRecord`, fallback-source log, cost config, IHARQ/fallback records | Lower burden may indicate efficiency or under-use; must be cost-contextualized | Primary | Source-supported family; exact definitions require confirmation | Fallback source may be proxy/simulation-only |
| Coverage and retained performance | coverage, accepted-trial accuracy, retained error, direct accepted count, deferred count | Prediction/calibration/selective records, `DeferralRecord`, labels for evaluation only | More coverage is not inherently better if wrong accepts increase | Primary | Source-supported family; dictionary required | Public EEG/proxy evaluation only |
| Wrong-accept and high-risk accept | wrong-accept rate among accepted actions, high-confidence wrong accepted rate, high-risk accepted error, accepted error under deferral | Prediction/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk records, `DeferralRecord`, evaluation labels | Lower is better when coverage/cost are matched | Primary | Source-supported family; denominators require dictionary | Not real patient-safety metric |
| Direct-versus-defer cost | expected direct cost, expected defer cost, realized proxy cost where available, matched-cost delta, cost-weight sensitivity | Cost config, direct-versus-defer table, `DeferralRecord`, evaluation labels | Lower proxy cost is better only under declared cost weights | Primary | Source-supported family; cost weights require confirmation | Cost model is computational/proxy, not clinical utility |
| Matched-coverage / matched-cost delta | delta wrong-accept at matched coverage, delta coverage at matched cost, delta fallback burden at matched cost | Matched-comparison report, metric dictionary, source records | Used to compare A8 with A2/A3/A5/A9 fairly | Primary | Required by framework; final test/statistic deferred | Unmatched deltas are diagnostic-only |
| Action distribution / policy stability | action distribution, action entropy, seed stability, subject/session stability, collapse-to-defer/collapse-to-direct indicators | `PolicyActionRecord` where emitted, `DeferralRecord`, policy artifact hash, seed/run IDs | Stability supports reproducibility; collapse may be negative result | Secondary | Source-supported family; exact stability metric requires confirmation | Does not imply deployment reliability |
| Temporal/regime-aware deferral | deferral by regime band, stop-loss compliance, risk-conditioned deferral rate | `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `DeferralRecord` | Useful only for optional A7/A8 interaction | Secondary / optional | Requires A7 metric dictionary linkage | No clinical fatigue or patient-state claim |
| Dashboard/reproducibility completeness | record completeness, matched-key completeness, card-source completeness, export manifest completeness, warning coverage | Layer 10-readable source records, manifests, matched reports | Higher completeness supports traceability, not empirical superiority | Secondary | Required for Layer 10; schema/path gaps preserved | Dashboard metric is not primary evidence |
| Claim-evidence completeness | limitation tags present, negative-result note coverage, diagnostic-only flags, claim-evidence linkage | Layer 0/Layer 10 claim-evidence artifacts | Required for final thesis-safe wording | Secondary | Requires final claim-evidence mapping confirmation | Governance evidence, not empirical performance |

#### 11.1 Metrics explicitly not allowed as A8 thesis-ready metrics

A8 must not introduce or display metrics named or interpreted as clinical triage success, expert handoff efficacy, patient safety rate, medical-device readiness score, rehabilitation improvement, real-time deployment safety, real FES control success, real muscle stimulation correctness, clinical fatigue diagnosis, or patient-specific outcome improvement. If a metric could be mistaken for one of these classes, it must be renamed and bounded as public-data/proxy, simulation-only, or diagnostic-only.

### 12. Split, Leakage, Threshold, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint area | A8 rule | Diagnostic-only / invalid trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Split discipline | Deferral policy training, target construction, cost tuning, threshold selection, and evaluation must use declared train/validation/test roles | Test-set tuning or post-hoc threshold/cost selection invalidates affected A8 claims |
| Decision-time feature legality | `ReadinessContextRecord` must contain only information available at decision time; true label, decoder correctness, future evidence, future reward, future embodiment outcome, and oracle costs are forbidden as policy-visible features | Hidden evaluation-only fields in context make the run invalid |
| Target construction | Deferral labels or pseudo-labels must come from declared cost/proxy construction with source IDs and split-safe target partitions | Undeclared target construction downgrades to diagnostic-only |
| Fallback/source declaration | Every deferral target must point to a declared fallback, safer model, request route, wait/no-action/safe-hold route, or explicitly labeled supervisor proxy | Ambiguous “defer” without target/fallback/cost source blocks A8 |
| Supervisor proxy and oracle routes | Supervisor/oracle/proxy fallback may be used only if explicitly labeled as proxy/simulation/evaluation-only and not exposed as real expert availability | Treating proxy/oracle as real clinical handoff invalidates claim |
| Threshold and operating points | A2/A3 thresholds and coverage/cost operating points must be registered before held-out evaluation | Post-hoc operating-point selection downgrades or invalidates |
| Policy frozen/update separation | Core A8 is frozen/offline by default; update-enabled mutation requires declared simulation mode and `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Untraced update in held-out evaluation invalidates frozen-policy comparison |
| Cost/reward sensitivity | Cost weights must be versioned; if conclusions depend strongly on weights, claim must be weakened | Unversioned or outcome-selected weights downgrade to diagnostic-only |
| Stress controls | Stress-conditioned deferral belongs to A12 unless explicitly scoped; clean/stressed source pairing and stress schedule IDs are required | Stress rows without stress lineage are diagnostic-only |
| Embodiment controls | Embodiment-aware deferral consequences belong to A13/Layer 9 and remain proxy/simulation-only | Embodiment claims without mapping/safety gate/outcome lineage are invalid |
| Dashboard boundary | Layer 10 may display/filter/warn/export but must not retune policies, create targets, or repair missing records | Dashboard-derived hidden evidence invalidates affected claims |

Local sub-ablations may be used only as children of A8. They must remain local, source-linked, and non-authoritative until confirmed. They must not become new global A IDs.

| Sub-ablation ID | Parent global ID | Variant definition | Required config difference | Required records | Metric purpose | Claim status |

| A8.2 | A8 | Uncertainty-aware deferral router | Adds entropy/margin/disagreement/selective-prediction features | A8.1 records plus `UncertaintyRecord`/`SelectivePredictionRecord` | Tests A3 feature contribution to deferral | `inferred_candidate`, requires confirmation |
| A8.3 | A8 | IHARQ-reason-code deferral router | Adds IHARQ action/reason/request/fallback/unsafe context | A8.2 plus `IHARQDecisionRecord`/`IHARQTraceRecord` | Tests whether A5 context improves routing | `inferred_candidate`, requires confirmation |
| A8.4 | A8 | Evidence-quality-aware deferral router | Adds learned or rule-derived evidence-quality score where legal | A8.3 plus `EvidenceQualityRecord` variant tags | Tests A6-style evidence-quality contribution | `inferred_candidate`, requires confirmation |
| A8.5 | A8 | Regime-aware deferral router | Adds causal `RegimeStateRecord` / `TrustStateRecord` fields | A8.4 plus Phase 5 temporal-trust records | Tests A7 context contribution to deferral | Optional; requires causal temporal records |
| A8.6 | A8 | Fallback-source sensitivity | Changes declared fallback source or safer-model route while keeping source split/cost keys matched | `DeferralRecord`, fallback-source log, cost config | Tests whether result depends on fallback assumption | `inferred_candidate`, requires confirmation |
| A8.7 | A8 | Cost-weight sensitivity | Varies declared cost weights without using held-out outcomes for selection | Direct-versus-defer cost table, matched reports | Tests robustness of A8 conclusion to cost model | Required if cost-sensitive claim is made |
| A8.8 | A8 | Deferral target ablation | Separates request-evidence, wait, no-action/safe-hold, fallback, safer-model, and supervisor-proxy routes | Target manifest, legality masks, route-specific records | Prevents one “defer” label from hiding incompatible actions | `inferred_candidate`; final target enum unresolved |

### 14. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 obligations are mandatory for A8, but Layer 10 remains read-only and derived. It must not train the deferral model, tune cost weights, create deferral targets, repair records, or convert diagnostic-only results into thesis-ready claims.

| Layer 10 output | Required source records | Required display/export content | Missingness warning |

| Learning-to-defer overview page | `DeferralRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, policy IDs, matched reports | Deferral rate, target distribution, burden, coverage, wrong-accept, cost, matched status, claim tags | “A8 dashboard incomplete: missing deferral source records or matched keys.” |
| Deferral burden curves | `DeferralRecord`, metric dictionary entries, fallback/cost configs | Deferral/fallback/request/no-action burden by dataset/subject/session/model/seed | “Burden curve diagnostic-only: metric dictionary or denominator missing.” |
| Direct-versus-defer cost table | Cost config, direct/defer cost table, matched reports | Expected and realized proxy costs, matched-cost deltas, cost sensitivity | “Cost comparison diagnostic-only: cost config or matched group missing.” |
| Comparator matrix | A0–A7/A9 comparator records and A8 matched report | Comparator status, fully/partially/unmatched flags, diagnostic-only labels | “Comparator incomplete: missing or unmatched baseline.” |
| Controller/deferral card | Controller card source bundle, policy artifact hash, feature list, action-space/legality files, target manifest | Policy identity, features, targets, costs, baselines, metrics, limitations, failure cases | “Card source incomplete: not thesis-ready.” |
| Negative-result page | `NegativeResultNote`, baseline-sufficiency table, diagnostic flags | Over-deferral, baseline-equivalent, high-cost, unstable, fallback-missing, leakage notes | “Negative-result note missing for affected result.” |
| Export manifest | Source record IDs, config hashes, seeds, metric dictionary IDs, dashboard export ID | Reproducibility package links and source-record lineage | “Export cannot support claim-evidence: missing source manifest.” |
| Claim-evidence view | Claim-evidence rows/manifests, Layer 0 tags, diagnostic-only flags | Allowed claims, forbidden-claim blockers, limitation inheritance | “Claim-evidence incomplete: Layer 0 review required.” |

#### 14.1 Layer 10 prohibitions for A8

Layer 10 must not:

- train or tune the learning-to-defer model;
- select fallback routes or cost weights using held-out outcomes;
- create pseudo-labels or deferral targets;
- alter `DeferralRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, or `PolicyActionRecord` source records;
- hide high-burden or negative-result rows through dashboard filtering;
- repair missing source IDs, matched keys, or metric dictionary entries;
- relabel proxy/supervisor/oracle fallback as real expert triage;
- turn diagnostic-only A8 results into claim-supporting thesis evidence.

### 15. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

A8 claim language must remain bounded to public-data, proxy-readiness, computational-policy, pseudo-label/cost-model, simulation-only where applicable, and diagnostic-only evidence.

| Claim class | Allowed A8 wording | Required conditions | Forbidden wording |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deferral baseline sufficiency | “Learning-to-defer is a strong matched-cost/matched-coverage baseline in the tested public-data proxy setting.” | Fully matched A8 versus A9/A5/A2/A3 comparisons; metric dictionary; negative results visible | “Deferral proves safe clinical handoff” |
| Deferral improves proxy trade-off | “A8 improves wrong-accept/cost/coverage trade-offs relative to matched baselines.” | Matched source records, cost config, fallback definition, metric dictionary | “A8 improves patient safety” |
| Deferral burden limitation | “The router reduced wrong accepts but increased deferral/fallback/no-action burden.” | Burden metrics and negative-result note | “A8 is safer because it defers more” |
| Fallback-source sensitivity | “A8 conclusions depend on the declared fallback source and cost model.” | Fallback/source/cost sensitivity report | “The system can safely route to experts” unless actual source supports and is still bounded |
| Regime-aware deferral context | “Temporal-trust features changed A8 behavior under matched causal context.” | Valid A7 records and temporal cutoff | “The model diagnoses fatigue or patient state” |
| Simulation-only deferral consequence | “A8 deferral route changed simulated closed-loop proxy outcomes.” | Phase 8/Layer 7 records and simulation-only tags | “A8 validates real-time deployment safety” |

#### 15.1 Required limitation labels

A8 outputs must inherit applicable labels, including `public_eeg_only`, `proxy_readiness`, `pseudo_label_based`, `computational_policy_only`, `evaluation_only`, `diagnostic_only`, `simulation_only` where replayed, `stress_conditioned` where stressed, `embodiment_proxy_only` where embodied, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, `not_medical_device_readiness`, `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`, `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`, and `not_deployment_safety`.

#### 15.2 Forbidden A8 claims

A8 must not claim or imply clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, clinical triage efficacy, real expert handoff validation, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real-world embodied control validation, clinical fatigue diagnosis, real physiological stress validation, or deployment-readiness/safety guarantees.

### 16. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

A8 must make negative and simpler-baseline outcomes visible.

| Outcome | Required interpretation | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A8 fails to beat A2 threshold | Simple thresholding may be sufficient for the tested cost/coverage setting | A8 superiority claim blocked; threshold baseline strengthened |
| A8 fails to beat A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | Ordinary uncertainty rejection may be sufficient without target-aware routing | A8 claim weakened; feature/target design review needed |
| A8 fails to beat A4 ordinary waiting/ensemble controls | Evidence accumulation or ordinary ensemble may be enough | A8 complexity weakened; delay burden must be reported |
| A8 fails to beat A5 IHARQ-lite | Interpretable rule evidence verification may be sufficient | A8 optional/diagnostic unless narrower route benefit exists |
| A8 matches A9 supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Deferral is a strong simpler baseline; A9 benefit may be unnecessary in that setting | A9 claims narrowed; A8 baseline-sufficiency statement required |
| A8 beats A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ may be overfit, cost-sensitive, or unnecessarily complex | A9 downgrade; A8 sufficiency claim allowed only if fully matched |
| A8 over-defers | Apparent wrong-accept reduction may come from excessive burden or coverage collapse | Claim weakened; burden/cost negative-result note required |
| A8 defers to unavailable fallback | Deferral route is not implementable under declared assumptions | Affected route diagnostic-only or invalid |
| A8 depends on supervisor/oracle proxy | Result is proxy/simulation/evaluation-only | No real expert or clinical handoff claim |
| A8 unstable across seeds/subjects/sessions | Policy may be fragile or cost-sensitive | Weakened/diagnostic unless stability is restored |
| A8 cost ranking changes under weights | Conclusion depends on arbitrary cost model | Cost-sensitive limitation required |
| A8 dashboard export incomplete | Reporting/reproducibility evidence incomplete | No thesis-ready dashboard/export claim |

### 17. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

A8 must be downgraded to diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work-only, or invalid when the required evidence contract fails.

| Trigger | Downgrade status | Required action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `DeferralRecord` | `blocked_section` for thesis-ready A8; possible `diagnostic_only` if mock/placeholder is declared | Do not claim A8 result; generate records or mark missing |
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` or invalid context | `invalid` or `diagnostic_only` | Rebuild from validated source records; exclude future labels/rewards |
| Deferral target not declared | `diagnostic_only` | Add target manifest and reason vocabulary mapping |
| Fallback source/cost not declared | `diagnostic_only` | Add fallback registry/log and cost config |
| Test-set target/cost/threshold tuning | `invalid` | Rerun with split-safe selection |
| Supervisor-proxy treated as real expert | `invalid_claim` | Relabel as proxy/simulation/evaluation-only or remove claim |
| Unmatched comparator keys | `unmatched_diagnostic` | Mark comparison diagnostic-only; do not rank variants |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | `diagnostic_only_metric` | Add metric dictionary or remove thesis-ready metric |
| Missing negative-result note for over-deferral/baseline equivalence | `claim_blocked` | Add `NegativeResultNote` before claim-evidence export |
| Hidden update/adaptation in frozen evaluation | `invalid` | Separate update-enabled and frozen runs; require `PolicyUpdateTrace` if updates occur |
| Missing action-space or legality-mask mapping | `diagnostic_only` | Add action-space version and legality validation |
| Unresolved IHARQ action aliases affect features | `diagnostic_only` for affected rows | Preserve alias issue and map tokens explicitly |
| Dashboard export lacks source manifest | `dashboard_claim_blocked` | Provide source-record/export manifest lineage |
| Claim exceeds public-data/proxy/simulation boundary | `forbidden` | Remove or rewrite claim under Layer 0 boundary |

### 18. Open Issues and Requires-Confirmation Items

| Issue | Type | A8 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeferralRecord.deferral_target` and `deferral_reason` final enum incomplete | schema/vocabulary gap | Different implementations may use incompatible deferral targets or reasons | Use manifest-mapped local vocabulary; mark final enum `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Fallback-source and supervisor-proxy status | schema/claim gap | Real fallback, safer-model, request, no-action, and supervisor-proxy routes can be confused | Require route type, availability, cost, and proxy/simulation/human status tags |
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 ownership nuance | ownership/schema conflict | Phase 8 may materialize run-specific contexts; A8 must preserve Layer 6 semantic ownership | Treat Phase 8 context instances as run-specific/adapter unless confirmed |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared-producer nuance | producer conflict | A8 may use Layer 4 rule-derived and Layer 6 learned variants | Require producer module, variant tag, phase ID, and source lineage |
| IHARQ action-token alias issue | alias conflict | A8 feature/context mapping may be ambiguous | Preserve `combine`/`combine_evidence` alias issue; require action-token map |
| Metric dictionary schema/path gap | metric-definition gap | Deferral metrics cannot be thesis-ready without dictionary entries | Mark exact entries `requires_confirmation: true` until finalized |
| Repository/storage path gaps | path/schema gap | Exact paths for target manifests, cost tables, and card source bundles may vary | Use manifest mapping; do not invent official paths beyond supported conceptual areas |
| Exact final datasets/seeds/runs/statistical tests | v0.1/v1.0 boundary | Final inference plan is not fixed | Defer to v1.0/final-run matrix with `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Exact dashboard routes/table/figure numbers | v0.1/v1.0 boundary | Layer 10 route names are not final | Require export manifests rather than hard-coded route claims |
| Cost-weight arbitrariness | metric/claim risk | A8 conclusions may depend on arbitrary costs | Require cost sensitivity and limitation labels |
| Trial/window identity ambiguity | matched-comparison issue | Deferral and wait/request comparisons can become unfair | Preserve `trial_id` / `window_id` lineage and mark standalone trial schema issue if unresolved |

### 19. Handoff to Later Protocol Sections

A8 hands forward deferral and routing evidence to later sections without owning downstream policy, simulation, stress, or embodiment claims.

| Downstream section | A8 handoff | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A9 — Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | A8 serves as the required simpler deferral comparator and baseline-sufficiency check | A9 must beat or contextualize A8 under matched cost/coverage to justify added complexity |
| A10 — Contextual bandit | A8 can serve as a fixed non-bandit deferral baseline or action route in simulation | A10 uses update/reward/adaptation evidence produced by Phase 10 / Layers 6–7 and requires `PolicyUpdateTrace` where updates occur |
| A11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | A8 can serve as a non-RL baseline and burden comparator | A11 remains simulation-only and stretch; A8 does not validate RL |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | A8 deferral behavior can be stress-conditioned where `StressProfileRecord`/`StressScheduleRecord` are present | Stress evidence belongs to A12 and remains controlled-stress proxy evidence |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | A8 deferral/no-action/fallback route may affect proxy command gating | Embodiment evidence belongs to A13/Layer 9 and remains proxy/simulation-only |
| Metric-family section | Requires exact deferral metric dictionary entries, denominators, grouping, direction, and limitation tags | Metrics not confirmed remain inferred/diagnostic |
| Matched-comparison rules | Adds A8-specific target/fallback/cost/action-legality keys | Unmatched A8 comparison cannot support superiority claims |
| Diagnostic-only rules | Adds missing-deferral, missing-target, missing-fallback, cost leakage, and supervisor-proxy triggers | Diagnostic-only status must propagate to dashboard and claims |
| Layer 10 export/dashboard obligations | Hands card source bundles, matched reports, burden curves, warnings, and export manifests | Layer 10 remains read-only and derived |
| Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries | Hands limitation tags and forbidden-claim blockers for deferral/routing | No clinical triage, patient safety, or deployment claim |

### 20. v0.1 Versus v1.0 Boundary for A8

|---|---|---|
| Scientific role of A8 | Defined | No |
| Required records and producer phases | Defined at record-family level | Exact implemented schema rows and validation paths |
| Baselines and comparators | Defined | Exact final run matrix and inclusion/exclusion list |

| Cost model | Required and versioned | Final cost weights, sensitivity grid, and selection rule |
| Fallback-source assumptions | Required | Final fallback-source inventory and availability model |
| Seeds/runs/datasets | Required conceptually | Exact final dataset list, seeds, repetitions, and run commands |
| Dashboard outputs | Required at obligation level | Exact route names, table/figure numbers, and UI paths |
| Claim wording | Bounded and forbidden classes listed | Final Layer 0 claim-evidence matrix wording |

### 0. A9 Document-Control Audit and Target Resolution

**Protocol version:** v0.1  
**Target section generated in this append:** A9  
**Target identity:** Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ / supervised adaptive readiness policy, where source-supported.  
**Output mode:** append new section to existing protocol.  
**Previous protocol sections provided:** A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8.  
**Current append handling:** the supplied A0–A8 protocol document is preserved substantively in the assembled output. This A9 section is appended after the supplied A0–A8 content. No previous protocol section is deleted, shortened, or re-scoped; source-grounded continuity repairs are documented where needed.

A9 is a global ablation/evaluation-use identifier. It is not Phase 6, not Layer 6, not a module owner, not an artifact producer, not a dashboard page, not a clinical readiness labeler, not an online adaptive controller, and not real BCI-FES deployment evidence. The source-supported implementation/evidence phase that primarily produces A9 source records is **Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ**, and the semantic producing architecture layer is **Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer**. A9 consumes and compares records produced by official layers and phases; A9 itself does not produce records.

A9 evaluates whether a supervised multi-action readiness policy learned from declared, split-safe, cost-based pseudo-labels improves computational readiness decisions over simpler baselines. The central question is whether supervised Adaptive-IHARQ can reduce wrong accepts, preserve useful coverage, control request/wait/fallback/no-action burden, and improve declared proxy utility under matched data, split, cost, coverage, action-space, legality-mask, and metric-dictionary conditions.

### 3. Target Purpose and Scientific Question

A9 asks whether supervised Adaptive-IHARQ adds scientifically meaningful value after the project already has decoder baselines, calibration, uncertainty, simple thresholds, selective prediction, ordinary aggregation controls, IHARQ-lite, RegimeRisk, evidence-quality estimation, and learning-to-defer comparison logic.

The A9 policy is trained from **declared cost-based computational pseudo-labels**, not human readiness labels. A valid A9 evaluation must therefore show not merely that a classifier can reproduce pseudo-labels, but that the frozen supervised policy yields a better or better-characterized computational trade-off under held-out, split-safe, matched comparisons.

| Scientific question | Required A9 answer |
|---|---|
| Does supervised Adaptive-IHARQ reduce wrong accepts compared with simpler baselines? | Compare A9 against A0–A8 under matched keys and report wrong-accept, coverage, cost, and burden trade-offs |
| Does A9 preserve useful coverage rather than hiding risk by refusing too often? | Report coverage, request/wait/fallback/no-action/unsafe burden, and action distributions |
| Does A9 improve declared proxy utility under versioned cost assumptions? | Evaluate matched-cost and cost-sensitivity behavior; do not treat arbitrary cost weights as universal truth |
| Does RegimeRisk/evidence-quality/IHARQ context help beyond calibration and uncertainty alone? | Run context ablations where records exist; mark unavailable context as not-applicable or diagnostic-only |
| Does A9 outperform or contextualize learning-to-defer? | Compare against A8 where A8 records exist; if deferral is sufficient, narrow A9 claims |
| Is A9 robust to split, subject/session/dataset, and cost changes? | Require held-out frozen evaluation, split controls, seed/config lineage, and negative-result visibility |
| Can A9 support clinical, real patient-safety, or deployment-readiness claims? | No. A9 supports only bounded public-data/proxy-readiness computational policy evidence |

A positive A9 result can support a bounded claim that supervised Adaptive-IHARQ improves proxy readiness-policy trade-offs in the tested public EEG setting under declared costs and matched comparisons. A negative result can be equally valid: if A2/A3/A5/A8 or another simpler baseline matches or exceeds A9, the protocol must report baseline sufficiency and restrict A9 to downstream baseline/context use.
