| Target-construction card/source bundle | Layer 6 target construction / Phase 6; Layer 10 renders later | Documents source labels, cost assumptions, allowed future information, leakage guard, limitation tags | supported concept; exact canonical artifact name/path unresolved | Missing card/source bundle downgrades A9 claim maturity |
| Supervised policy artifact | Layer 6 / Phase 6 | Frozen trained policy, selected on validation only | source-supported | Missing model hash/seed/config/split selection blocks reproducible A9 evidence |
| `PolicyActionRecord` | Layer 6 supervised policy / Phase 6 | Logs selected action, action probability, expected cost, source IHARQ action, legality mask, policy ID, context ID, claim boundary | source-supported | Missing lineage/action-space/legality/cost fields downgrades or blocks A9 |
| Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Layer 6 evaluation exporter / Phase 6 | Stores A9 results, metric IDs, matched keys, diagnostic status, negative-result links | source-supported evaluation artifact | Metric or matched-key gaps make affected results diagnostic-only |
| A9 `MatchedComparisonReport` | Layer 6 evaluation exporter / Phase 6 | Required fair comparison record against A0–A8 and later baselines where applicable | source/registry-supported | No superiority claim if absent or unmatched |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` references | Evaluation/metric governance; Phase 2/6/14/15 linkage | Defines metrics, directionality, source fields, limitations, display/export semantics | required; schema/path gap preserved | Metrics without entries cannot support thesis-ready claims |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Layer 6 evaluation exporter / Layer 0 interface | Records baseline equivalence, instability, over-fallback, over-wait, leakage failure, missing baseline, or weak results | source-supported evaluation/claim artifact | Hidden negative results block final handoff |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Layer 6 / Layer 0 interface | Marks rows/metrics/comparisons that cannot support thesis-ready claims | source-supported claim-safety artifact | Required for leaky/unmatched/incomplete items |
| Controller-card source bundle | Layer 6 source bundle; Layer 10 renders later | Documents policy identity, inputs, action space, target construction, metrics, limitations, failure cases | supported; rendered output belongs to Layer 10 | Missing bundle weakens Layer 10/Phase 15 traceability |
| Phase 6 / A9 handoff manifest | Layer 6 / Phase 6 | Lists paths/IDs/hashes/status/open issues/claim tags for downstream phases and Layer 10/0 | required reproducibility artifact | Missing manifest downgrades downstream and final integration readiness |

### 9. A9 Evaluation Design

#### 9.1 Minimum viable A9 evaluation

A minimum viable A9 section is thesis-usable only if it includes:

1. validated upstream Phase 1–5 source records for every eligible A9 row;
2. split-safe `ReadinessContextRecord` assembly with decision-time/evaluation-only partitioning;
3. declared action-space and legality-mask configuration;
4. declared cost-model configuration;
5. pseudo-label files and target-construction card/source bundle with split/leakage status;
6. supervised policy trained on training split and selected on validation split only;
7. held-out frozen evaluation on test/evaluation rows;
8. `PolicyActionRecord` export with action probabilities/expected cost where applicable, `source_iharq_action`, context ID, action-space version, legality-mask ID, cost config ID, policy ID, seed, config hash, and claim tags;
9. matched comparison against A5 IHARQ-lite plus A2/A3 threshold/selective baselines, and A0/A1 baselines where available;
10. metric dictionary references, matched-comparison report, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and Layer 10/Layer 0 handoff metadata.

If any minimum item is missing, A9 may still be included as diagnostic analysis, but it cannot support a superiority or thesis-ready adaptive-policy claim.

#### 9.2 Strong / thesis-ready A9 evaluation

A strong A9 evaluation additionally includes:

- comparisons against A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, probability averaging, and ordinary ensembles;
- comparison against A6 evidence-quality threshold or evidence-quality-aware IHARQ where valid;
- comparison against A7 RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ or regime-aware policy context where Phase 5 outputs are valid;
- comparison against A8 learning-to-defer where Phase 7 `DeferralRecord` and matched cost/coverage lineage exist;
- subject/session/dataset generalization analysis;
- context ablations: decoder-only; decoder plus calibration/uncertainty; calibration/uncertainty plus IHARQ evidence; plus evidence-quality; plus RegimeRisk/trust; optional history where causally available;
- action-space ablations: reduced action set versus full declared action set;
- cost sensitivity across wrong-accept, wait/request, fallback, no-action, and unsafe penalties;
- action-class imbalance analysis and illegal-action count;
- action probability calibration where probabilistic policies are used;
- negative-result visibility when simpler baselines are sufficient or A9 collapses to overly conservative behavior;
- controller-card source bundle and dashboard-readable export manifest ready for Layer 10.

#### 9.3 Forbidden or misleading A9 evaluation designs

The following are not valid thesis-ready A9 designs:

- training and evaluating pseudo-label replication on the same split;
- using `true_label`, `decoder_correct`, future-window evidence, future reward, oracle cost, future stress outcome, or future embodiment outcome as ordinary decision-time features;
- comparing A9 against baselines on different row populations without a diagnostic-only label;
- allowing illegal actions during evaluation and counting them as valid policy outputs;
- selecting thresholds, cost weights, feature sets, or policies on test labels;
- presenting dashboard-generated cards or warnings as primary empirical evidence;
- merging update-enabled bandit/RL curves with frozen supervised A9 evaluation;
- describing cost-based pseudo-labels as human readiness labels or clinical action labels.

### 10. Baselines and Comparators

A9 must be compared against simpler and neighboring baselines under matched conditions. Missing comparators must be disclosed; they cannot be silently omitted from superiority language.

| Comparator | Required status for A9 | Matched dimensions | If comparator matches or beats A9 | If A9 beats comparator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / accept-all | Required where prediction records exist | dataset, subject/session/window, model, split, seed/config | A9 may be unnecessary or over-conservative; raw baseline sufficiency noted with limitations | A9 may claim improved proxy trade-off only if cost/coverage matched |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Required where calibration exists | same model/split/calibration ID and score fields | Calibration alone may be sufficient | A9 adds value beyond calibration visibility |
| A2 simple registered threshold | Required | threshold registry, coverage/cost operating point, split, model, seed/config | Simple threshold sufficiency; A9 superiority unsupported | A9 improves beyond simple threshold under declared matched conditions |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | Required where uncertainty/selective outputs exist | uncertainty features, selective threshold, coverage/cost, split | Selective prediction sufficiency; A9 narrows | A9 improves beyond rejection-only strategy |
| A4 longer-window/voting/averaging/ordinary ensemble controls | Required where ordinary controls exist | row/window population, aggregation config, model family, split, seed/config | Ordinary aggregation may explain gains | A9 adds beyond delay/aggregation/ensemble effects |
| A5 IHARQ-lite | Primary required baseline | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, source action tokens, reason codes, cost/action space, split | Rule-based IHARQ sufficient; A9 complexity not justified | A9 adds supervised learned readiness benefit over interpretable IHARQ |
| A6 evidence-quality estimator / threshold | Required where valid learned quality outputs exist | evidence-quality variant, target-construction ID, split, threshold/cost settings | Evidence-quality scoring alone may be enough | A9 adds multi-action policy benefit beyond score/threshold |
| A7 RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ/context | Required where Phase 5 records valid | regime/trust temporal cutoff, stop-loss status, row identity, split | Temporal-trust context alone may be sufficient | A9 learns useful interactions with RegimeRisk/trust features |
| A8 learning-to-defer | Required where Phase 7 records exist | deferral target, fallback availability, cost model, action space, matched coverage/cost, split | Deferral sufficiency; A9 claim narrowed to no better than simpler routing | A9 adds value beyond deferral-only routing |
| Fallback-only / no-action conservative route | Required where fallback/no-action configs exist | fallback availability, action-space legality, cost config, split | Conservative route may dominate under high penalties | A9 can claim balanced policy only with burden/cost evidence |
| A10/A11 bandit/RL | Downstream comparator, not required for core A9 | simulation state/reward/update mode where later records exist | Simulation policy may outperform; A9 remains frozen baseline | A9 can remain strong simpler baseline; no online adaptation claim |

### 11. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

A9 comparisons require row-level and configuration-level matchability. The matched-comparison record must state whether each comparison is `fully_matched`, `partially_matched_diagnostic_only`, or `unmatched_excluded_from_claim`.

#### 11.1 Required matched keys

```text
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
selective_prediction_id where applicable
iharq_decision_id
regime_state_id where applicable
trust_state_record_ids where applicable
evidence_quality_id where applicable
readiness_context_id
action_space_version
legality_mask_id
cost_config_id
target_construction_id
pseudo_label_version
policy_id
policy_family
training_stage
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
phase_id
ablation_id
metric_dictionary_id
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
```

#### 11.2 Matched-comparison matrix

| Comparison family | Must match | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A9 vs A0/A1 | same data rows, model, split, seed/config, calibration status where applicable | missing model/calibration lineage or different row populations |
| A9 vs A2/A3 | threshold/uncertainty/selective operating point, coverage/cost target, split, model, metric dictionary | test-tuned threshold or unmatched coverage/cost |
| A9 vs A4 | window identities, aggregation/ensemble config, model family, split, seed/config | ordinary control evaluated on different windows/subjects without label |
| A9 vs A5 | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, source IHARQ action token, reason code, cost/action-space mapping, row identity | missing source action token or invalid alias mapping |
| A9 vs A6 | evidence-quality variant, target-construction ID, producer module, split, feature legality | untagged learned/rule quality variant or target leakage |
| A9 with versus without A7 context | same rows/policy protocol except visible RegimeRisk/trust fields | regime/trust fields use future or target-derived information |
| A9 vs A8 | deferral target, fallback availability, cost model, action-space/legality, row identity, coverage/cost | Phase 7 deferral rows missing, deferral target undefined, or fallback availability unmatched |
| Context ablations | same train/validation/test rows, same policy family/selection protocol, changed only declared observable field set | hidden features or different rows used |
| Cost sensitivity | same data/context rows with varied `cost_config_id` and declared pseudo-label version | cost variants generated from different splits without diagnostic label |
| Action-space ablations | same rows and cost model with declared action-space version differences | unlogged action alias or illegal-action mismatch |

#### 11.3 Missing key handling

If any required matched key is absent:

1. the affected comparison row must be marked `diagnostic_only`;
2. the missing key must be listed in the A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`;
3. a `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` must identify the affected records, metrics, and claims;
4. a `NegativeResultNote` must be created when the gap changes interpretation;
5. Layer 10 must surface the mismatch as a warning;
6. Phase 15 must not use the affected row as thesis-confirmatory evidence.

### 12. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

Every A9 metric must have a metric dictionary entry before it supports a thesis-ready claim. Metric names below are protocol-level metric families or required measurement concepts; exact formulas, denominators, units, statistical tests, and dashboard display names remain `requires_confirmation` unless already instantiated by the metric dictionary.

| Metric family | Example measurement concepts | Source records | A9 interpretation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wrong-accept / unsafe-accept family | wrong-accept rate; wrong accept at matched coverage; unsafe-action violation count | `PredictionRecord`, labels in evaluation partition, `PolicyActionRecord`, legality-mask file/ID, `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Primary risk-reduction proxy; not real patient safety | metric dictionary required |
| Coverage / accepted-decision family | accepted coverage; accepted correct fraction; coverage at fixed cost | `PolicyActionRecord`, matched report, evaluation labels | Shows whether A9 preserves useful decisions | metric dictionary required |
| Request/wait/fallback/no-action burden family | request rate, wait rate, fallback burden, no-action rate, unsafe block rate | `PolicyActionRecord`, action-distribution report | Prevents hiding risk by refusing/deferring too often | metric dictionary required |
| Declared proxy utility / cost family | mean declared cost, cost at matched coverage, cost sensitivity deltas | cost config, pseudo-label files, `PolicyActionRecord`, `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Evaluates trade-off under declared computational costs only | metric dictionary required; cost config required |
| Action-distribution and legality family | action histogram, illegal-action count, legality-mask compliance, action-class imbalance | `PolicyActionRecord`, action-space file, legality-mask file | Detects policy collapse, invalid actions, and unsupported action aliases | metric dictionary required |
| Pseudo-label stability family | label distribution by cost config, action-cost margin, pseudo-label flip rate across cost variants | pseudo-label files, target-construction card, cost configs | Shows whether A9 depends on arbitrary cost weights | inferred_candidate unless metric dictionary confirms |
| Context-ablation family | delta in wrong accept/coverage/cost when adding calibration, IHARQ, evidence-quality, RegimeRisk, history | context-ablation table, `ReadinessContextRecord`, matched report | Tests whether added context is useful | metric dictionary required |
| Action-probability calibration family | policy action probability calibration, multiclass calibration proxy, confidence in selected action | `PolicyActionRecord`, validation/evaluation partitions | Optional for probabilistic policies; supports reliability visibility | optional/inferred_candidate; requires confirmation |
| Matched-delta family | delta wrong accept at matched coverage; delta coverage at matched cost; delta burden at matched cost | A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric dictionary | Fair comparison against A0–A8 | required for superiority claims |
| Generalization/stability family | subject/session/dataset split performance, seed variability, policy-selection stability | splits, `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, policy artifacts | Detects overfitting and instability | metric dictionary and final statistics deferred |
| Dashboard warning / diagnostic family | missing keys, leakage flags, unmatched rows, invalid action tokens | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, validation reports, Layer 10 warning inputs | Reporting/governance only, not empirical performance | dashboard/read-only; not primary evidence metric |

Metrics that imply clinical validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real-time deployment safety, or validated therapeutic effectiveness are forbidden. A9 can discuss only public EEG proxy-readiness and computational policy evidence under declared costs.

### 13. Split, Leakage, Threshold, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint family | A9 requirement | Downgrade if violated |
|---|---|---|
| Split separation | Pseudo-label construction, feature normalization, policy training, validation selection, threshold selection, cost tuning, and final evaluation must respect train/validation/test and subject/session/dataset boundaries | Thesis-facing A9 claim blocked; affected rows diagnostic-only |
| Decision-time visibility | `ReadinessContextRecord` may contain only information observable at the decision point or causally available in declared replay; target/evaluation fields stay partitioned | Hidden targets/oracle/future fields invalidate policy evaluation |
| Pseudo-label construction | Cost-based pseudo-labels must be versioned, split-safe, action-legal, and linked to cost vectors/source labels/allowed future information | Missing or leaky pseudo-labels make A9 diagnostic-only |
| Threshold and calibration | Thresholds/calibration used by A9 must come from registered split-safe sources; test-label tuning is forbidden | A2/A3/A9 comparisons diagnostic-only |
| Action legality | Action legality mask must apply before optimization and evaluation; unsafe/stop-loss/fallback/request-budget/no-future-window restrictions must be enforced | Illegal valid actions block affected `PolicyActionRecord` rows |
| Source IHARQ token preservation | Layer 4-compatible actions and source `uncertain` state must be preserved and mapped through declared action-space/alias-map rules | Alias-mapped rows diagnostic-only until validation passes |
| Cost sensitivity | Wrong-accept, delay/wait/request, fallback, no-action, unsafe, and optional route costs must be reported and sensitivity-tested | Cost-superiority claims weakened or diagnostic-only |
| Frozen policy evaluation | A9 thesis-facing evaluation must use a frozen selected policy; no updates during held-out evaluation | Mixed update/training/evaluation curves block A9 claim |
| Policy-update trace | Not required for ordinary frozen A9; required only if an update-enabled simulation branch is explicitly invoked | Missing trace invalidates update-enabled claims and moves content to A10/A11 diagnostic context |
| Stress context | Stress profiles are downstream/A12 context; no stress-conditioned claim unless stress records and clean/stressed matching exist | Stress rows diagnostic-only or downstream_context_only |
| Embodiment context | Embodiment records are downstream/A13 proxy context; no real motor-control claim | Embodiment rows diagnostic-only or embodiment_proxy_only |
| Dashboard boundary | Layer 10 views/cards/warnings cannot be used as source features or primary evidence | Dashboard-derived evidence claim blocked |

### 14. Local A9 Sub-Ablation Policy

A9 may define local sub-ablations only as children of A9. They are not new global A IDs and must not be treated as official implementation phases.

| Local sub-ablation | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A9.1 context-level ablation | Decoder-only; +calibration/uncertainty; +IHARQ/evidence; +evidence-quality; +RegimeRisk/trust; optional history where causal | source-supported concept; exact run matrix requires confirmation |
| A9.2 action-space ablation | Reduced action set versus full declared action set; verifies whether added routes help | source-supported concept; exact action subset requires confirmation |
| A9.3 cost-sensitivity ablation | Vary wrong-accept, request/wait, fallback, no-action, unsafe costs | source-supported concept; exact grid requires confirmation |
| A9.4 policy-family ablation | Logistic regression / calibrated gradient-boosted classifier / shallow MLP / cost-sensitive or hierarchical classifier where data supports | architecture-supported model examples; exact final model list requires confirmation |
| A9.5 legality-mask ablation | Diagnostic-only named ablation to show effect of legality constraints, never to validate illegal deployment | diagnostic_only; cannot support safety claim |
| A9.6 A8-sufficiency comparison | Tests whether learning-to-defer explains A9 benefit | source-supported where Phase 7 A8 records exist; otherwise future handoff |

Any local sub-ablation not supported by records, configs, and matched keys must be marked `inferred_candidate` and `requires_confirmation: true` in downstream run matrices.

### 15. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 reads and renders A9 evidence but does not create primary empirical evidence. It must preserve lineage, warnings, limitation tags, metric dictionary references, matched-comparison keys, and negative-result notes.

| Layer 10 output/input family | Required A9 source records | Required display/export behavior | Prohibition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Policy/action dashboard view | `PolicyActionRecord`, action-distribution report, action-space file, legality mask | Show action rates, legal/illegal action status, source IHARQ token lineage, action-space version, policy ID | Must not rewrite action tokens or hide illegal-action rows |
| Matched-comparison table | A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric dictionary entries, baseline records | Show fully/partially/unmatched status, missing keys, diagnostic-only rows, negative-result notes | Must not display unmatched rows as confirmatory |
| Cost-sensitivity view | cost configs, pseudo-label files, cost-sensitivity report | Show cost variants, label shifts, metric shifts, sensitivity warnings | Must not present one arbitrary cost setting as universal utility |
| Target-construction summary | pseudo-label files, target-construction card/source bundle, leakage validator | Show source labels, allowed future information, target route, leakage guard, limitation labels | Must not display pseudo-labels as human or clinical readiness labels |
| Context-ablation view | `ReadinessContextRecord`, observable field set IDs, context-ablation table | Show feature groups and deltas under matched rows | Must not hide unavailable or leaky context groups |
| Controller card | controller-card source bundle, policy artifact metadata, metrics, limitations, failure cases | Summarize policy family, inputs, action space, training protocol, metrics, negative results, claim boundary | Must not become a model-selection or policy-repair interface |
| Warning panel | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, validation reports, missing-key logs, claim-safety tags | Surface leakage, missing metric dictionary, missing matched keys, missing pseudo-labels, invalid actions, forbidden wording | Must not convert warnings into empirical evidence |
| Reproducibility export | handoff manifest, source IDs, hashes, seeds, config IDs, metric IDs, matched report IDs | Export enough lineage for rerun/review | Must not omit failed/negative/diagnostic rows |

### 16. Layer 0 Claim-Safety Boundaries

#### 16.1 Allowed bounded A9 claims

A9 may support only bounded claims such as:

| Allowed claim form | Required evidence | Required limitation |
|---|---|---|
| “Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ improves declared proxy readiness-policy trade-offs over matched baselines in the tested public EEG setting.” | Fully matched A9 versus A0–A8 comparisons, metric dictionary, split-safe pseudo-labels, frozen held-out evaluation | Public EEG/proxy-readiness/computational policy only |
| “A9 reduces wrong accepts at matched coverage/cost compared with a specified baseline.” | Matched wrong-accept/coverage/cost metrics, source labels only in evaluation partition, matched report | Not real patient safety or clinical validation |
| “A9 uses IHARQ, evidence-quality, and RegimeRisk context to improve computational policy decisions where ablations support it.” | Context ablation table, valid source records, no leakage, matched keys | RegimeRisk is proxy temporal trust, not clinical state/fatigue diagnosis |
| “A simpler baseline is sufficient relative to A9 in this setting.” | Negative-result note, matched baseline results, visible limitation language | A negative/simplifying result is thesis-valid but narrows A9 superiority |
| “A9 provides a frozen supervised baseline for later simulated closed-loop, stress, bandit, RL, or embodiment-proxy studies.” | Policy artifact, `PolicyActionRecord`, handoff manifest, claim tags | Downstream studies require their own simulation/stress/embodiment evidence |

#### 16.2 Required limitation labels

A9 outputs and reports must carry applicable labels from:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
computational_policy_only
evaluation_only
frozen_supervised_policy
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where applicable
simulation_only where downstream simulation records are used
stress_conditioned where downstream stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where downstream embodiment records are used
```

#### 16.3 Forbidden A9 claims

A9 must not claim or imply:

- validated clinical readiness decisions;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation or therapeutic benefit;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real BCI-FES deployment readiness;
- real-time online adaptive safety;
- clinical fatigue, drift, or physiological diagnosis;
- human expert readiness labels unless separately provided and validated, which the supplied architecture does not assume;
- that pseudo-labels are ground-truth readiness labels;
- that dashboard views/cards are primary evidence.

### 17. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

A9 must preserve negative and simplifying results. A9 does not fail scientifically merely because a simpler baseline is sufficient.

| A9 result pattern | Required interpretation | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A9 beats A2/A3 but not A5 | Threshold/selective baselines are insufficient, but rule-based IHARQ remains sufficient | A9 superiority over IHARQ-lite unsupported |
| A9 beats A5 but not A8 | Learned routing/deferral may explain most benefit | A9 narrows; A8 baseline sufficiency emphasized |
| A9 beats A5/A8 only by lowering coverage heavily | Improvement may be refusal/burden-driven | Require coverage/burden/cost limitation; no broad superiority claim |
| A9 collapses to fallback/wait/no-action | Policy may be over-conservative or cost-biased | Report action distribution; downgrade superiority unless burden justified |
| A9 over-accepts wrong predictions | Learned policy unsafe under proxy objective | Create negative note; no risk-reduction claim |
| A9 sensitive to cost weights | Results depend on arbitrary cost assumptions | Cost-superiority claim diagnostic-only unless sensitivity supports robustness |
| Context ablations show RegimeRisk/evidence-quality adds no benefit | Simpler context is sufficient | Narrow claims; preserve result |
| A9 unstable across seeds/subjects/sessions | Generalization weak | Restrict to diagnostic/provisional evidence |
| Leakage or hidden target detected | Evaluation invalid | Block thesis-facing A9 claims |
| Metric dictionary or matched keys missing | Results not reproducible/fair | Diagnostic-only until repaired |

### 18. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

Affected A9 records, rows, metrics, comparisons, or claims must be downgraded to diagnostic-only when any of the following applies:

1. upstream Phase 1–5 source records are missing, invalid, or unjoinable;
2. required Phase 6 A9 source artifacts or records are missing or invalid, including `ReadinessContextRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`, policy metadata, pseudo-label files, cost-model config, action-space file, or legality-mask file;
3. split leakage exists in feature construction, pseudo-label generation, threshold selection, cost tuning, model selection, or final evaluation;
4. `ReadinessContextRecord` includes `true_label`, `decoder_correct`, future-window evidence, future reward, oracle action/cost, future stress outcome, future embodiment outcome, or dashboard-derived fields as decision-time features;
5. pseudo-label files are missing, unversioned, not linked to cost vectors, or not leakage-audited;
6. target-construction card/source bundle is missing or uses clinical readiness language;
7. action-space version or legality-mask file is missing;
8. illegal actions are emitted as valid policy outputs;
9. source IHARQ action tokens are not preserved or action aliases are unvalidated;
10. cost-model config is unversioned or no sensitivity analysis exists for a cost-based superiority claim;
11. policy is selected or tuned on test/evaluation labels;
12. held-out evaluation is not frozen or is mixed with update-enabled training/adaptation curves;
13. required baselines are missing without explicit limitation;
14. matched-comparison keys are incomplete;
15. metric dictionary entries are missing;
16. learned/rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants are not distinguishable;
17. RegimeRisk/trust fields violate temporal cutoff or non-clinical boundary;
18. A8 comparison is claimed but Phase 7 deferral/fallback lineage is missing;
19. dashboard-generated cards/views are used as primary evidence;
20. negative results or baseline-equivalence outcomes are hidden;
21. forbidden clinical, deployment, patient-safety, rehabilitation, or real motor-control wording appears.

| Issue | Type | A9 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact pseudo-label and target-construction artifact names/paths | registry/path/schema gap | A9 requires these artifacts but cannot promote final names if unresolved | Keep as required candidate/source-bundle artifacts; mark `requires_confirmation` for final path/name |
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 boundary | ownership/materialization nuance | A9 uses Layer 6 canonical context; later simulation may materialize compatible variants | Preserve Layer 6 semantic ownership; mark Layer 7 variants downstream/unresolved |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` shared producer/lifecycle | shared producer/update governance | Ordinary A9 is frozen and does not require updates; update-enabled branches require trace | Mark update-enabled A9-like content as A10/A11/simulation diagnostic unless traced |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` Layer 4/Layer 6 variants | producer/variant ambiguity | A9 may consume both rule-derived and learned variants | Require producer module, derivation type, target-construction ID/version, source IDs |
| Action-token aliases and source `uncertain` state | alias/vocabulary issue | Invalid action mapping can corrupt A9 action distributions | Validate action alias map; preserve `source_iharq_action`; diagnostic-only if unresolved |
| Deferral target/reason vocabularies | vocabulary gap | A9-vs-A8 comparison needs matched deferral target/fallback lineage | Use source-supported `DeferralRecord` fields; exact enum confirmation remains v1.0 |
| Metric dictionary schema/path | metric-definition gap | A9 metrics cannot support thesis claims without dictionary entries | Require metric dictionary entries; unresolved metrics diagnostic-only |
| Final statistical tests / run counts / seeds | v1.0 run-matrix gap | v0.1 cannot lock exact inferential tests unless source-fixed | Mark `requires_confirmation: true` |
| Dashboard route and final figure/table numbering | final integration gap | Layer 10 export must be traceable, but exact UI routes/numbering may be later | Defer to Phase 14/15 final integration |
| Repository storage homes for card/source bundles | repository/path gap | A9 handoff must map artifacts even if canonical homes unresolved | Use manifest-mapped paths; do not invent official paths |
| ClaimEvidenceMatrix versus ClaimEvidenceManifest naming | naming/registry issue | Final claim linkage may use either unresolved naming branch | Preserve as open naming issue until resolved |

### 20. Handoff to Later Protocol Sections

## A10 — Contextual Bandit / Simulation-Bounded Immediate-Reward Adaptation

### 0. A10 Document-Control Audit and Target Resolution

**Protocol version:** v0.1  
**Target section generated in this append:** A10  
**Target identity:** Contextual bandit / simulation-bounded immediate-reward adaptation, where source-supported.  
**Output mode:** append new section to existing protocol.  
**Previous protocol sections provided:** A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9.  
**Current append/revision handling:** the supplied A0–A9 protocol document is preserved substantively in the assembled output, with only source-grounded continuity and producer/consumer wording repairs applied where they improve consistency with the framework, registry, execution/evidence plan, and prompt. This A10 section is appended after the supplied A0–A9 content. No previous section is deleted, shortened, or re-scoped.

A10 is a global ablation/evaluation-use identifier. It is not Phase 10, not Layer 6, not Layer 7, not a module owner, not an artifact producer, not a dashboard page, not an online clinical controller, and not deployed BCI-FES evidence. The source-supported implementation/evidence phase that primarily produces A10 contextual-bandit evidence is **Phase 10 — Contextual bandit**. The semantic producing architecture layer for bandit policy outputs is **Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer**. Layer 7 owns simulated transition, reward, session, rollout, environment-diagnostic, and safety-event records used by A10 evaluation. A10 consumes and compares records produced by official layers and phases; A10 itself does not produce records.

A10 evaluates whether a lightweight contextual bandit improves immediate or near-immediate simulated reward under a declared action space, reward model, exploration/update protocol, legality mask, matched-comparison envelope, and frozen held-out evaluation boundary. Its central question is whether simulation-authorized online adaptation of readiness action, threshold mode, decoder-trust choice, or deferral route adds value beyond validated non-bandit baselines, without hidden leakage, unsafe exploration, simulator overfitting, reward cherry-picking, or claim overreach.

| Control item | A10 handling |
|---|---|
| Official A-ID | A10 only; no new top-level ablation ID is introduced |
| Correct normalized identity | Contextual bandit / simulation-only immediate-reward adaptation |
| Primary producer/consumer boundary | Layer 6 / Phase 10 is the source-supported producer context for contextual-bandit policy configuration, bandit `PolicyActionRecord` rows, bandit policy artifacts, exploration/action-probability traces, update-governance lineage, and controller-card source bundles. Layer 7 / Phase 8 and Phase 10 evaluation runs own or materialize transition, reward, session, rollout, episode, environment-diagnostic, and safety-event records. Evaluation artifacts such as `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, metric dictionaries, and claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries are produced or prepared by the evaluation/claim-safety/reporting workflow, not by A10 as an ablation owner. |
| Primary upstream evidence context | Phases 1–9 records: clean public-data lineage, decoder predictions, calibration/uncertainty/threshold/selective-prediction evidence, IHARQ-lite evidence-verification outputs, RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss records where active, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ and learning-to-defer baselines, stable Layer 7 simulated closed-loop records, and Phase 9 stress profiles only for stress-conditioned A10 claims. |
| Primary scientific role | Tests whether simple immediate-reward adaptation in simulation adds value beyond fixed thresholds, selective prediction, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality-aware IHARQ, RegimeRisk-aware policy context, learning-to-defer, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, and best-fixed policy controls. |
| Layer 10 role | Read, validate, summarize, warn, visualize, export, card, and package saved A10 records and evaluation artifacts; no hidden bandit updates, reward retuning, dashboard-side policy repair, threshold tuning, negative-result suppression, or source-record mutation. |
| Layer 0 role | Claim-safety review, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrade, forbidden-claim blocking, negative-result governance, and final claim-evidence linkage. |
| v0.1 boundary | Defines evaluation requirements, records, comparisons, metric families, matched keys, leakage/update/frozen-evaluation rules, downgrade triggers, Layer 10 outputs, and Layer 0 boundaries; exact datasets, final seeds, run counts, statistical tests, exact command-line execution, exact bandit hyperparameter grids, final dashboard routes, and table/figure numbering remain deferred unless later source-fixed. |

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A10 identity

A10 is the **contextual bandit** evaluation context. In Stretch C, it is simulation-only and immediate-reward bounded. It evaluates bandit adaptation over declared contexts, actions, rewards, exploration policies, and update/frozen-evaluation modes. It does not evaluate delayed-consequence RL, clinical online control, real patient safety, real muscle stimulation, or deployed assistive-control readiness.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

The A10 scientific question is:

> Under the same public-data proxy context, declared reward model, legality mask, simulated closed-loop environment, and matched comparison keys, does a contextual bandit improve immediate-reward readiness behavior over validated fixed, rule-based, supervised, and deferral baselines without increasing wrong accepts, unsafe proxy events, exploration burden, reward sensitivity, seed sensitivity, or simulator-overfitting risk?

#### 3.3 A10 contribution to the cumulative protocol

A10 is the first update-enabled adaptation test in the A0–A13 ladder. It should be attempted only after stable upstream records, validated non-bandit baselines, and a validated Layer 7 simulated environment exist. A10 is scientifically useful even if negative: a failed, flat, unstable, reward-sensitive, or unsafe bandit result can justify retaining simpler fixed policies or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ and can prevent overclaiming the need for online adaptation.

### 9. Baselines and Comparators

A10 must be compared against the strongest validated non-bandit baselines available under the same matched envelope. A10 superiority is not thesis-ready if it only beats weak or unmatched baselines.

| Comparator | Required status | Matching focus | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / accept-all | Required where source outputs exist | Same dataset/window/split/model family and reward evaluation mapping | Tests no-readiness-policy reference |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Required where calibration exists | Same calibration ID and split-safe probabilities | Tests calibration-only reference |
| A2 simple registered threshold | Required | Same threshold registry, coverage/cost target, split and reward model | Tests whether fixed confidence threshold is enough |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction | Required where uncertainty/selective outputs exist | Same uncertainty definitions and operating-point policy | Tests risk-coverage and rejection baseline |
| A4 longer-window / multi-window / ordinary ensemble controls | Required where available | Same source window set, delay accounting, ensemble/voting/averaging config | Tests whether A10 gains are only ordinary evidence aggregation |
| A5 IHARQ-lite | Required | Same IHARQ config, action token map, request budget, fallback/unsafe rules | Tests interpretable rule-based readiness baseline |
| A6 evidence-quality-aware IHARQ | Conditional expected | Same evidence-quality record/source and split-safe target route | Tests learned reliability contribution without bandit updates |
| A7 RegimeRisk-aware policy context | Conditional | Same RegimeRisk/trust records and regime strata | Tests temporal/regime context without bandit update claims |
| A8 learning-to-defer | Required where Phase 7 outputs exist | Same deferral routes, fallback availability, cost model, and reward mapping | Tests whether simpler routing is enough |
| A9 supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Required where Phase 6 outputs exist | Same action space, cost/reward config, legality mask, context level, and held-out split | Tests whether supervised frozen policy is sufficient |
| Best-fixed policy under the same reward | Required for regret or adaptation claims | Same action set, reward config, simulator version, stress profile, seed set | Tests whether adaptation beats a strong fixed policy |
| A11 RL | Downstream only | Not required for A10 | A11 later uses A10 as simpler adaptive baseline; A10 does not need RL |

If a comparator is unavailable, A10 must disclose the missing comparator in the `MatchedComparisonReport`, narrow the claim, and, where material, add a `NegativeResultNote` or `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` rather than asserting broad superiority.

### 10. Matched-Comparison Key Requirements

#### 10.1 Required key families

A10 comparisons must be matched, or explicitly downgraded, using the following key families:

| Key family | Required keys / examples | A10 purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Source-data keys | dataset ID, subject ID, session ID, trial/window ID, split ID, split role, label-budget ID where applicable | Prevents source-population mismatch |
| Decoder/calibration keys | model family, model ID, calibration ID, threshold registry ID, uncertainty config, selective-prediction config | Prevents A10 from benefiting from different upstream predictors |
| Policy-context keys | `ReadinessContextRecord` ID/hash, observable field set, context level, decision-time cutoff, source record IDs, target partition | Proves legal policy-visible context |
| Action-space keys | action-space version, legality-mask ID, action token map, threshold/action mode, fallback availability, request budget, unsafe override rules | Prevents unfair action-set or legality differences |
| Reward/cost keys | reward config ID, cost config ID, penalty hierarchy, stress multipliers, optional embodiment term status, reward term version | Prevents reward cherry-picking |
| Simulation keys | simulator/environment version, closed-loop session ID, episode/rollout ID, transition schema version, environment diagnostic status | Ensures Layer 7 conditions are comparable |
| Update/frozen keys | update mode, training/adaptation split, held-out frozen evaluation split, `PolicyUpdateTrace` completeness, disabled-update audit status | Separates adaptation curves from frozen evaluation |
| Comparator keys | baseline policy ID, policy family, config hash, seed, best-fixed/oracle definition for regret | Ensures fair baseline and regret interpretation |
| Stress keys | stress profile ID, stress schedule ID, stress seed, stress intensity, clean/stressed pair ID | Required only for stress-conditioned A10 |
| Embodiment keys | embodiment mode, embodiment run ID, Layer 9 reward term ID, command mapping status | Downstream/optional only; absence means no A13/A10-embodiment claim |
| Metric/reporting keys | metric dictionary ID, matched-comparison report ID, diagnostic flag ID, negative-result note ID, dashboard/export config ID | Supports Layer 10 and Phase 15 traceability |

#### 10.2 Pass/fail rule

A10 comparisons are thesis-facing only when all material keys are present and consistent. Missing, inconsistent, post-hoc, or unmatched keys require `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. Partially matched comparisons may remain in exploratory appendices only if their limitation labels are visible and not used as evidence of A10 superiority.

### 11. Metric Families and Metric-Dictionary Status

Every A10 metric requires a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or explicit diagnostic-only status before thesis-facing use.

| Metric family | Example metrics | Required source records | Metric-dictionary status | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reward/regret | cumulative reward, reward decomposition, cumulative regret against declared best-fixed/oracle, terminal reward where applicable | `RewardTraceRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, reward config, comparator ID | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` for final formulas, denominators, directionality | Simulation-only computational reward, not clinical utility |
| Readiness trade-off | coverage, accepted-trial accuracy, wrong-accept rate, wrong-accept-over-time, wait/request/fallback/no-action/unsafe rates | `PolicyActionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, source labels for evaluation only, matched keys | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` | Public EEG/proxy readiness only |
| Policy behavior | action distribution, action entropy, action-probability trace, exploration burden, exploration unsafe-block rate, policy stability across seeds | Bandit `PolicyActionRecord`, exploration logs, `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` | Policy-inspection evidence only |
| Safety-oriented proxy | illegal-action count, safety override count, unsafe proxy event count, high-confidence wrong accepted rate, stop-loss compliance | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, `SafetyEventRecord`/logs, `PolicyActionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, RegimeRisk/stop-loss context | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation`; safety-event alias may be unresolved | Simulated/proxy warnings only, not real patient safety |
| Baseline comparison | matched-cost delta, matched-coverage delta, best-fixed delta, A10-vs-A8/A9 delta, baseline sufficiency result | `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric dictionary IDs, comparator source records | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` | Comparison evidence only under matched envelope |
| Sensitivity/robustness | reward sensitivity, cost-weight sensitivity, seed sensitivity, stress-conditioned delta, policy ranking stability | Reward configs, stress records where active, seed manifest, rollout summaries | `requires_confirmation` for exact sensitivity grid and downgrade threshold | Limitation evidence; unstable rankings narrow claims |
| Simulation outcome | task success, late assist, over-assist, under-assist, repeated-failure count, transition reward | Layer 7 transition/episode/rollout records | `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` | Simulated closed-loop evidence only |
| Embodiment outcome | endpoint error, command-status proxy, simulated movement success | Layer 9 records only if later implemented | `downstream_context_only` for core A10 | Not applicable to core A10; cannot support real motor-control claims |

Forbidden metric classes remain blocked: clinical validation metrics, real patient safety metrics, medical-device readiness metrics, rehabilitation efficacy metrics, real-time deployment safety metrics, real BCI-FES or muscle-stimulation control metrics, clinical fatigue diagnosis metrics, and patient-specific outcome metrics.

### 12. Split, Leakage, Threshold, Policy, Simulation, Stress, and Embodiment Constraints

| Constraint family | A10 rule | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Decision-time leakage | `ReadinessContextRecord` policy-visible fields must exclude true labels, decoder correctness, future rewards, future next states, oracle costs, future windows not revealed by a declared transition, future embodiment outcomes, and dashboard inspection notes | Any forbidden field appears in policy-visible context |
| Adaptation/frozen split | Update-enabled training/adaptation curves must be separated from held-out frozen-policy evaluation. Frozen evaluation requires disabled-update/no-mutation evidence | Mixed curves, mutation during held-out evaluation, or no audit |
| Update trace | Every simulation-authorized mutation of action-selection parameters requires `PolicyUpdateTrace` with policy/action/reward/next-state/update IDs, update mode, split, seed, config hash, and simulation-only tag | Any mutation lacks trace or trace sequence incomplete |
| Reward fixation | Reward formula, cost weights, penalty hierarchy, stress multipliers, optional embodiment terms, and sensitivity grid must be declared before evaluation and versioned | Post-hoc reward tuning on held-out outcomes or missing reward config |
| Action legality | Legal actions must be determined before selection; unsafe override, stop-loss, fallback availability, request budget, action-space version, and unsupported command handling must be enforced | Illegal selected action, unsupported action token, missing legality mask, or unsafe exploration |
| Exploration | Exploration schedule must be versioned, bounded, and legality-aware. Unsafe actions may not be explored simply to improve reward estimates | Unbounded exploration, illegal exploration, or unsafe proxy inflation |
| Simulation environment | Layer 7 environment diagnostics must be valid before A10 claims. Simulator version and transition/reward lineage must be traceable | Critical `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` warning or invalid Phase 8 substrate |
| Threshold and operating point | Static comparator thresholds must use registered threshold IDs and not be retuned from final held-out results | Test-tuned thresholds or unmatched coverage/cost target |
| Stress | Stress-conditioned A10 requires Phase 9 stress profiles/schedules, stress seeds, clean/stressed matched keys, and stress-only/proxy limitation tags | Missing stress records or post-hoc stress selection |
| Embodiment | Core A10 does not require embodiment. Optional endpoint-error/command-status reward terms require declared Layer 9 records and must be simulation/proxy-only | Embodiment outcome leaked into policy context or A13 claim made without Layer 9 evidence |
| RL boundary | A10 must not evaluate delayed sequential RL or imply RL results | Delayed-consequence policy learning folded into A10 without A11 controls |

### 13. Local Sub-Ablation Policy for A10

Local sub-ablations may be used only as children of A10. They do not create new top-level ablation IDs.

| Local ID | Local sub-ablation | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A10.1 | Threshold-mode contextual bandit | Select conservative/balanced/aggressive threshold modes under immediate reward | `source_supported_candidate` |
| A10.2 | Readiness-action contextual bandit | Select among declared readiness actions such as accept, wait, request evidence, fallback, no-action, or a conservative unsafe/block outcome only where the action map and legality mask explicitly permit it | `source_supported_candidate` |
| A10.3 | Decoder-trust contextual bandit | Select decoder-family trust/action modes where multiple validated model families exist | `conditional_candidate_requires_source_records` |
| A10.4 | Deferral-route contextual bandit | Select deferral or fallback route using Phase 7 `DeferralRecord` lineage | `conditional_candidate_requires_A8_records` |
| A10.5 | Stress-conditioned contextual bandit | Evaluate A10 under Phase 9 stress profiles and clean/stressed matched keys | `conditional_candidate_requires_Phase9` |
| A10.6 | Embodiment-reward diagnostic branch | Include optional Layer 9 reward terms in a declared downstream simulation branch | `downstream_context_only`; `requires_confirmation`; not core A10 |
| A10.7 | Algorithm-family diagnostic comparison | Compare epsilon-greedy, UCB-style, Thompson sampling, contextual linear bandit, and only if justified lightweight neural bandit | `optional_only`; final hyperparameter grid `requires_confirmation` |

Sub-ablation results must inherit all A10 claim boundaries, matching requirements, update-trace obligations, reward sensitivity rules, and diagnostic-only triggers.

### 14. Layer 10 Dashboard, Card, Export, and Reproducibility Obligations

Layer 10 must render A10 from saved records and manifests only. It may not update a bandit policy, retune rewards, hide negative results, repair missing traces, create hidden matched groups, or mutate source records.

| Layer 10 output | Required source inputs | Required warning / limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Contextual bandit overview page | Bandit policy artifact, bandit `PolicyActionRecord`, run manifest, config hash, seed | `simulation_only`, `proxy_readiness`, update/frozen mode visible |
| Reward/regret curves | `RewardTraceRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, comparator ID, metric dictionary ID, matched keys | Diagnostic if reward config, regret baseline, or metric dictionary missing |
| Exploration burden and action-probability view | Exploration logs, action-probability traces, legality-mask IDs | Warn on unbounded/illegal exploration or missing probabilities |
| Wrong-accept-over-time and action distribution | `PolicyActionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, evaluation labels used only for scoring, matched groups | Public EEG proxy only; no real safety claim |
| Policy stability / seed sensitivity view | Seed manifest, rollout summaries, reward/regret summaries | Warn if ranking unstable or run count unconfirmed |
| Update-trace completeness card | `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update/no-mutation audit | Missing trace blocks update-enabled claim |
| Frozen-evaluation card | Frozen policy artifact, held-out split/session IDs, no-mutation evidence | Mutation during evaluation blocks frozen superiority claim |
| Matched comparison table | `MatchedComparisonReport`, comparator source records, metric dictionary IDs | Missing baseline or key narrows claim or marks diagnostic |
| Reward/cost sensitivity matrix | Reward configs, sensitivity grid, reward/regret summaries | Reward-sensitive ranking must be labeled and downgraded |
| Stress-conditioned A10 view | Stress profiles/schedules, clean/stressed matched keys | `stress_conditioned` and `simulation_only`; absent stress records mean no stress claim |
| Negative-result page | `NegativeResultNote` records | Negative results must remain visible and exportable |
| Diagnostic-only warning surface | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, environment diagnostics, missingness reports | Diagnostic labels must be visible in dashboard and exports |
| Controller card / source bundle | Policy identity, inputs, action space, reward design, update/frozen status, baselines, metrics, failures, limitations, lineage | Card is derived/reporting output, not primary evidence |
| Reproducibility/export package | Run registry, artifact manifest, config files, source record IDs, seeds, code version where available | Export incomplete if source lineage or config hashes missing |

### 15. Layer 0 Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

#### 15.1 Allowed bounded A10 claim classes

A10 may support only bounded claims such as:

| Allowed claim class | Required evidence | Required limitation wording |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation-only immediate-reward adaptation behavior | Valid A10 bandit runs, reward/regret source records, matched baselines, update/frozen separation | “in a declared simulated closed-loop readiness environment” |
| Public EEG proxy-readiness comparison | Source-traceable public-data records, split-safe contexts, matched comparison reports | “public-data/proxy-readiness evidence, not clinical readiness” |
| Contextual bandit baseline sufficiency or insufficiency | A10 compared to best fixed, IHARQ-lite, learning-to-defer, and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ where available | “under the tested reward/config/simulator assumptions” |
| Stress-conditioned simulated adaptation | Valid Phase 9 stress profiles and matched clean/stressed keys | “stress-conditioned simulation-only result” |
| Negative-result / limitation evidence | Negative-result notes, reward/seed sensitivity, diagnostic flags | “evidence constrains or narrows the claim rather than proving deployment failure” |

#### 15.2 Forbidden A10 claim classes

A10 must not support or imply:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real-time deployment safety;
- real muscle stimulation or real assistive-control success;
- validated therapeutic effectiveness;
- clinical fatigue diagnosis;
- real physiological stress validation;
- real online adaptive control in patients;
- real-world embodied control validation;
- superiority of RL or delayed-consequence learning;
- embodiment-aware benefit without Layer 9 records;
- dashboard-generated plots as primary evidence.

#### 15.3 Required limitation labels

A10 outputs must carry the strictest applicable labels from the source records and evaluation mode: `public_eeg_only`, `proxy_readiness`, `evaluation_only`, `simulation_only`, `stress_conditioned` where applicable, `pseudo_label_based` where inherited from upstream learned labels, `embodiment_proxy_only` only for downstream optional branches, `diagnostic_only` when required, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, `not_medical_device_readiness`, `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`, and `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`.

### 16. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Interpretation

| Outcome | Interpretation | Required reporting |
|---|---|---|
| A10 fails to beat best-fixed policy | Fixed policy may be sufficient under the declared reward/simulator; online adaptation not justified for that setting | `NegativeResultNote`; baseline-sufficiency note; no superiority claim |
| A10 beats weak baselines but not A8/A9 | Learned deferral or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ may be sufficient; A10 complexity not justified | Narrow claim; disclose stronger baseline result |
| A10 helps only during adaptation but not frozen evaluation | Online adaptation behavior exists, but frozen-policy generalization is unsupported | Separate curves; no frozen superiority claim |
| A10 helps only under stress/drift | Adaptation may be conditionally useful under those simulated conditions | Stress-conditioned limitation; requires Phase 9 matched keys |
| A10 increases wrong accepts or unsafe proxy events | Reward design or exploration may be unsafe/proxy-bad in simulation | Diagnostic-only or negative safety-proxy result; forbidden real-safety claims blocked |
| A10 ranking changes under reward/cost sensitivity | Result is reward-sensitive and should not be treated as robust | Reward-sensitivity downgrade and matrix |
| A10 ranking changes across seeds | Result is seed-sensitive and may be exploratory | Seed-sensitivity note; exact run-count criteria require confirmation |
| Regret baseline is undefined or unfair | Regret curve cannot support thesis-facing adaptation claim | Diagnostic-only regret reporting |
| Simulator diagnostics reveal invalid transitions/rewards | A10 may be measuring simulator defects | Block or diagnostic-only until Phase 8/Layer 7 repair |
| A10 overfits stress schedule | Stress-conditioned gain is not general robustness evidence | Held-out stress-seed limitation; downgrade |

Negative results are valid thesis evidence when traceable to run IDs, config hashes, matched keys, metric dictionary entries, diagnostic labels, and Layer 0 limitation tags.

### 17. Diagnostic-Only Downgrade Triggers

A10 must be marked diagnostic-only, or narrower than thesis-ready, when any of the following applies:

| Trigger | Downgrade consequence |
|---|---|
| Invalid or missing Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundation | A10 evidence cannot be thesis-ready |
| Missing or invalid upstream source records | Affected comparison blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Invalid Phase 8 simulated environment, transition, reward, or diagnostic records | A10 blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Hidden labels, decoder correctness, future reward, future next state, oracle costs, or future embodiment outcomes in policy-visible context | A10 leakage failure; no claim evidence |
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` source IDs or observable-field declaration | Context evidence diagnostic-only |
| Missing action legality mask or unsupported action token | Policy output invalid or blocked |
| Illegal selected action in thesis-facing evaluation | Run diagnostic-only and safety warning required |
| Unversioned reward/cost model or post-hoc reward tuning | Reward/regret claims blocked |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for any mutation | Update-enabled A10 claim blocked |
| Mutation during held-out frozen evaluation | Frozen superiority claim blocked |
| Adaptation and frozen-evaluation curves mixed | Curves diagnostic-only until separated |
| Missing disabled-update/no-mutation audit for frozen evaluation | Frozen evaluation not thesis-ready |
| Missing held-out subject/session/seed separation for generalization claim | Generalization claim blocked |
| Missing or weak baselines without claim narrowing | Superiority claim blocked or narrowed |
| Missing `MatchedComparisonReport` | Thesis-facing comparison blocked |
| Missing `MetricDictionaryEntry` for reward/regret/exploration/safety metrics | Metric dashboard-only or diagnostic-only |
| Missing Phase 9 stress profiles or unmatched stress keys for stress-conditioned A10 | Stress-conditioned claim blocked |
| Safety-event alias/path unresolved where material | Safety summary warning-only or diagnostic-only |
| Missing negative-result note for failed/flat/unsafe/reward-sensitive result | Claim package incomplete |
| Missing diagnostic-only flag for invalid run | Claim-safety failure |
| Missing Layer 10 source/export lineage | Dashboard/export not thesis-ready |
| Missing claim-evidence entry or limitation tags | Phase 15 claim integration blocked |
| Clinical, deployment, real-safety, rehabilitation, stimulation-control, or medical-device wording appears | Forbidden claim blocked by Layer 0 |

### 18. Open Issues and Requires-Confirmation Items

| Open issue | Status | A10 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` exact schema/path and shared producer lifecycle | `requires_confirmation` | Update-enabled A10 invalid without trace; exact storage unresolved | Use registry-supported fields and manifest-map path until finalized |
| Disabled-update audit exact schema/name/path | `requires_confirmation` | Frozen evaluation requires no-mutation proof | Record audit artifact and preserve unresolved name/path |
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 materialization boundary | `unresolved_ownership_nuance` | Simulation-visible context variants may be run-specific or adapter outputs | Keep Layer 6 semantic ownership and manifest-map Layer 7 instances |
| `SafetyEventRecord` vs safety-event CSV/log aliases | `unresolved_alias_path_conflict` | Safety proxy summaries may be warning-only if linkage unclear | Use canonical name with storage alias mapping and visible warning |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path | `requires_confirmation` | Reward/regret/exploration metrics not thesis-ready without definitions | Require metric dictionary entries before claims |
| Regret baseline definition | `requires_confirmation_per_run` | Regret claims invalid if oracle/best-fixed baseline is undefined | Declare best-fixed/oracle comparator and matching rule before evaluation |
| Reward/cost sensitivity grid and downgrade threshold | `requires_confirmation` | Robustness of A10 ranking cannot be finalized | Mark sensitivity results as v0.1 requirements, exact thresholds deferred |
| Seed sensitivity and minimum run count | `requires_confirmation` | Bandit stability may be overclaimed | Defer exact final seeds/run counts/statistical tests |
| Bandit algorithm/hyperparameter grid | `requires_confirmation` | v0.1 cannot prescribe final algorithm choices beyond allowed families | Treat exact grid as v1.0/final-run item |
| Repository paths for bandit outputs | `unresolved_path_status` | Artifact discovery may fragment | Use manifest-mapped paths and do not assert unsupported final homes |
| ClaimEvidenceMatrix vs ClaimEvidenceManifest naming | `unresolved_alias_governance` | Phase 15 claim linkage must preserve naming ambiguity | Preserve both names or explicit mapping until final registry resolves |
| Dashboard/export route and ID conventions | `deferred_to_phase14` | A10 can prepare source bundles but not final dashboard routes | Defer exact routes/IDs to Layer 10/Phase 14 |
| Stress-conditioned A10 pointer/view names | `requires_confirmation_inherited_from_phase9` | Stress claims may be diagnostic if stress lineage naming unresolved | Preserve candidate status and matched clean/stressed keys |
| Optional embodiment reward terms | `downstream_optional_requires_confirmation` | Core A10 cannot include A13 claims | Defer to Phase 12/13 and Layer 9 records if implemented |

## A11 — Reinforcement-Learning Policy / Simulation-Bounded Sequential Policy Learning

### 0. A11 Document-Control Audit and Target Resolution

**Protocol version:** v0.1  
**Target section generated in this append:** A11  
**Target identity:** Reinforcement-learning policy, where source-supported and simulation-bounded.  
**Output mode:** append new section to existing protocol.  
**Previous protocol sections provided:** A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10.  
**Current append handling:** the supplied A0–A10 protocol document is preserved unchanged in this assembled output. This A11 section is appended after the supplied A0–A10 content. No previous section is deleted, shortened, silently re-scoped, or stylistically rewritten.

A11 is a global ablation/evaluation-use identifier. It is not Phase 11, not Layer 6, not Layer 7, not a module owner, not an artifact producer, not a dashboard page, and not deployed or clinical controller evidence. The source-supported implementation/evidence phase that primarily produces A11 reinforcement-learning evidence is **Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy**. The semantic producing architecture layer for RL policy outputs is **Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer**, especially the reinforcement-learning readiness-policy branch. **Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment** owns the transition, reward, session, rollout, environment-diagnostic, and simulation safety/proxy evidence used to evaluate delayed consequences. A11 consumes records produced by official layers and phases; A11 itself does not produce records.

A11 evaluates whether sequential policy learning under delayed simulated consequences provides defensible value beyond simpler policies, especially fixed baselines, threshold/selective-prediction controls, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality-aware policies, RegimeRisk-aware context, learning-to-defer, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, and the A10 contextual-bandit baseline. It must be simulation-only, reward-configuration-bound, update-trace-complete where policy mutation occurs, and evaluated through held-out frozen rollouts that cannot mutate the policy.

| Control item | A11 handling |
|---|---|
| Official A-ID | A11 only; no new top-level ablation ID is introduced |
| Correct normalized identity | Reinforcement-learning policy / simulation-bounded sequential policy learning under delayed consequences |
| Primary producer/consumer boundary | Layer 6 / Phase 11 is the source-supported producer context for RL policy artifacts and `PolicyActionRecord` rows emitted for RL policies, action-space declarations, reward/cost policy settings, policy-family identity, and controller-card source content. Layer 7 owns or materializes `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, and `SafetyEventRecord` where simulation/proxy events are materialized. Evaluation artifacts such as `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, metric dictionaries, and claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries are produced or prepared by evaluation, Layer 10, Layer 0, or final-reporting workflows, not by A11 as an ablation owner. |
| Primary upstream evidence context | Phases 0–10 records: schema/config/run foundations; clean public-data lineage; decoder predictions; calibration/uncertainty/threshold/selective-prediction evidence; IHARQ-lite evidence-verification records; RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss records where active; supervised Adaptive-IHARQ and learning-to-defer records; stable Phase 8/Layer 7 simulation environment; Phase 9 stress records only for stress-conditioned A11 claims; A10 contextual-bandit evidence where validated. |
| Primary scientific role | Tests whether delayed-consequence RL adds value beyond immediate-reward bandit adaptation and other simpler validated policy families, and identifies when RL is unstable, reward-sensitive, seed-sensitive, overfit, unsafe in proxy simulation, or unnecessary. |

Exact datasets, final seeds, number of runs, statistical tests, RL algorithm/hyperparameter grids, reward-weight grids, command lines, dashboard routes, and table/figure numbering remain `requires_confirmation` unless later source-fixed. |

### 3. Target Identity and Scientific Purpose

#### 3.1 Official A11 identity

A11 is the reinforcement-learning policy evaluation section. It evaluates sequential decision policies under delayed simulated consequences inside the declared Layer 7 environment. It is a Stretch C policy-learning branch, not a required proof of core IHARQ validity and not a clinical deployment claim.

#### 3.2 Scientific question

The A11 scientific question is:

```text
Under public-data, proxy-readiness, and simulation-only assumptions, does a frozen RL policy trained or adapted under a declared reward/cost configuration improve delayed-consequence return, wrong-accept/safety-proxy behavior, waiting/request/fallback/deferral burden, policy stability, or stress-conditioned behavior beyond simpler validated policies, when evaluated on held-out frozen rollouts with complete lineage, update traces, matched keys, and limitation tags?
```

A11 is scientifically useful even when RL fails. A negative A11 result can show that delayed-consequence policy learning is unnecessary, unstable, reward-sensitive, seed-sensitive, or simulator-overfit relative to simpler and more interpretable baselines. The protocol must preserve that result through `NegativeResultNote`, diagnostic flags, Layer 10 warnings, and Layer 0 claim downgrade rather than hiding it.

#### 3.3 What A11 must not answer

A11 must not be framed as evidence that the system is safe for real patients, ready for clinical BCI-FES, able to control real muscle stimulation, effective for rehabilitation, medically deployable, or validated for real-world embodied control. A11 can only support bounded claims about simulation-only policy learning under declared public-data/proxy assumptions.

### 4. Relationship to Official Layers 0–10

| Layer | A11 relationship | Ownership and boundary rule |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews A11 wording, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, negative-result handling, and forbidden claims | Does not produce RL evidence; blocks clinical, deployment, rehabilitation, real-safety, real-control, or medical-device claims |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies immutable dataset/window/split/label/preprocessing lineage inherited through downstream records | Clean source records cannot be overwritten by RL training, simulation, stress, dashboard filtering, or post-hoc repair |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies predictions, model IDs, baseline metrics, model provenance, and decoder-card source context | Decoder records are upstream evidence; not policy updates or RL outputs |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibrated probabilities, uncertainty scores, threshold registry entries, selective-prediction records, and reliability warnings | Thresholds/calibration must be frozen according to split rules; reliability diagnostics cannot leak into decision-time state unless legally past and declared |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies IHARQ decisions, action tokens, evidence quality, fallback/unsafe/request/wait logic, and trace context | RL may consume or compare with IHARQ output but must not erase canonical IHARQ token lineage |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Supplies regime/trust/stop-loss context where enabled | Regime/trust fields remain operational proxy temporal-trust evidence, not clinical fatigue or patient-risk evidence |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Primary semantic owner of RL policy artifacts and `PolicyActionRecord` rows emitted for RL policies, action-space declarations, policy configs, reward/cost policy settings, and controller-card source bundles | Must distinguish policy training/adaptation from held-out frozen evaluation and preserve policy-update trace requirements |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Runs simulation, applies actions, validates legality, returns transitions/rewards/next states, writes rollout/session/episode/diagnostic records, and logs update/frozen separation | Owns simulation evidence; frozen evaluation must not mutate policy; delayed outcomes remain simulated/proxy only |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Supplies `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord` only for stress-conditioned A11 analysis | Stress is conditional; stress records remain Layer 8-owned and must not overwrite clean records |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite / OpenSim / Static-Replay Embodiment | Optional downstream context if later embodiment records are available and explicitly included | Core A11 does not require embodiment records; embodiment-aware RL terms are `downstream_context_only` until Phase 12/13 support exists |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, Export, and Reproducibility | Reads saved A11 source records, renders controller/reward/update/stress cards, warnings, comparison views, and reproducibility packages | Must not train, tune, mutate, repair, hide negative results, or convert diagnostic-only evidence into thesis-ready claims |

### 5. Relationship to Official Phase 0–15 Sequence

A11 depends on official Phase 0–15 evidence production. The ablation ID is not a phase; Phase 11 is the main implementation/evidence-production phase for A11.

| Phase | A11 use | Required status for thesis-facing A11 |
|---:|---|---|
| Phase 0 — Repository, configuration, and record schema | Schema/config/validator/run ID/config hash/seed/manifest foundations | Required; gaps must be logged and downgraded |
| Phase 1 — Public data and split protocol | Immutable dataset/window/split/label/preprocessing lineage and matched keys | Required; missing split/source lineage blocks thesis-ready A11 |
| Phase 2 — Baseline decoders | `PredictionRecord`, model provenance, raw/accept-all baseline context | Required for decoder-grounded readiness states and baseline comparisons |
| Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty | `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord` | Required when used in readiness context or comparators; leakage invalidates comparison |
| Phase 4 — IHARQ-lite evidence verification | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, evidence quality, fallback/unsafe/request/wait trace context | Required for IHARQ baselines and canonical action-token lineage |
| Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust | `RegimeStateRecord` and optional `TrustStateRecord` where active | Conditional; required only for RegimeRisk-aware A11 claims |
| Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned evidence-quality branch, supervised policy baseline | Required for policy-context assembly and A9 comparator where source-supported |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | `DeferralRecord` and deferral/routing baseline evidence | Required when A8/A11 deferral burden comparison is claimed |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | `TransitionRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` | Hard prerequisite for A11 thesis-facing simulation evidence |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress manifests and validity reports | Required only for stress-conditioned A11 claims |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | A10 immediate-reward adaptation baseline, update-trace conventions, reward/regret context | Strong comparator where validated; absence narrows or downgrades A11 claims |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | Main A11 evidence phase: RL policy configs/artifacts/actions, update traces, frozen held-out rollouts, reward/stability/sensitivity evidence | Required for A11 |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | Optional downstream embodiment records | `downstream_context_only` for core A11; required only for embodiment-aware RL claims |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison | Optional downstream replay/embodiment comparison | `downstream_context_only` unless explicitly evaluated |
| Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards | Dashboard/card/export/reproducibility rendering | Required for final dashboard-ready A11 reporting, but not producer of empirical RL evidence |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | Final claim-evidence, limitation, paper/thesis integration | Required for final thesis claim wording |

### 6. Relationship to A0–A13 and Capability Tiers C0–C4

| Neighbor / comparator | A11 relationship | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A0–A4 | Decoder, calibration, threshold/selective, longer-window/multi-window/voting/ordinary controls | Provide non-policy and ordinary-control baselines; cannot be treated as RL policies |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite rule-based evidence verification | Interpretable readiness baseline; canonical tokens must be preserved |
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Evidence-quality-aware comparator and possible context source |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Regime/trust-aware comparator and context source when active |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Deferral-aware non-RL baseline; sufficiency is a valid negative A11 result |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Frozen supervised adaptive readiness baseline; proxy labels remain non-clinical |
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Immediate-reward adaptation baseline and update-trace/frozen-evaluation continuity source |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Target section: delayed-consequence sequential policy learning in simulation |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests | Stress-conditioned A11 analysis is valid only with Phase 9/Layer 8 stress records and matched stress keys |
| A13 | Layer 9 embodiment demo | Downstream/optional; not required for core A11 and not a real embodied-control validation |

#### 6.1 Capability-tier relationship

| Capability tier | A11 relevance | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| C0–C2 | A11 not required | Core public-data, reliability, IHARQ, and non-RL policy evidence can remain valid without RL |
| C3 | Directly relevant | Bandit/RL simulation layer; A11 may contribute only if Layer 7 simulation and update/frozen separation are valid |
| C4 | Conditional stretch relevance | A11 may feed advanced simulation/stress/optional embodiment narratives, but only with stress/embodiment records and non-clinical limitation tags |
