### 4. Protocol-Wide Negative-Result Interpretation Rules

#### 4.1 Core rule

A negative result is any result in which an evaluated component fails, underperforms, matches a simpler baseline, cannot be fairly matched, collapses under a declared stress/simulation/embodiment condition, lacks required records, lacks metric-dictionary support, lacks Layer 10 export lineage, or cannot pass Layer 0 claim-safety review.

A negative result must never be hidden, silently dropped from the ablation table, converted into a stronger claim by selective wording, or treated as proof of a clinical/deployment property. It must be recorded as one or more of the following, depending on source support:

| Negative-result artifact / status object | Required role | Source-status discipline |
|---|---|---|
| `NegativeResultNote` | Captures bounded interpretation, failure/non-improvement/baseline-sufficiency reason, and claim downgrade | Registry-supported evaluation/claim-governance artifact; exact schema may require confirmation |
| `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Preserves evaluated result, ablation ID, metric dictionary reference, matched-comparison key, and diagnostic status | Use source-supported fields only; layer-specific contexts remain under producer ownership |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Records match status, missing keys, unmatched/partial status, and consequence for fair comparison | Required for thesis-ready comparison; missing report downgrades comparison |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Marks incomplete, exploratory, unsupported, unmatched, or claim-unsafe evidence | Must not be removed by Layer 10 or claim writing |
| `FailureCaseIndex` / failure taxonomy where available | Surfaces failure cases, representative examples, failure categories, and limitation context | Used only where source-supported; no patient-safety interpretation |
| `DashboardMetricRecord` / `DashboardViewRecord` warning fields | Makes negative result visible in Layer 10 dashboard/export/card views | Derived/read-only only; not primary empirical evidence |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` row | Links claim, metric, ablation, negative-result note, limitation, warning, and export lineage | Alias/schema issue remains open; do not silently resolve the name conflict |

#### 4.2 Baseline-sufficiency rule

If a simpler baseline is sufficient, the protocol must treat that as a valid scientific finding, not as a failed experiment. A simpler baseline may include A0 raw decoder behavior, A1 calibration visibility, A2 thresholding, A3 uncertainty/selective prediction, A4 ordinary controls, A8 deferral baselines, non-learning policies, or other source-supported controls. The correct claim is narrowed to the observed evidence.

| Baseline-sufficiency scenario | Required interpretation | Forbidden interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| A0 is sufficient or hard to beat | Raw decoder baseline establishes a strong reference or exposes limited added value of later machinery | Do not claim advanced modules improve readiness without matched evidence |
| A1 calibration adds little or worsens metrics | Calibration visibility is still informative; reliability limitations must be shown | Do not hide calibration failure or imply reliability improvement |
| A2 registered threshold matches richer methods | Threshold sufficiency narrows the need for complex uncertainty/IHARQ claims | Do not relabel A2 as A3 or A5 |
| A3 uncertainty/selective prediction is sufficient | Selective uncertainty behavior may explain most benefit under matched cost/coverage | Do not overstate IHARQ/policy novelty |
| A4 ordinary controls outperform IHARQ/policy branches | Ordinary longer-window/voting/ensemble controls are meaningful comparators | Do not present IHARQ superiority as settled |
| A8 deferral baseline matches adaptive policies | Deferral may be an adequate control under declared costs | Do not claim policy learning is necessary |
| Non-learning or frozen policies beat bandit/RL | Learned adaptation may be unstable or reward-sensitive | Do not claim deployed adaptive control readiness |
| Clean baseline performs better than stressed branch | Stress exposes robustness limits | Do not treat stress failure as clinical/physiological failure evidence |
| Static/proxy embodiment fails or is skipped | Embodiment remains optional/proxy/future-work as appropriate | Do not infer real embodiment safety or efficacy |
| Dashboard/export lineage is incomplete | Traceability/reproducibility claim is weakened or diagnostic-only | Do not infer upstream model performance changed unless source lineage is invalid |

#### 4.3 Negative-result interpretation by global ablation context

| Global context | Negative-result examples | Required bounded interpretation | Required Layer 10 surface | Required Layer 0 consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder weak, unstable, missing scores, score schema incomplete | Establishes baseline difficulty, data/protocol limitation, or missing evidence condition | Baseline table, failure cases, missing-score warning | No readiness/safety claim; public-data-only limitation |
| A1 | Calibration does not improve ECE/Brier/NLL, reliability curves worsen, high-confidence wrong cases persist | Calibration visibility still documents reliability limits; improvement claim blocked unless supported | Reliability card, calibration plot, negative-result note | Claim narrowed to calibration audit/visibility |
| A2 | Threshold harms coverage, selected post-hoc, missing threshold registry, or fails to beat raw decoder | Threshold baseline is insufficient or invalid if split rules fail | Threshold table, operating-point warning, registry warning | Diagnostic-only or invalid if threshold selection leaks test information |
| A3 | Uncertainty/selective prediction does not improve risk/coverage or lacks metric definitions | Rich uncertainty/selective behavior not sufficient under current evidence | Risk-coverage view, uncertainty feature warning | Claim weakened or diagnostic-only |
| A4 | Voting/averaging/longer-window/ordinary ensemble controls underperform, outperform, or cannot be fairly matched | Ordinary controls define an important baseline; success narrows advanced-module novelty | Ordinary-control card/table with delay/matching warnings | Improvement claims over ordinary controls blocked if unmatched |
| A5 | IHARQ does not reduce wrong accepts, increases burden, or reason-code lineage incomplete | Rule-based verification may be too costly, insufficient, or incompletely evidenced | IHARQ reason-code/failure dashboard and negative-result note | IHARQ claim weakened or diagnostic-only |
| A6 | Evidence-quality estimator adds no value, leaks labels, or target construction unsupported | Learned evidence-quality branch becomes optional/diagnostic unless source-legal | Estimator trace card, target-construction warning | No learned-readiness claim if target invalid |
| A7 | RegimeRisk adds no benefit, shuffled/random control matches, or temporal leakage found | Temporal trust context is not supported as improvement; may still expose instability | Regime timeline, negative-control report, leakage warning | Temporal-trust claim diagnostic-only/invalid if leakage exists |
| A8 | Deferral baseline does not improve cost/coverage or expert/fallback assumption unsupported | Deferral framing may be weak or assumption-bound | Deferral cost/coverage export and assumption warning | Deferral claim narrowed to proxy/computational setting |
| A9 | Supervised adaptive policy overfits or pseudo-labels unsupported | Policy evidence is proxy-label and may be non-thesis-ready | Controller card with pseudo-label/source warning | Adaptive-policy claim diagnostic-only or future-work-only |
| A10 | Bandit instability, reward sensitivity, insufficient held-out performance | Contextual bandit remains simulation-only and reward-dependent | Bandit reward/update trace card | No deployed adaptation claim |
| A11 | RL instability, seed sensitivity, delayed-reward collapse, unsafe simulated events | RL branch may be optional/stretch/diagnostic; instability is a valid result | RL rollout/reward/safety-event view | Simulation-only, no real-world control/safety claim |
| A12 | Stress collapse, sensitivity to intensity, unmatched clean/stressed records | Robustness limits are visible controlled-stress evidence | StressCard, clean/stressed matched table | Stress-only limitation; no physiological stress claim |
| A13 | Adapter failure, command mapping invalid, simulator skipped, safety event proxy appears | Embodiment remains simulated/proxy/optional or future-work as appropriate | EmbodimentCard, demo-manifest warning | No clinical, FES, real-patient, or rehabilitation claim |

#### 4.4 Required fields for a negative-result note

The exact serialized schema for `NegativeResultNote` remains a registry/schema confirmation item. Protocol `v0.1` nevertheless requires that every negative-result note, equivalent row, or linked status object preserve the following information where applicable:

| Field family | Required content | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | `negative_result_note_id`, run ID, config hash, source record IDs, schema version | v0.1 requirement; exact field names may be finalized later |
| Evaluation context | global ablation ID A0--A13, optional local sub-ablation ID, layer, phase, evaluation mode | v0.1 requirement |
| Comparison context | comparison ID, matched-key status, baseline/comparator, metric dictionary ID | v0.1 requirement |
| Negative-result class | non-improvement, weaker-than-baseline, baseline sufficiency, missingness, validation failure, leakage, stress collapse, policy instability, embodiment failure, dashboard/export missingness, claim-safety violation | v0.1 requirement |
| Evidence state | thesis-ready, weakened, diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work-only, blocked, or invalid | v0.1 requirement |
| Interpretation | bounded statement of what the result does and does not show | v0.1 requirement |
| Layer 10 lineage | dashboard/card/export/reproducibility warning reference | v0.1 requirement when exported |
| Layer 0 claim consequence | allowed claim class, forbidden claim class, limitation tags, downgrade action | v0.1 requirement |
| Open issue link | candidate/unresolved/alias/schema/metric/phase-dependency issue if applicable | v0.1 requirement |

#### 4.5 Negative-result downgrade matrix

| Trigger | Minimum status | Claim handling | Required visible artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valid matched result but no improvement over simpler baseline | `weakened` or `baseline_sufficient` | Narrow claim to baseline sufficiency or limited added value | `NegativeResultNote`, ablation table row, dashboard warning/card |
| Missing metric dictionary entry or undefined formula/direction/denominator | `diagnostic_only` | No thesis-ready metric claim | Metric dictionary gap note, diagnostic flag |
| Missing matched-comparison keys | `diagnostic_only` or `invalid` depending on key criticality | No fair-comparison claim | `MatchedComparisonReport` with missing keys |
| Test-set threshold tuning or post-hoc operating point selection | `invalid` | Block threshold/selective/comparison claim | Leakage/invalid note, Layer 0 claim block |
| Missing source record IDs, schema version, config hash, seed, or validation state | `blocked` or `diagnostic_only` | No thesis-ready claim until restored | Validation/failure record and dashboard missingness warning |
| Dashboard/export lacks source lineage or reproducibility manifest | `weakened` for dashboard/reproducibility claim; may become `diagnostic_only` for final reporting if source trace cannot be established | Do not use dashboard output as thesis-ready evidence | Layer 10 missing-lineage warning, export manifest gap |
| Claim uses clinical, medical-device, real-patient, real-time deployment, therapeutic, FES-safety, or real-world embodiment wording | `forbidden` or `invalid` | Claim must be blocked or rewritten | `InvalidClaimFlag` / claim ledger entry |
| Policy-update and frozen-evaluation curves are mixed | `invalid` for policy comparison | Block policy improvement claim | Policy update/frozen separation warning |
| Clean source record overwritten by stress/simulation/embodiment/dashboard mutation | `invalid` | Block affected comparison and reproducibility claim | Source-record immutability violation note |
| Candidate/unresolved registry item silently promoted | `blocked` until status is restored | No claim dependent on promoted object | Open issue carried into handoff |

### 5. Protocol-Wide Sub-Ablation Policy

#### 5.1 Core rule

Sub-ablations are allowed only as local children of official global A0--A13 evaluation contexts. They are local bookkeeping labels for variants, controls, rows, or diagnostic comparisons. They do not create new global ablations, new phases, new layers, new modules, new record owners, or new claim authority.

Correct examples:

```text
A5.local.no_fallback
A12.local.dropout_stress
A13.local.static_replay_only
local_sub_ablation_id: A4.longer_window_control
parent_global_ablation_id: A4
```

Incorrect examples:

```text
A14
Phase A5
Layer A12
A4 produces EnsembleControlRecord
A5 owns IHARQDecisionRecord
```

#### 5.2 Required sub-ablation metadata

Every local sub-ablation row must include, at minimum, the following metadata before it can be used in a thesis-facing comparison.

| Required field | Purpose | Missingness consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `local_sub_ablation_id` | Local row identity; must be unique only within parent/global context | Row cannot be linked or exported reliably |
| `parent_global_ablation_id` | Official A0--A13 parent | Row invalid if parent is not A0--A13 |
| `variant_definition` | Describes what is removed, added, changed, frozen, stressed, or compared | Diagnostic-only if ambiguous |
| `required_config_difference` | Shows the controlled change relative to comparator | Diagnostic-only if no controlled difference is recorded |
| `source_record_ids` | Links to primary producer records | Blocked if missing for claim-relevant rows |
| `producer_layer` and `producer_phase` | Preserves layer/phase ownership | Invalid if ablation is treated as producer |
| `matched_comparison_id` / key status | Connects to fair comparison | Unmatched rows cannot support improvement claims |
| `metric_dictionary_id` / metric status | Connects metrics to definitions | Metric claim diagnostic-only if undefined |
| `layer_10_export_status` | Records dashboard/card/export/reproducibility visibility | Dashboard/reproducibility claim weakened if absent |
| `layer_0_claim_status` | Records allowed, weakened, diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work-only, blocked, invalid, or forbidden status | Claim blocked if absent |
| `negative_result_note_id_if_any` | Preserves non-improvement/failure/baseline-sufficiency result | Required when row fails, is skipped, or is weaker than baseline |
| `registry_status` | Preserves final/candidate/unresolved status of objects used | Silent promotion blocks claim use |
| `v0_1_or_v1_0_status` | Distinguishes current rule requirement from later exact run choice | Exact run matrix claim blocked if not v1.0-confirmed |

#### 5.3 Permitted local sub-ablation families by parent ID

The following table defines permitted local sub-ablation families. It does not require every local row to be run in Protocol `v0.1`; it only defines how such rows must be governed if they are included later.

| Parent ID | Official normalized identity | Permitted local row family where source-supported | Local-only constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder | Decoder family, feature set, low-calibration budget, score availability, accept-all/raw reference rows | No readiness/safety claim from raw performance alone |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder | Calibration method, calibration budget, reliability-audit, no-calibration comparator | Split-safe calibration required; no post-hoc calibration on test |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Threshold type, registered threshold value/rule, matched coverage/cost operating point | Must not absorb uncertainty/selective prediction beyond simple threshold baseline |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Uncertainty feature, selective-prediction rule, risk/coverage operating point, matched cost/coverage row | Must not relabel A2 threshold-only rows or A4 ordinary controls |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Window length, voting rule, averaging rule, ordinary ensemble membership, delay-burden row | Must remain ordinary-control comparison, not IHARQ or selective prediction |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Confidence-only, entropy-only, margin-only, no-stability, no-fallback, no-unsafe, no-combination, fallback-only, regime-unaware where source-supported | Local rows remain IHARQ variants; they do not create new global ablation IDs |
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Rule-derived versus learned evidence-quality, feature-family ablation, estimator calibration row | Target construction and split legality must be explicit |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | With/without temporal trust, stop-loss on/off, shuffled/random risk negative control | No clinical fatigue or patient-state diagnosis |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Deferral cost model, fallback/expert route, oracle/proxy expert assumption, coverage-cost row | Expert/fallback source must be declared |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Policy feature set, pseudo-label family, cost-sensitive row, frozen policy comparator | Pseudo-label and training/evaluation split boundaries required |
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Exploration/update setting, reward/cost configuration, frozen-evaluation row | Simulation-only; update traces separated from evaluation curves |
| A11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Reward design, policy class, rollout horizon, seed-sensitivity row | Simulation-only; held-out rollout and unsafe-event lineage required |
| A12 | StressForge stress tests | Stress family, intensity, schedule, clean/stressed pair, combined-stress row | Clean source records immutable; stress-only limitation required |
| A13 | Layer 9 embodiment demo | Static replay, MyoSuite mode, OpenSim optional replay, adapter/mapping row, command/safety-event row | Simulation/proxy only; no real embodiment/rehabilitation/FES claim |

#### 5.4 Sub-ablation status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning | Thesis-use consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `source_supported` | Local row is supported by architecture/registry/execution evidence and has required records | May be used if matched, metric-defined, exported, and Layer 0-approved |
| `registry_supported` | Local row uses confirmed registry record/artifact names and valid producer-consumer roles | May be used subject to metrics/comparisons |
| `inferred_candidate` | Useful local row or object is plausible but not final in registry/source docs | Must remain candidate and cannot support strong claims alone |
| `requires_confirmation` | Exact schema, formula, path, route, run choice, or naming is not finalized | Carry to open issues; do not pretend resolved |
| `optional_only` | Stretch/local branch not required for core thesis validity | May appear as optional result or appendix only |
| `future_work_only` | Conceptual branch not implemented/evaluable in current scope | No result claim |
| `diagnostic_only` | Useful for debugging/exploration but incomplete/unmatched/undefined | No thesis-ready improvement claim |
| `blocked` | Required records, schema, validation, or claim boundary missing | Do not report as evaluated result |
| `invalid` | Leakage, source mutation, forbidden evidence use, or unsupported recomputation detected | Exclude from claim-supporting tables except as invalidated failure entry |
| `forbidden` | Claim wording or metric class violates project boundary | Block or rewrite claim |

#### 5.5 Sub-ablation comparison requirements

A local sub-ablation can support a comparative statement only if the comparison is properly matched or if the protocol explicitly marks the limitation. The required key envelope inherits the existing matched-comparison rules and includes, where applicable:

- dataset ID;
- subject/session/trial/window identity;
- split ID and split role;
- preprocessing ID;
- label-map ID;
- label-budget ID;
- model ID or model-family ID;
- seed and config hash;
- calibration ID;
- threshold registry ID;
- policy configuration ID;
- reward/cost configuration ID;
- stress profile/schedule ID;
- simulation environment ID;
- embodiment mode / adapter / mapping ID;
- metric dictionary ID;
- run ID;
- Layer 10 export ID;
- claim-evidence row ID where claim-facing.

| Match status | Allowed interpretation |
|---|---|
| `fully_matched` | Thesis-ready only if metrics, exports, and Layer 0 claim review also pass |
| `partially_matched` | Weakened or diagnostic-only; must state missing key and likely bias |
| `unmatched_diagnostic` | Exploratory/diagnostic only; no superiority claim |
| `invalid` | Leakage, source mutation, or unsupported recomputation; claim blocked |
| `not_applicable` | Key not relevant to that target; justification required |

#### 5.6 Sub-ablation Layer 10 and Layer 0 obligations

Layer 10 must expose local sub-ablation rows only as derived/read-only views over saved records. It may filter, summarize, warn, visualize, export, card, and package them, but it must not train models, tune thresholds, create pseudo-labels, alter policy behavior, mutate stress schedules, repair source records, rerun hidden evidence, or upgrade diagnostic-only rows into thesis-ready claims.

Layer 0 must apply the strictest inherited limitation tag from the source evidence and the local row. A local row cannot remove limitations inherited from public data, proxy labels, simulation, stress conditioning, embodiment proxy, dashboard-derived status, optional-only status, or diagnostic-only status.

| Sub-ablation issue | Layer 10 action | Layer 0 action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing local row metadata | Show missingness warning; export incomplete status | Block or diagnostic-only |
| Missing matched-comparison report | Show unmatched/partial match status | No fair-comparison claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Show metric-definition gap | No thesis-ready metric claim |
| Candidate registry object used | Preserve candidate status in view/export | Claim weakened or diagnostic-only |
| Local row outperforms parent/control | Show result with matched keys and limitations | Allow only bounded claim if fully supported |
| Local row fails or baseline is sufficient | Show negative result and link note | Narrow claim; preserve negative-result note |
| Local row implies clinical/deployment claim | Show claim violation if detected | Block/forbid claim |

|---|---|---|
| Registry alias / schema | `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` versus `ClaimEvidenceManifest` | Claim-evidence linkage is required, but exact canonical schema/name needs final reconciliation |
| Registry ambiguity | Standalone `TrialRecord` ambiguity versus trial fields in `WindowRecord` | Use existing trial/window identifiers; do not promote standalone record unless confirmed |
| Dashboard boundary | `DashboardMetricRecord` source-versus-derived boundary | Dashboard metrics are derived/read-only unless future schema states otherwise |
| Schema/path gap | `FigureTableManifest` schema/path and final export manifest IDs/paths | Figures/tables/exports require lineage; final names/paths deferred |
| Metric dictionary gap | Exact metric formulas, denominators, units, directionality, aggregation, statistical tests, and confidence intervals | Metric claims remain diagnostic-only or `requires_metric_dictionary_confirmation` until defined |
| Matched comparison schema | Exact storage schema/path for `MatchedComparisonReport` | Matching rules are required; final implementation details deferred |
| Layer 0 artifact schema | Claim ledger, invalid claim flag, limitation map, claim evidence schema/path | Claim-safety function required; exact storage schema/path deferred |
| Alias conflict | `combine` versus `combine_evidence` | Export canonical/mapped action tokens; unresolved aliases cannot support ambiguous claims |
| Candidate records | `StressedRecordPointer` / `StressedRecordView`, `SafetyEventRecord` storage alias, `Layer9RewardTrace` where relevant | Preserve candidate or unresolved status until registry confirms |
| Phase dependency | Phase 0 templates and validators required before downstream claim use | Downstream claims blocked or diagnostic-only if Phase 0 foundations missing |
| Phase 14 maturity | Static, interactive, or hybrid dashboard exact implementation not fixed | Dashboard obligation exists; exact route/export implementation deferred |
| Phase 15 maturity | Final thesis claim-evidence schema and wording not finalized | Final claim wording and table/figure numbering deferred |
| v1.0 run matrix | Exact dataset list, model set, seeds, run counts, hyperparameter grids, stress intensities, MyoSuite/OpenSim configuration, commands, and paths | Protocol `v0.1` cannot be cited as the final run matrix |

### 9. Concise Final Note on the Newly Added and Revised Assembly Section

This final assembly revision completes the requested `negative-result interpretation rules`, `sub-ablation policy`, and `full protocol assembly / final audit` target. The prior A0--A13 and protocol-wide governance sections remain present above this final section. The revision does not broaden claims or silently resolve unresolved registry issues; it clarifies current full-file status, preserves the corrected A2/A3/A4 identities, and replaces the prior final handoff with the framework-required `protocol_section_handoff` block.

# Controlled Intake Addendum — Layer 1 Finalized Method-Selection Package

**Addendum status:** controlled intake from the finalized Layer 1 Method Selection and Design Rationale Register.  
**Application date:** 2026-07-09.  
**Application mode:** bounded append-only addendum; no existing section above this addendum is rewritten, deleted, renamed, or superseded.  
**Source package consumed:** `Layer1_Method_Selection_Register_MERGED_FINAL_VERIFIED_V7_FINAL_GREENLIGHT_LOCK.md` plus `Layer1_Post_Finalization_Upstream_Update_Impact_Packet_REVISED_METICULOUS_V2.md` and the revised Canonical Registry controlled-intake completeness-lock update.  
**Authority boundary:** this addendum consumes the finalized Layer 1 method-selection package as a downstream planning constraint. It does not create new architecture, canonical records, phase IDs, ablation IDs, implementation paths, CLI commands, final experiment results, dashboard rendering rules, or thesis claims.

## CI-0. Preservation and no-drift statement

# R23 Layer 2 A0/A4 and Measurement-Contract Synchronization Addendum

## R23.1 Scope

This addendum applies stable Layer 2 measurement semantics established by M7. It does not finalize the Protocol v1.0 run matrix, numerical grids, repetitions, alpha/multiplicity, exact interval resample counts, resource ceilings or final statistical software lock.

## R23.2 A0 — raw/accept-all decoder reference

A0 uses eligible raw Layer 2 predictions without Layer 3 calibration, registered thresholds, rejection or selective prediction. Each claim-bearing row must resolve the exact dataset/task, participant/session, source-event/window, split/role, preprocessing, label map, model/version, label budget, seed/repetition, class order, score type and metric dictionary identity.

Primary metric families remain accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-F1 and multiclass AUC only where native score semantics and class support make AUC valid. Complete denominators, failed/missing cells and diagnostic downgrades are mandatory. Participant-first and dataset-stratified summaries prevent trial-rich participants from dominating aggregate claims.

For unresolved/invalid ordinary-control outputs, the internal contingency representation may use K registered classes plus one nonclass unresolved column. Accuracy treats unresolved as error; balanced accuracy and macro-F1 treat unresolved as a false negative for its true class and no false positive for a predicted class. Export remains the standard K×K confusion matrix plus unresolved-by-true-class counts and complete denominators. The unresolved column is never a class.

## R23.3 Low-label evidence

Label-budget subsets must be inherited, legal, class-aware and nested according to Layer 1/Protocol identity. The same frozen evaluation partition and metric semantics apply across budgets. Sparse, invalid or impossible budgets terminate visibly and remain in curve-support and denominator reporting; Layer 2 does not redesign budgets from test outcomes.

## R23.4 A4 — ordinary longer-window, multi-window and ensemble controls

A4 includes only predeclared ordinary controls:

1. longer-window alternatives permitted by the inherited protocol;
2. multi-window hard voting;
3. compatible equal-weight native-probability averaging;
4. fixed ordinary model ensembles;
5. disagreement and delay/burden evidence.

Hard-vote resolution is deterministic: a unique vote maximum wins; a tied vote may use a probability tie-break only when every eligible member provides finite, class-aligned compatible probabilities, and only over tied classes; a unique tied-class probability maximum resolves the case; otherwise it remains unresolved. Truth, correctness, class order and random choice are forbidden tie-breakers.

Probability averaging is an arithmetic ordinary-control comparator, not calibrated confidence. Member sets, compatibility criteria, missing-member policy, zero-member terminal behavior, complete-case rules and aggregation mode are predeclared. Test-time selection of the preferred aggregator or member set is forbidden.

Registered threshold selection, rejection, coverage-risk optimization and selective prediction remain A2/A3 and Layer 3-owned. Confidence-threshold architecture shorthand is interpreted only as preserved score context or an A2-linked diagnostic, not an A4 operating policy.

## R23.5 Matching, aggregation and uncertainty

A0/A4 comparison requires exact matched keys and source-hash closure. Unmatched or incomplete rows are diagnostic-only. Primary effects are paired and participant-first; dataset synthesis is conditional on compatible metric/effect/variance definitions and adequate dataset support. BCa intervals, paired tests, random-effects synthesis and multiplicity procedures remain technically specified by M7 but their exact numerical settings become binding only in Protocol v1.0.

## R23.6 Failure and claim rules

Failed, unsupported, blocked, skipped, zero-member, unresolved and missing-score outcomes cannot disappear from denominators or coverage narratives. `LeakageWarningRecord`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` and `NegativeResultNote` must propagate. Bounded technical tests do not constitute empirical A0/A4 results. Layer 0 retains claim approval.

# R24 Layer 2 Bidirectional Protocol Synchronization Addendum

## R24.1 Authority boundary

The Protocol controls ablation identity, metric and estimand meaning, matched-comparison requirements, denominator rules, statistical decision procedures and the final run matrix. M8 controls the internal algorithms that produce valid source evidence. M8 formulas labeled Protocol-owned or illustrative do not become final experiment settings until Protocol v1.0 accepts them.

## R24.2 Stable versus owner-gated surfaces

| Surface | Stable synchronized rule | Still Protocol v1.0-owned |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | raw/accept-all decoder evidence from validated predictions; participant-first and source-complete | exact run cells, primary/secondary metric set, confidence levels, repetitions and multiplicity |
| A4 | predeclared longer-window, hard-vote, compatible probability-average and fixed ordinary ensemble controls | exact member/window grid, confirmatory rows, resource/burden ceilings and statistical decision rules |
| vote ties | unique vote wins; compatible finite probability tie-break only over tied classes; otherwise unresolved | whether a specific unresolved summary is primary/secondary and final inferential treatment |
| probability averaging | equal-weight compatible native probabilities; not calibration | exact comparator matrix and confirmatory designation |
| low-label | inherited legal nested budgets; no test-driven redesign | exact budget set/repetitions and inferential summaries |
| matching | exact keys, source hashes and denominators; unmatched rows diagnostic-only | final matched key profile if Registry/Protocol v1.0 adds fields |
| participant synthesis | participant-first; conditional dataset synthesis | exact BCa/bootstrap/random-effects/multiplicity parameters |
| A1--A3/A5--A13 | Layer 2 supplies preparation/lineage/readiness only | downstream layer methods and final experiment cells |
| thresholds/rejection | remain Layer 3/A2--A3-owned | exact operating-point selection and selective metrics |

## R24.3 Reverse Protocol workflow

A Protocol change to metric identity, estimand, denominator, matching, run-cell membership, interval, multiplicity, support rule or confirmatory/diagnostic classification triggers an M8 successor where the technical algorithm, record transformation, validation or readiness surface is affected. A technical feasibility finding in M8 is submitted as a Protocol proposal; it cannot silently rewrite A0/A4 meaning.

Test outcomes may not select a new model, budget, aggregation rule, member set or metric. Any accepted protocol correction creates new run/config identities and invalidates dependent metric, comparison, curve, profile, A4, readiness and report products.

# R25 A5 Evaluation and Ablation Synchronization Addendum

**Applied status:** `CURRENT-STAGE SYNCHRONIZATION APPLIED`  
**Compatibility set:** `L4-METHOD-SELECTION-POST-FINALIZATION-SYNC-R1-20260718`  
**Prepared:** 18 July 2026

## 1. Authority boundary

This addendum freezes method identities, eligibility, matching, metric-family and negative-result obligations for A5. It does not set final equations, alpha/SESOI values, resampling counts, delay targets, horizons or the run matrix; those remain Protocol v1.0.

## 2. Required A5 bindings

| EVAL-L4-MS-001 | Integrated A5 identity | Freeze A5 as the complete deterministic Layer 4 portfolio; no selected base/core/stretch split and no A14. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-002 | Comparator preservation | Preserve A0 raw/accept-all, A1 calibrated, A2 registered-threshold, A3 uncertainty/selective and A4 ordinary temporal/ensemble controls. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-003 | Exact local A5 labels | Freeze exactly eleven local labels; logging/export removals remain diagnostic analyses unless separately approved. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-004 | Branch/capability eligibility | Evaluate a local removal only where the removed component existed, was valid and was used; otherwise N/A/diagnostic. |

| EVAL-L4-MS-006 | Denominator, independent unit and attrition | Every metric/report declares denominator, independent unit, aggregation level, support count, missing-cell/attrition reasons and branch eligibility. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-007 | Metric-family binding | Bind reliability/wrong-accept, coverage/effective coverage, action/request/wait/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe, delay/tail, burden/cost, trace/reason and degraded-evidence families to approved MetricDictionary entries. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-008 | Evidence-quality/comparability evaluation | Preserve component states, partial order and incomparability; never treat an optional overall category as correctness probability. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-009 | Dependence/common-mode evaluation | Report overlap groups, dependence clusters, effective-source count, correlated/common-mode failures, contradiction and insufficient diversity. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-010 | Request, wait, combination and route burden | Measure evidence count, reservation/timeout/exhaustion, compute/storage/latency, fallback availability/failure and unsafe recovery burden. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-011 | No-harm and overconservatism | Require coverage/burden/delay/fallback collapse and simpler-control parity/noninferiority/equivalence or explicit negative result where applicable. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-012 | Negative-result outcome taxonomy | Preserve beneficial, harmful/degraded, practically equivalent, inconclusive/underpowered, invalid/ineligible and diagnostic-only outcomes with claim impact. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-013 | Baseline sufficiency | A2/A3/A4 or simpler controls matching/surpassing A5 must narrow claims and create NegativeResultNote rather than be hidden. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-014 | Inference-family boundary | Participant-aware paired/hierarchical inference and uncertainty intervals are selected as families; exact alpha, resamples, SESOI, horizons and cutovers remain Protocol v1.0. |

| EVAL-L4-MS-016 | A7 boundary | Core A5 is regime-unaware; A7 uses causal Layer 5 context in a separately versioned matched rerun. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-017 | A12/A13 and simulation boundaries | Stress, simulation and embodiment contexts retain clean/stressed and source-action/consumer-action separation and proxy-only claim limits. |
| EVAL-L4-MS-018 | v0.1/addendum versus Protocol v1.0 | This addendum freezes identities, eligibility and evidence obligations; equations, constants, run matrix and final statistical serialization remain v1.0-owned. |

## 3. Exact A5 identity

A5 is one integrated deterministic, non-learned, regime-unaware Layer 4 portfolio. A0–A4 remain upstream comparators. A6 and A7 are separate matched contexts. No A14 is created.

## 4. Exact local A5 labels

```text
A5.local.confidence_only
A5.local.entropy_only
A5.local.margin_only
A5.local.no_stability
A5.local.no_combination
A5.local.no_fallback
A5.local.no_unsafe
A5.local.fallback_only
A5.local.no_channel_subset
A5.local.no_model_agreement
A5.local.regime_unaware
```

A local removal is evaluable only when the removed component was available, valid and active for the parent branch. Otherwise the result is N/A or diagnostic-only.

## 5. Minimum matched-key and support envelope

Where applicable, comparison rows carry dataset/task, subject/session/run/trial/window, split/role, label budget, preprocessing/label map, model/checkpoint/family/class order/score type, calibration/uncertainty/threshold/operating point, branch capability, A4 aggregation, A5 rule/config/budget/request/fallback/unsafe identities, local label, context/stress/simulation/embodiment identity, metric/profile version, source closure, denominator, independent unit and attrition/missing-cell status.

## 6. Required metric families

- accepted reliability, wrong accept and unsafe/wrong-accept proxies;
- coverage, effective coverage and retained performance;
- action distribution and reason distribution;
- request, wait, combine, fallback, uncertain and unsafe rates;
- evidence count, burden, compute/storage and delay/tail behavior;
- cost families and budget exhaustion;
- trace/reason/config completeness and replay success;
- contradiction, dependence/common-mode and degraded-evidence outcomes;
- matched deltas against A0–A4 and eligible local variants;
- overconservatism, route failure, fallback/unsafe failure and baseline sufficiency.

Every metric requires an approved `MetricDictionaryEntry` or explicit requires-confirmation/diagnostic status.

## 7. Outcome and negative-result discipline

The Protocol successor must preserve at least these outcomes: beneficial; harmful/degraded; practically equivalent only through an affirmative predeclared procedure; inconclusive/underpowered; invalid/ineligible/unmatched; diagnostic-only. Nonsignificance is not equivalence. Simpler-control parity/superiority, coverage collapse, request/fallback burden, route failure and unavailable capabilities require `NegativeResultNote`/claim narrowing where applicable.

## 8. Denominator, attrition and missing-cell discipline

No row is silently dropped. Reports disclose initial eligible support, exclusions, denominator, independent unit, branch capability, missing cells, attrition reason and whether the absence reflects unsupported capability, missing data, validation failure or behavior not activated.

## 9. Downstream boundaries

- A6 learned quality remains producer/target-separated from rule-derived A5 quality.
- A7 uses causal Layer 5 context in a versioned rerun; core A5 remains regime-unaware.
- A12 and A13 retain clean/stressed and source-action/consumer-action separation.
- simulation, stress and embodiment outputs remain proxy/simulation-only and cannot backfill clean A5 evidence.

## 10. No-change lock

A0–A13, eleven local labels, comparator ownership and Phase 4/6/5/7–10/0 boundaries remain unchanged. Numeric execution details remain Protocol v1.0-owned.

## 3. Confirmatory and diagnostic run classes

- **Confirmatory primary:** `PRIMARY-FROZEN-A7`, immutable A5 versus separately versioned A7, exact common support and frozen method/config identity.
- **Delayed-update research:** separately tagged; cannot support the primary confirmatory claim.
- **Oracle headroom:** separately tagged evaluation-only upper-bound analysis.
- **Stress/update simulation and embodiment context:** A12/A13 diagnostics under their original ownership and proxy boundaries.

## 4. Local A7 dependency and gatekeeping rule

The full accepted portfolio and strong-simple comparator are evaluated first. Component-removal variants follow the directed dependency graph and may not create scientifically incoherent combinations. Confirmatory local families use Holm or the Protocol v1.0 declared stronger dependence-aware control; explicitly exploratory interactions may use BH-FDR. No local variant becomes a new global ablation.

## 5. Exact matching and support

Primary inference is fail-closed on exact A5/A7/control common support. Matching includes dataset, subject, session, trial/window/ordered sequence, target epoch, split, model/decoder, calibration and threshold identity, action/evidence budget/cost, seed/root config, event and availability cutoff, horizon count/duration/support, cadence/reset and metric identity. Attrition/support flow and unmatched rows are reported; unmatched rows are diagnostic only.

## 6. Metrics and negative-result zones

The metric hierarchy contains outcome/risk utility; finite-horizon event detection (false-alarm probability, high-probability latency, miss rate and event precision/recall); and intervention/recovery/interpretability burden. Trust and stop-loss burden are explicit. SESOI/equivalence and supported-benefit, practical-equivalence, inconclusive, overconservative, harmful and invalid zones are preregistered. Nonsignificance is not equivalence.

## 7. Negative controls and invariants

Required controls include A5, confidence-only, uncertainty-only, disabled/static, burden-matched random, contiguous-block permutation, circular shift, lead/lag placebo, conditional trust-target permutation, strong-simple and coherent component-removal variants. Every transformation records seed/block/shift/burden-match parameters and preserves source labels, matching identities and declared invariants.

## 8. Artifact obligations

A claim-ready A7 evidence package requires the accepted `RegimeStateRecord` projection, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, timelines, trust and warning exports, Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, negative-control report, metric references, `NegativeResultNote`, narrow `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, RegimeCard source-lineage bundle and reproducibility/handoff manifest.

## 9. Protocol v1.0 deferred numerical/statistical freeze

- [ ] exact equations and normalizers
- [ ] short/medium/long count and duration values
- [ ] minimum effective-support thresholds
- [ ] ADWIN/PH/KSWIN/WATCH/e-process hyperparameters and confirmation rule
- [ ] FSM thresholds, persistence, hysteresis and critical-bypass constants
- [ ] HSMM state count, sojourn family, priors and fitting details
- [ ] trust update rates, asymmetry gate, trusted-set cutoffs, cooldown and re-entry constants
- [ ] failure-event horizon, censoring cutoff and branch selection
- [ ] SESOI/equivalence margin, alpha, multiplicity and resampling counts
- [ ] dataset/model/seed/run matrix and power/precision stopping rule
- [ ] final MetricDictionary formulas, units, direction and denominator
- [ ] final file/schema serialization and dashboard routes

## 10. No-change and claim lock

A5 remains `regime_aware=false`; A7 is separately versioned; Layer 5 remains non-executive; no A14 is introduced; no clinical fatigue, patient-safety, medical-device or deployment claim is authorized; test outcomes cannot be used to reselect methods or thresholds after evaluation.

## 4. Frozen A7 identity

A7 remains the separately versioned causal rerun of Layer 4 with the accepted integrated Layer 5 context. A5 remains immutable and `regime_aware=false`. A7 does not authorize Layer 5 to own actions or Layer 6 adaptation.

The frozen method identity includes:

- legal field-visible causal intake;
- support-aware temporal feature construction;
- robust volatility and drawdown;
- uncertainty-distribution drift hierarchy with strong-simple controls;
- dropout, fatigue-like diagnostic and failure-risk branches;
- grouped monotone RegimeRisk and hysteretic FSM authority;
- conditional duration-aware adjunct;
- target-specific trust and support-aware trusted sets;
- stop-loss/cooldown/recovery/re-entry recommendations;
- full provenance, negative-result and claim-safety behavior.

## 5. Confirmatory, local-variant and diagnostic run classes

| Class | Role | Claim status |
|---|---|---|
| Frozen A5 | Immutable matched baseline | Confirmatory comparator |
| Frozen integrated A7 | Accepted M7 portfolio | Confirmatory treatment |
| Strong-simple A7 control | Minimal transparent component hierarchy | Gatekeeping/comparator |
| Component-removal variants | Remove one dependency-valid component or group at a time | Local explanatory evidence |
| Static/disabled variants | Remove temporal adaptation/state behavior while preserving support | Local explanatory evidence |
| Burden-matched random control | Match intervention burden without information | Negative control |
| Block permutation/circular shift/lead-lag | Destroy or misalign temporal information while preserving structure where possible | Negative control |
| Conditional trust-target variants | Compare eligible target-specific trust definitions | Local/diagnostic unless preregistered confirmatory |
| Oracle/headroom | Evaluation-only upper bound | Diagnostic only |
| Stress/embodiment contexts | A12/A13 downstream contexts | Separate context; not clean A7 replacement |
| Delayed-update research | Offline/delayed-label analysis | Diagnostic/research only |

No A14 is created. Local A7 variants remain under A7 and are not new global ablations.

## 6. Matching, estimands and support

- Primary comparison uses exact common support between frozen A5 and separately versioned A7.
- Matching preserves dataset, participant, session, split, model/configuration, seed where relevant, window/sequence identity, chronology/horizon/support profile and evidence mode.
- Participant/session clustering and paired structure are preserved.
- Attrition, unsupported rows, blocked branches and effective denominator flow are reported.
- Unmatched rows may support diagnostics but not the primary matched estimand.

## 7. Metrics and burden

Protocol v1.0 must define formulas, direction, denominator, independent unit, aggregation, intervals, multiplicity family and SESOI/equivalence zone for applicable families:

- task/performance and wrong-accept outcomes;
- selective prediction and coverage where relevant;
- risk-error alignment and calibration;
- regime/change detection, delay and persistence;
- trust discrimination, over-trust and under-trust;
- intervention, warning, stop-loss and recovery burden;
- oscillation, dwell, transition and re-entry behavior;
- interpretability/provenance completeness;
- negative-control invariants.

## 8. Negative-result and claim rule

Results are classified as supported benefit, practical equivalence, inconclusive, overconservative, harm, invalid or diagnostic-only. Nonsignificance is not equivalence. Null/adverse/invalid results require `NegativeResultNote` and claim-impact propagation.

## 10. Deferred numerical/statistical freeze

R27 does not set final alpha, SESOI, equivalence margins, bootstrap/permutation counts, horizon values, thresholds, seeds, run counts, stopping rules or exact formulas. Those must be frozen in Protocol v1.0 after Registry and Layer 5 Nuts-and-Bolts synchronization.

## 11. Future-layer interaction rule

A8–A13 may consume Layer 5 context only through accepted interfaces and must keep their own policy/simulation/stress/embodiment estimands separate. A future-layer method selection cannot retrospectively redefine A7, A5, Layer 5 thresholds or Layer 5 output semantics without a controlled reopen and synchronized successor set.

# R34 Layer 5 R7 Post-Finalization Experiment, Ablation, Evaluation, and Bidirectional Synchronization Addendum

**Synchronization date:** 25 July 2026  
**Compatibility set:** `L5-R7-POST-FINALIZATION-UPSTREAM-BIDIRECTIONAL-SYNC-R1-20260725`  
**Finalized Layer 5 source:** `IHARQ_Layer5_Detailed_Design_Nuts_and_Bolts_FULLY_MERGED_HARMONIZED_R7_FINAL_FINISHING_PASS_AUTHORITY_CERTIFIED_MARKDOWN_ONLY.md`  
**Finalized Layer 5 SHA-256:** `f1a82a1eb2e3f81525c373dda0568da036818b8d87c20e562065a1414740da72`  
**Accepted technical-method change:** `NONE`  
**Architecture topology/module change:** `NONE`  
**New canonical record family:** `NONE`  
**Global ablation change:** `NONE`; A0–A13 remain the complete global set and no A14 is created.  
**Purpose:** propagate only authority-appropriate Layer 5 R7 realization details upstream and make the reverse correction/invalidation path explicit without deleting or silently rewriting predecessor content.

## 1. Purpose and fixed protocol boundaries

The authority order remains Architecture → Canonical Registry → Execution and Evidence Plan → Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol → Phase Execution Playbook → accepted Method Selection → Nuts-and-Bolts → Implementation Build Book → execution evidence. The Layer 5 R7 document is a detailed-design realization and cannot unilaterally change a superior authority. This successor therefore distinguishes: (a) clarification already supported by the authority stack, (b) authority-specific synchronization text, (c) Registry/Protocol/Build Book/project-instance/consumer/empirical/claim matters that remain owner-gated, and (d) controlled reverse-impact packets for any future proven contradiction.

This R34 Protocol successor does not create a new global ablation or alter A0–A13. It records the finalized Layer 5 realization of A7 and its local variants/controls while preserving Protocol ownership of numerical and statistical commitments.

## 2. A5/A6/A7 identity and causal contract

- A5 is the immutable, deterministic, regime-unaware Layer 4 baseline and cannot be overwritten.
- A6 remains a separately versioned Layer 6-owned result and cannot absorb Layer 5 ownership.
- A7 is a separately versioned Layer 4 rerun using only causally prior, source-complete, valid Layer 5 context. Same-event, future, descendant, reset-incompatible, incomplete-lineage, or hidden repaired context is ineligible.
- Local removals/substitutions remain local A7 variants and do not create A14.
- Component-attribution interpretation is lawful only when the component was available, valid, executed, and able to influence the matched decision path; otherwise the variant is `inapplicable`, not evidence of no effect.

## 3. Matching, denominators, controls, and negative evidence

A5/A7 comparisons require exact common support, registered matching identity, one-to-one or explicitly governed pairing, denominator and attrition conservation, source/configuration closure, and complete exclusion reasons. Required controls include accepted strong-simple/static-disabled, burden-matched random, block permutation, circular shift, lead/lag placebo, and conditional trust-target controls where applicable. Invalid control invariants invalidate the control; they do not become null evidence.

`MatchedComparisonReport` is the canonical report family; A7 is carried as comparison/configuration identity. `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` and all outcome labels remain evaluation-only. Nonsignificance is not equivalence. Equivalence requires a preregistered SESOI and interval/TOST rule wholly inside the equivalence region. Negative/adverse/inconclusive/invalid/overconservative/baseline-sufficient results require first-class `NegativeResultNote` or equivalent governed representation and cannot be omitted.

## 4. Protocol v1.0 freeze package

Before outcome access, the Protocol owner must freeze: endpoint hierarchy and orientation; matching keys and null policy; independent unit and clustering; interval/resampling method; SESOI, equivalence, no-harm and burden margins; multiplicity graph and opening rules; control block sizes/offsets/placebos; cost dictionary; result-zone precedence; A7 root/local run matrix; diagnostic contexts; ties, censoring, undefined metrics and minimum support. R7 supplies semantic slots and validation rules, not these final values.

## 5. Layer 5 output and interface bindings

The Protocol consumes only validated, immutable exports through the `Layer 4/5 Evaluation Export Interface`. It must not train/adapt from evaluation exports, recompute hidden metrics, or promote unmatched/invalid evidence. Repository promotion is separately validated through the `Repository Promotion Interface`.

## 6. Reverse-impact protocol

A future Layer 5 finding may not silently repair or reinterpret an upstream authority or Layers 1–4 source. It must emit a versioned reverse-impact packet containing the affected proposition, exact evidence, impacted records/interfaces/steps/gates/ablations/consumers, migration and compatibility consequences, earliest invalidated dependency, proposed owner action, and closure test. Accepted corrections create immutable successors and trigger dependency-based invalidation/regeneration from the earliest changed authority input. Rejection preserves the current authority and leaves the affected Layer 5 branch blocked, downgraded, inapplicable, or diagnostic-only as appropriate.

## 7. Qualification

R7 documentary/mechanical verification is not empirical confirmation of A7 benefit, equivalence, no-harm, burden reduction, recovery, deployment, clinical validity, or patient safety.

## 1. R35 purpose and no-protocol-invention boundary

The governing order remains Architecture -> Canonical Registry -> Execution and Evidence Plan -> Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol -> Phase Execution Playbook -> accepted Method Selection -> Nuts-and-Bolts -> Implementation Build Book -> execution evidence. Detailed design may reveal representational or feasibility evidence, but it cannot silently override a superior authority. ## 4. Negative, adverse and invalid evidence

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. Unsupported, null, adverse, overconservative, invalid, baseline-sufficient and inconclusive results remain separate, source-linked and visible. Any metric without its exact denominator/support/undefined rule is blocked. Any post-outcome change to matching, metric, threshold, control, multiplicity or exclusion creates a new Protocol version and invalidates dependent comparisons.

## 5. Bidirectional Protocol impact

Layer 5 may submit a protocol-impact packet with candidate values, bounded tests and feasibility evidence, but only the Protocol owner may accept a freeze. An accepted Protocol successor rebinds Layer 5 R8 via a new compatibility set and regenerates affected A7 variants, controls, reports, negative-result notes and claim-evidence rows. Historical results remain under their original Protocol version.

## 6. R35 qualification

- Detailed design may define algorithms, legal configuration slots, validation predicates, and candidate operating ranges; it may not retrospectively freeze thresholds, horizons, tolerances, statistical units, SESOI/equivalence/no-harm margins, multiplicity, or confirmatory endpoints.

# Part II — Proposed A12.5/A13 synchronization addendum

# Experiment Protocol R41 PROPOSED — A12.5/A13 Layer 8/9 Post-Finalization Synchronization Addendum, Proposal Revision R3

**Current controlling Protocol:** R40 (`a6f4c527164295bd38901f40f6f42965060cc10443be4b598fc5d03644be34c6`)  
**Proposed successor:** R41  
**Status:** `[PROPOSED] [PROTOCOL OWNER ACCEPTANCE REQUIRED] [R40 REMAINS CONTROLLING] [NO NUMERICAL VALUES INVENTED] [NO A14]`

## 1. Scope and ownership

A12/A12.5 stress-side design, matching inputs and stress evidence remain Layer 8-owned. A13 embodiment-proxy evaluation remains Layer 9-owned. This addendum defines only the lawful bridge, applicability, matching, status, denominator and interpretation rules.

## 2. Mode applicability and evidence ceiling

| Mode | Eligibility | Required evidence | Permitted A13 use | Invalid/absent disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0 | always lawful as explicit no-embodiment closure | mode/absence reason and source status | status and burden/absence only | metrics requiring commands/states are undefined, not zero |
| E1 | validated static fixture and lawful intake/gate/map | deterministic timeline, no-step/blocked states, manifest | interface/chronology/burden evidence | no physics/endpoint/reward claim |
| E2 | accepted MyoSuite task/action profile and tested compatible lock | state/outcome/safety, seeds, task/config/map/gate/adapter IDs | simulation-only embodiment proxy | MYOSUITE_NOT_FEASIBLE or SIMULATOR_INVALID retained |
| E3 | valid E2 plus validated Layer 8 R13 project-instance package | E2 products plus profile/schedule/run/match/transform and paired clean/stress evidence | conditional stress-derived simulation evidence and A12.5 bridge | LAYER8_INPUT_PENDING, mismatch or invalid payload prevents E3 step/cell |
| E4 | accepted optional role and compatible runtime/assets/units/timebase/state/control/estimand | replay/visualization evidence; equivalence receipt for quantitative use | qualitative/diagnostic by default | OPENSIM_NOT_JUSTIFIED/UNAVAILABLE lawful |
| E5 | compatible lawful lower-mode cells | matching, applicability, denominators, status and limitation manifest | A13 comparative report | no forced cells; absent/invalid/unmatched cells explicit |

## 3. Required matching identity

For each lawful comparison cell, use the applicable subset of: dataset/split/window/subject lineage; policy/frozen-update identity; readiness-context identity; proxy-intent/action/command identity; mode; session/run; configuration; mapping; gate; adapter; platform; task; environment; seed; Layer 8 stress profile/schedule/run/matching/transform; metric version; availability time; and source hashes. A missing key makes the cell unmatched unless the Protocol owner explicitly defines a lawful coarser estimand.

## 4. Applicability, denominators and attrition

1. Determine branch eligibility before computing a metric.
2. Distinguish not-applicable, explicitly absent, blocked, invalid, unmatched, diagnostic and valid.
3. Never encode undefined or missing metrics as zero.
4. Report branch attrition and reasons from the initial eligible population through final matched cells.
5. Preserve statistical unit and denominator per estimand; do not pool incompatible modes/platforms/tasks.
6. Simulator-invalid rows remain in failure/attrition products and are not silently treated as policy failure.

## 5. A12.5/A13 reciprocity

Layer 8 supplies validated profile/schedule/run/matching/transform identities and clean/stress evidence. Layer 9 supplies validated final-payload gate state, embodiment state/outcome/safety products, A13 applicability and comparison results. A correction or invalidation on either side invalidates dependent cells until matched regeneration succeeds.

## 6. Metrics and MetricDictionary gate

Only existing Protocol-authorized metric families may be used. Task-specific endpoint/command-success, burden, safety-proxy, optional reward and stress-sensitivity metrics require MetricDictionary entries, units, direction, applicability and denominator definitions before thesis-facing use. Numerical tolerances, seed/run counts, confidence levels, multiplicity, equivalence margins and simulator-validity thresholds remain `[PROTOCOL-v1.0 SYNC REQUIRED]`.

## 7. Negative controls and result-status vocabulary

Required statuses include lawful variants of `MYOSUITE_NOT_FEASIBLE`, `OPENSIM_NOT_JUSTIFIED`, `LAYER8_INPUT_PENDING`, `SIMULATOR_INVALID`, `NO_REWARD_FEEDBACK`, `BASELINE_OR_FALLBACK_SUFFICIENT`, explicit absence, negative result and diagnostic-only. Exact token adoption is Registry/Protocol-owner controlled; this addendum does not create a new canonical vocabulary by itself.

## 8. Platform treatment

MyoSuite 2.12.2 declares Python `>=3.10,<3.14`, `gymnasium<1.3`, and `mujoco>=3.6,<3.7`. Current upstream MuJoCo 3.11.0 and Gymnasium 1.3.0 are not a compatible tuple by assumption. OpenSim 4.6 is an official released core/API line with official Python distributions, but E4 remains optional and quantitative comparison remains equivalence-gated.

## 9. Adoption and rollback

R40 remains controlling. R41 becomes current only after Protocol-owner acceptance, Registry compatibility check, reverse synchronization receipt and Build Book implementation profile. Rollback restores R40 without changing Layer 8 R13 or Layer 9 R20 decisions/designs; affected confirmatory cells remain pending/diagnostic.

## Acceptance, compatibility and rollback

The owner must accept, reject or revise each clause individually or as an explicitly enumerated package. Partial acceptance activates only the named clauses. Every acceptance record must identify the effective version, scope, compatibility set, migration, rollback, dependent Layer 10 sections and consumer acknowledgments. Rejection leaves the controlling predecessor in force and the affected Layer 10 product blocked or downgraded.
